$$\theta\ \text{is a function of the abstract pair data};\qquad \delta^2\ \text{is not, depending on the embedding.}$$
**Consequently the enumeration cannot be run on Cartan's list alone; it must carry the conjugacy class of $\mathfrak k$ in $\mathfrak{so}(n)$, not just the isomorphism type.** This also bounds what Step 5's zero-defect proof establishes: $\mathrm{Alt}(\Pi_{\mathfrak m})=0$ because $\mathfrak m$ has a decomposable orthonormal basis, which is true of the *block* embedding and hence of every sphere product, balanced or not, but it says nothing about a possible alternative embedding of the same abstract pair, which $\mathbb{HP}^2$ shows can be defective.

**Step 7, the alternative embedding exists in exactly one dimension, and it is not one that matters.** The $\mathbb{HP}^2$/$S^3\times S^5$ coincidence was first verified rather than assumed: run through a single code path, the two have $\theta=1.115546702045$ to twelve digits and $\delta^2=0$ versus $0.031746031746=2/63$; they are genuinely distinct operators ($\|W_1-W_2\|_F=1.183$, $\langle W_1,W_2\rangle=0.300$) with sorted spectra agreeing to $3.3\times10^{-16}$; and since both defects are unchanged under a random $SO(8)$ rotation, they are provably **not** $O(8)$-conjugate. So this is a real isospectral pair, not a frame artifact.

The mechanism is a spin representation: $\mathbb R^8=\mathrm{spin}_3\otimes\mathrm{spin}_5=2\otimes4$, which is how $\mathfrak{sp}(1)\oplus\mathfrak{sp}(2)$ on $\mathbb H^2$ realizes the same abstract isotropy as the block $\mathfrak{so}(3)\oplus\mathfrak{so}(5)$. Enumerating that possibility is a finite computation, because spin dimensions grow exponentially ($2^{\lfloor k/2\rfloor}$) while $N$ grows linearly. **Solving $\dim(\mathrm{spin}_j)\cdot\dim(\mathrm{spin}_{N-j})=N$ over all $N<200$, restricted to $j,N-j\ge3$ where the spin representations are the relevant ones, returns exactly one dimension: $N=8$** *(correction from Reviewer 11: without that restriction the full solution set is $(4,2),(8,1),(8,3),(8,5),(8,7)$, so the restriction must be stated rather than assumed)*, at $j=3$ and its mirror $j=5$. From $N=12$ on, the smallest available spin-tensor dimension already exceeds $N$ ($16>12$), and the gap explodes, $262144$ against $40$ at $N=40$. So no pair above $\sqrt{3/2}$ can admit a spin-type alternative embedding, for the elementary reason that no such embedding exists at any dimension past $8$. **Scope, stated plainly:** this enumerates the spin$\,\otimes\,$spin family, which is the one $\mathbb{HP}^2$ realizes; alternative embeddings built from other representation types are not covered, though the same growth argument applies to every non-vector irrep, all of which grow at least quadratically in the rank.

**Step 8, the unitary pairs, and family A closed.** Symmetric subalgebras of $\mathfrak{so}(N)$ are classified up to conjugacy: the blocks $\mathfrak{so}(j)\oplus\mathfrak{so}(N-j)$ and $\mathfrak u(N/2)$. The blocks are the sphere products, swept in Steps 5–6 and provably defect-free. The unitary class had never been given a value, the two-eigenvalue screen rejected it because $\mathfrak u(m)=\mathfrak{su}(m)\oplus\mathbb R$ is not simple, yet it is precisely where a defect is expected, since $\mathfrak u(m)$ carries the invariant $4$-form $\omega\wedge\omega$. Built directly ([scripts/review_r11_unitary_pairs.py](scripts/reviewers/r11/review_r11_unitary_pairs.py)) as $W=a_1\Pi_{\mathfrak{su}(m)}+a_2\Pi_{\mathbb R J}-b\,\Pi_{\mathfrak m}$ with $\mathfrak u(m)=\{A:[A,J]=0\}$:

| $n=2m$ | $\theta$ | $\delta^2$ | criticality residual | $\max\lvert\mathrm{Ric}\rvert$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 6 | $1.054092553$ | $0.088888889=4/45$ | $5.7\times10^{-16}$ | $1.9\times10^{-16}$ |
| 8 | $0.986013297$ | $0.079365079=5/63$ | $1.4\times10^{-12}$ | $1.8\times10^{-12}$ |
| 10 | $0.948683298$ | $0.074074074=2/27$ | $1.1\times10^{-12}$ | $6.4\times10^{-13}$ |
| 12 | $0.924962462$ | $0.070707071=7/99$ | $4.6\times10^{-13}$ | $3.2\times10^{-13}$ |

Every member is defective and every one sits **below** $\sqrt{3/2}$, decreasing in $m$. The $n=6$ row is an independent validation rather than a new claim: $(\mathfrak{so}(6),\mathfrak u(3))$ is $\mathbb{CP}^3$, and $\theta=\theta_0(6)$ with $\delta^2=4/45$ reproduces exactly the values already recorded for it in the $\mathcal A_n$ section. *A trap worth recording: the first run of this script omitted trace-freeness and returned $\theta$ up to $\sqrt2$ with $\max\lvert\mathrm{Ric}\rvert\approx1.4$, solutions that are critical for $Q$ but not Weyl operators at all. Irreducibility of $\mathfrak h$ makes $\mathrm{Ric}(W)$ a multiple of the identity, so trace-freeness is exactly what enforces Ricci-flatness, and it has to be imposed rather than hoped for.*

**Consequence, the graded half is settled for $\mathfrak h=\mathfrak{so}(N)$ acting standardly on $\mathbb R^N$.** Every symmetric subalgebra is now accounted for: the block ones give the sphere products, which exceed $\sqrt{3/2}$ but have $\delta^2=0$ for all $N$ and every split; the unitary one gives $SO(2m)/U(m)$, which is defective but stays below $\sqrt{3/2}$. **So no defective graded critical point in this family exceeds $\sqrt{3/2}$.** The one loophole, non-conjugate embeddings of the same abstract pair, is closed by the classification itself: two symmetric subalgebras of the same type are conjugate unless an outer automorphism separates them, which for $\mathfrak{so}(N)$ happens only at $N=8$, triality, exactly where $\mathbb{HP}^2$ appears, and harmlessly, since $1.1155<\sqrt{3/2}$. This is a cleaner statement of Step 7's conclusion, resting on the classification rather than on a dimension count.

**Step 9, the complex Grassmannians, and an open identification closed.** Family B's non-simple isotropy class, $(\mathfrak{su}(m),\mathfrak s(\mathfrak u(j)\oplus\mathfrak u(m-j)))$, built the same way as the unitary class ([scripts/review_r11_grassmann_pairs.py](scripts/reviewers/r11/review_r11_grassmann_pairs.py)) with $W=a_1\Pi_{\mathfrak{su}(j)}+a_2\Pi_{\mathfrak{su}(m-j)}+a_3\Pi_{\text{centre}}-b\,\Pi_{\mathfrak m}$:

| $n=2m$ | $j$ | $\theta$ | $\delta^2$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4 | 1 | $\sqrt{3/2}=1.224744871$ | $1/9$, **the Fox gate** |
| 6 | 1 | $\sqrt{6/5}=1.095445115$ | $1/10$ |
| 8 | 1 | $1.054092553$ | $4/45$ |
| 8 | 2 | $0.968245837$ | $1/10$ |
| 10 | 1 | $1.035098339$ | $5/63$ |
| 10 | 2 | $0.925820100$ | $2/21$ |
| 12 | 1 | $1.024695077$ | $1/14$ |
| 12 | 2 | $0.905711047$ | $5/56$ |
| 12 | 3 | $0.881917104$ | $2/21$ |

Every member is defective, as expected for a Kähler class, and **every one except the Fox gate row sits below $\sqrt{3/2}$**, decreasing in both $m$ and $j$.

**Adversarial review, per the standing rule.** *(a) Gate:* the $m=2,j=1$ row reproduces Fox exactly ($\theta=\sqrt{3/2}$, $\delta^2=1/9$, residual $3.9\times10^{-16}$). *(b) Cross-check:* the $m=3,j=1$ row is $\theta=\sqrt{6/5}$ with $\delta^2=1/10$, **exactly the "uncatalogued" three-eigenvalue critical point that the frontier battery found by unconstrained gradient ascent** in the full $300$-dimensional Weyl space. Two structurally unrelated methods land on the same point, so **that open identification is now closed: it is $\mathbb{CP}^2=SU(3)/S(U(1)\times U(2))$**, and it is distinct from the $(\mathfrak{su}(3),\mathfrak{so}(3))$ member which shares its $\theta$ but has $\delta^2=5/48$, two different pairs at one critical value, exactly the degeneracy the $(p,q,c_{\mathfrak k})$ formula predicts. *(c) Validity screen:* Ricci-flatness $\le1.6\times10^{-11}$ and criticality residual $\le6\times10^{-11}$ on every row. *(d) Ceiling:* every $\theta\le\sqrt2$. Every $\delta^2$ is a small-denominator rational to $\le4\times10^{-10}$, consistent with a structured origin.

***A false negative caught by the rule, worth recording.*** The first run of this script reported "no Ricci-flat critical point exists" for every $m\ge3$ while the Fox row survived, an implausible pattern that turned out to be a crude Cartan split: consecutive diagonal differences assigned by index do not decompose $\mathfrak s(\mathfrak u(j)\oplus\mathfrak u(m-j))$ into its ideals. Splitting the diagonal correctly, traceless within each block plus the single central direction $\mathrm{diag}((m-j)I_j,-jI_{m-j})$, reversed the result completely, from "no solutions anywhere" to "a solution in every case." Had the gate row not been there, the false negative would have read as a clean structural finding.

**Step 10, the classical enumeration, consolidated.** With (R1) tested against true Casimirs throughout, and the ideal-wise system solved where $\mathfrak k$ is non-simple, the classical picture is:

| symmetric pair | verdict | above $\sqrt{3/2}$? | defect |
|---|---|---|---|
| $(\mathfrak{so}(2m),\mathfrak{so}(m)\oplus\mathfrak{so}(m))$, balanced spheres | genuine | **yes**, $m\ge6$ | $0$, proven all $m$ |
| $(\mathfrak{so}(N),\mathfrak{so}(j)\oplus\mathfrak{so}(N-j))$, $j\ne N-j$, unbalanced spheres | genuine (181 of 342) | **yes**, 108 of them | $0$, proven |
| $(\mathfrak{so}(N),\mathfrak{so}(N-1))$ | no such $W$: $2q\le p$ for $N>6$ | nothing recorded | nothing recorded |
| $(\mathfrak{so}(2m),\mathfrak u(m))=SO(2m)/U(m)$ | genuine | no | $4/45,5/63,2/27,7/99$ |
| $(\mathfrak{su}(m),\mathfrak{so}(m))$. Ricci-flat Kähler | genuine | only Fox, at equality | $1/9$ at $m=2$, falling |
| $(\mathfrak{su}(m),\mathfrak s(\mathfrak u(j)\oplus\mathfrak u(m-j)))$, complex Grassmannians | genuine | only the Fox row | $1/10,4/45,5/63,\dots$ |
| $(\mathfrak{sp}(2j),\mathfrak{sp}(j)\oplus\mathfrak{sp}(j))$ | **inconsistent**, no isotropy-scalar graded critical point | nothing recorded | nothing recorded |
| $(\mathfrak{su}(2k),\mathfrak{sp}(k))$ | **inconsistent** for every $k\ge2$ | nothing recorded | nothing recorded |

Both rejections mean *no **isotropy-scalar** graded critical point*, the phrasing Reviewer 11 asked for, since the ideal-wise case is a separate question. (R1) is applied throughout in the $\mathfrak{so}(n)$-induced normalisation, where coordinate $2$-planes are orthonormal. The last row is new and was settled in exact rational arithmetic: for $(\mathfrak{su}(2k),\mathfrak{sp}(k))$ one has $p=k(2k+1)$, $q=(2k+1)(k-1)$, $C=C_2(\omega_2)=2k$ and $c_{\mathfrak k}=2(k+1)$, whence (R1) returns $(2k^2-8k+2)/(k-1)$, which equals $2k+2$ only at $k=\tfrac12$, so the family carries no graded critical point at any integer $k\ge2$. Hand algebra and code agree exactly (both give $26/5$ at $k=6$).

**So across the classical families, every graded critical point above $\sqrt{3/2}$ is a sphere product, balanced or unbalanced, and all of those are provably defect-free.** The classical gap that remains is family C's non-simple classes, $(\mathfrak{sp}(m),\mathfrak u(m))$ and the unbalanced $(\mathfrak{sp}(m),\mathfrak{sp}(j)\oplus\mathfrak{sp}(m-j))$, which need the ideal-wise treatment the unitary and Grassmannian classes received; every $\mathfrak{sp}$-type value computed so far ($\mathbb{HP}^m$ at $1.1155,0.853,0.745$, decreasing) sits well below $\sqrt{3/2}$, but that is a pattern, not a check. Beyond the classical families, the exceptional $\mathfrak h$ remain untouched.

### The ungraded half, measured, and it is a loose problem rather than a sharp one

**Purpose.** With the graded half settled across the classical families, the remaining case is $S>0$, where $S$ is the slack of the graded compression inequality,
$$S(W):=\|\mathrm{Ric}(W_-)\|^2+6\delta^2-\theta\operatorname{tr}(W_-)-\operatorname{tr}(W_-^2)\;\ge\;0,$$
vanishing exactly on the graded class. Code: [scripts/review_r11_grading_slack.py](scripts/reviewers/r11/review_r11_grading_slack.py) (definition and validation) and [scripts/review_r11_ungraded_frontier.py](scripts/lib/review_r11_ungraded_frontier.py) (the population sweep). *Validation:* $S=0$ to $10^{-16}$ at all 22 graded catalogue points, and $S=0.673401$ at $\mathbb{HP}^3$, tracking its independently measured $[\mathfrak m,\mathfrak m]$-in-$\mathfrak m$ fraction of $0.421$.

**The measured ungraded population**, screened for Ricci-flatness and criticality:

| $S$ | $\theta$ | point |
|---|---|---|
| $0.391608$ | $0.702559$ | sphere $(2,2,8)$, $n=12$ |
| $0.400000$ | $0.645497$ | sphere $(2,2,2)$, $n=6$ |
| $0.467532$ | $0.690849$ | sphere $(2,2,4)$, $n=8$ |
| $0.571429$ | $0.540062$ | sphere $(2,2,2,2)$, $n=8$ |
| $0.571429$ | $0.720082$ | sphere $(3,3,2)$, $n=8$ |
| $0.571429$ | $0.836660$ | $SU(3)$ bi-invariant, $n=8$ |
| $0.649351$ | $0.572172$ | sphere $(2,2,2,6)$, $n=12$ |
| $0.673401$ | $0.852944$ | QK $\mathbb{HP}^3$, $n=12$ |
| $0.861244$ | $0.802044$ | sphere $(3,3,6)$, $n=12$ |
| $0.920000$ | $0.387298$ | the $\delta^2=3/25$ violator, $n=8$ |

**Two findings, and the first refutes the conjecture I had proposed.** The natural guess, $\theta\le\Theta(S)$ with $\Theta$ decreasing, mirroring the defect-penalty shape, **does not hold**: at $S=4/7$ the value ranges over $0.540,0.720,0.837$, and $S=0.861$ carries $\theta=0.802$ while the smaller $S=0.649$ carries only $0.572$. The relation is not monotone and no such $\Theta$ exists.

**What the data shows instead is a gap, wide, but not where I first put it.** The constructed population all sits at $\theta\le0.852944$, and I recorded that as the ceiling. **A stronger search then refuted it.** [scripts/review_r11_gap_attack2.py](scripts/lib/review_r11_gap_attack2.py) replaces the earlier stalling Powell run with an analytic-gradient L-BFGS minimisation of $\|Q(W)\|^2-\theta^2+\lambda(\theta-\theta_t)^2$ (using $\nabla\|Q\|^2=4B(W,Q(W))$, $\nabla\theta=3Q(W)$), and separates the branches the first version conflated. At $n=8$ it converges to **55 critical points, 17 graded and 38 ungraded**, and the ungraded maximum is $\theta=0.900828$ with $S=0.303691$, above the recorded ceiling and inside the band I had called empty. Verified before being believed: criticality residual $4.8\times10^{-8}$, $\max|\mathrm{Ric}|=2.3\times10^{-16}$, unit norm, and an **independent** grading check giving $[\mathfrak m,\mathfrak m]$-fraction $0.4419$, so it is genuinely ungraded rather than a numerical artifact (saved as `gap_band_point_n8.npy`).

So both figures move: the observed ungraded ceiling is $\ge0.900828$, not $0.852944$, and the smallest observed slack is $0.303691$, not $0.391608$. **The qualitative gap survives**, at $n=8$ the graded population reaches $1.145644$ while the ungraded stops at $0.900828$, against $\sqrt{3/2}=1.224745$, a margin of $0.32$. But the ceiling has now risen once under better search, so it should be read as "nothing found above" rather than a bound, and a further improvement in search may raise it again.

**Why this matters more than the numbers do.** It reframes the crux. The graded half was *tight*. Fox sits exactly at $\sqrt{3/2}$, so the enumeration had to be exact. The lifted-chain route was tighter still, needing a bound inside a window of width $0.011$ at $n=12$. **The ungraded half is loose by a factor of nearly thirty:** any argument showing $S>0\Rightarrow\theta\le c$ for any $c<1.2247$ suffices, and the evidence puts the true ceiling somewhere near $0.9$. So the remaining statement is
$$S(W)>0\ \Longrightarrow\ \theta(W)\le c\quad\text{for some } c<\sqrt{3/2},$$
which, with the graded enumeration, closes the core. *(Written when the assembled bound appeared to separate every point with wide margins. Reviewer 12 refuted that separation, so "a crude bound would do" no longer holds: the surviving candidate is the sharp (II)-side bound, whose margins are real but whose sharpness at Fox is exact.)*

**The two adversarial tests, and why only the second counts.** The first ([scripts/review_r11_gap_attack.py](scripts/reviewers/r11/review_r11_gap_attack.py)) pinned $\theta$ inside the band and rewarded slack, and reported nothing, but it was cut to 6 seeds and 60 Powell iterations over an 84-dimensional space after a full-strength run was killed for memory, and it could not distinguish "found only graded points" from "converged to nothing". Its apparent confirmation was worthless. The second (`gap_attack2`) fixes both defects and promptly **moved the ceiling**, which is what a real adversarial test looks like. Note also its $n=6$ result: only 5 critical points converge there and all are graded, consistent with the known dominance of Fox's basin at that dimension, so the $n=8$ population is where the evidence lives.

**Confidence.** High for the definition and its validation (exact zero on the graded class, matching the independent bracket measure off it). High for the refutation of the monotone form, it rests on three points at identical $S$ with $\theta$ spread over $0.3$. **The gap is empirical and its ceiling has already moved once**: from $0.853$ (10 constructed points) to $0.900828$ (55 converged points at $n=8$ under a properly converging search). The separation from $\sqrt{3/2}$ is robust across both rounds, the specific ceiling is not. **Unreviewed.**

### The ungraded population at $n=8$ and $n=12$, a harder search, and a classification trap

**Purpose.** P1 step (i): before spending proof effort on *"$S>0\Rightarrow\theta\le c<\sqrt{3/2}$"*, test it where it could break. Code: [scripts/gap_push_n8.py](scripts/misc/gap_push_n8.py), [scripts/gap_push_n12.py](scripts/misc/gap_push_n12.py), both using the analytic-gradient L-BFGS formulation (at $n=12$ on [scripts/run_unconstrained_search_n12.py](scripts/lib/run_unconstrained_search_n12.py)'s BLAS-fast $Q$).

**Result at $n=8$, 209 converged critical points, and the gap holds.** Pinning $\theta$ at nine targets from $0.88$ to $1.24$, 120 seeds each: **175 graded, 34 ungraded**. Every ungraded point found lies at $\theta\le0.879$ in this run (the separate $0.900828$ point from the earlier run stands, so the observed ceiling remains $\ge0.9008$). Above $\theta\approx0.9$ the search returns **only graded points**, 36 at target $1.10$, 7 at $1.15$, 12 at $1.20$, and all 120 at $1.24$. Targets $0.92,0.96,1.00,1.05$ converged to nothing in *that* run, which was read at the time as an empty stretch of the $\theta$-axis. **[reviews/INDEX.md](reviews/INDEX.md)'s Reviewer 11 refutes that reading**: a genuine graded point sits at $\theta=0.979796=2\sqrt6/5$ (residual $1.2\times10^{-15}$), with further graded points at $1.0647$–$1.0988$ beyond the named catalogue. The stretch is populated; the search simply failed to converge there. Minimum observed slack drops again, to $0.1867$, so "$S$ bounded away from zero" continues to weaken with each better search, while the $\theta$-separation does not.

**Result at $n=12$, the first such sweep ever run here.** 30 converged critical points across five targets: 23 graded (max $\theta=1.236033=\theta_0(12)$, exactly the conjectured maximizer) and 7 ungraded, of which 5 sit at $\theta\le0.8997$. At the time this was read as "no ungraded critical point above $0.9$ at $n=12$". **That is false**. Reviewer 11 padded the $n=8$ witness to $n=12$ and it is critical there at residual $10^{-15}$, so the $0.900828016$ ceiling holds at both dimensions.

***A classification trap, and the correction it forces.*** Two $n=12$ points were first flagged ungraded at $\theta=1.095445$, inside the band, which would have been a refutation. They are not. Their spectrum is $0.365149$, $\pm0.1826$, and then roughly thirty eigenvalues of magnitude $10^{-4}$ to $10^{-6}$: an **under-converged** copy of a known $\theta=\sqrt{6/5}$ point whose kernel has not yet collapsed. Because $E_\pm$ are defined by the *sign* of the eigenvalue, a kernel that is only numerically zero gets split arbitrarily between them, and the bracket test then reports a spurious grading defect ($[\mathfrak m,\mathfrak m]$ mass $0.107$, $[E_+,E_+]$ mass $0.149$, $[E_+,E_-]$ mass $0.128$, all three conditions "violated" at once, which is the signature). The (GC) slack, by contrast, reads $S=5.4\times10^{-6}$ and correctly calls it graded, because $W_-$ genuinely has no mass in those directions.

**Two consequences.** First, **$S$ is the more robust classifier and the bracket test is not**, the reverse of what one would guess, since the bracket test is the structural definition. Any grading claim must therefore be screened for a spectral gap at zero before it is believed; a point with eigenvalues at $10^{-4}$ has no well-defined $E_\pm$ splitting at all. Second, and this is where the diagnosis overreached, the $n=8$ witness at $\theta=0.900828$ was **wrongly condemned** by it and is in fact genuine (see the retraction above); its near-zero eigenvalues survive an LM polish to residual $10^{-15}$. It is **unaffected**: its spectrum runs $0.553,0.422,0.169,\dots,-0.232,-0.245,-0.261$, with no eigenvalue near zero, so its bracket fraction of $0.4419$ is measuring real structure. That point stands as the ungraded ceiling.

**Status of the target, after two independent audits.** The observed ungraded ceiling has moved a third time: Reviewer 12 found $\theta=0.906671671$ (residual $1.1\times10^{-15}$, two independent seeds, decomposition and screens holding at $10^{-15}$). Across all sweeps nothing ungraded appears above that, while the graded population reaches $\theta_0(n)$ at both dimensions. The separation from $\sqrt{3/2}=1.224745$ survives its hardest test so far, including the first probe at the threshold dimension itself. **Confidence:** high for the $n=8$ census and the artifact diagnosis (the spectrum is unambiguous); moderate for the $n=12$ picture, which rests on 14 seeds per target rather than 120, and where a genuine ungraded point in the band would be the single most valuable thing to look for next. **Unreviewed.**

### The slack has a closed Gram form, the crux route is open, and the ceiling it was measured against is contaminated

**Purpose.** P1 step (ii). The proof route for the crux assumes the (GC) slack $S$ equals the bracket mass the derivation discards. That is testable rather than hopeful. Code: [scripts/review_r11_slack_gram.py](scripts/reviewers/r11/review_r11_slack_gram.py).

**Result 1, the closed form, and it is exact.** With $Wv_i=-\mu_iv_i$ an orthonormal eigenbasis of $E_-$ ($\mu_i>0$), define
$$G_1:=\sum_{i,j}\mu_i\mu_j\,\bigl\|P_{E_-}[v_i,v_j]\bigr\|^2 .$$
Then at every genuinely critical point with a clean spectrum,
$$\boxed{\,S=\tfrac12\,G_1\,}$$
to displayed precision, ratio $0.5000$ at **nine of nine** such points: the multi-block sphere products $(2,2,2)$, $(2,2,4)$, $(3,3,2)$, $(2,2,2,2)$, $(2,2,8)$, $(3,3,6)$, $(2,2,2,6)$ across $n=6,8,12$, the $SU(3)$ bi-invariant, and quaternionic $\mathbb{HP}^3$.

**This is exactly the handle the route needed.** $G_1$ is manifestly nonnegative, so the identity re-proves $S\ge0$, i.e. (GC) itself, from bracket positivity alone, and it makes the slack an explicit, differentiable function of the eigen-structure rather than an opaque residual. The reverse-compression step now has something concrete to work with: *the slack is precisely the $E_-$-internal bracket mass, weighted by the negative spectrum.*

**Result 2, it is a consequence of criticality, not an identity.** Six random (non-critical) unit Weyl tensors at $n=8$ give $S\approx2.03$–$2.22$ against $G_1/2\approx0.24$–$0.32$, missing by $\approx1.8$ throughout. So the relation is not formal: it holds *because* $Q(W)=\theta W$, which is what makes it usable as a criticality-plus-cleanliness certificate.

***Result 3. RETRACTED. The certificate flagged the $\theta=0.900828$ witness, and the flag was wrong.*** This section originally read the witness's $S/G_1=1.278$ and its four eigenvalues at $-1.010\times10^{-3}$ as an uncollapsed kernel, and condemned the point. [reviews/INDEX.md](reviews/INDEX.md)'s Reviewer 11 shows otherwise: **the witness Levenberg–Marquardt-polishes from residual $4.2\times10^{-8}$ to $1.0\times10^{-15}$ with $\theta$ and the eigenvalue quadruple unchanged.** Those eigenvalues are real structure, not numerical residue. The point is a genuine, ungraded, $F_1$-violating critical point, it was **independently re-found from random seeds**, and padding makes it critical at $n=12$ as well (residual $10^{-15}$). Its $S/G_1$ ratio deviates because $S=\tfrac12G_1$ is conditional on F1/F2, which it violates, not because the point is defective.

**So the ceiling of $0.900828016$ stands, at both $n=8$ and $n=12$**, together with four further genuine ungraded points at $0.854425$–$0.899$. The screen this section proposed is withdrawn: a ratio test built on a conditional identity cannot certify convergence. **The correct screen is second-order, an LM polish of the residual vector, plus a spectral-gap-versus-residual comparison**, since first-order searches stall at $10^{-8}$–$10^{-9}$, which is ambiguous between a genuine critical point and a positive local minimum of the residual functional.

**Confidence.** High for the closed form (exact ratio $0.5000$ at nine structurally unrelated points across three dimensions, and it fails by a factor of $\sim7$ on random tensors, so it is not an artifact of normalization). High for the contamination diagnosis (the offending eigenvalues are visible and the ratio test flags exactly the two points already independently suspected). The identity is **not yet proven**, it is a numerically exact pattern awaiting derivation from the (GC) compression step, which is the immediate next task. **Unreviewed.**

### The slack identity, derived, and the grading conditions are not all-or-nothing

**Purpose.** P1 step (ii)(a): prove $S=\tfrac12G_1$ rather than observe it. The derivation reduces to two structural facts, and separating them out changes the picture of what "graded" means.

**The chain.** Write $W=W_+-W_-$ for the spectral parts ($W_\pm\succeq0$), $P_\pm$ the eigenprojections, $\delta^2=\|\mathrm{Alt}(W_-)\|^2$.

1. *Compress criticality onto $E_-$.* $W$ and $W^2$ preserve $E_-$, so $P_-(W^2+W^\#)P_-=\theta P_-WP_-$ gives $W_-^2+P_-W^\#P_-=-\theta W_-$, hence
   $$\theta\operatorname{tr}(W_-)+\operatorname{tr}(W_-^2)=-\operatorname{tr}(P_-W^\#P_-).$$
   This is (GC)'s left-hand side, exactly. *(Proven, algebra.)*
2. *Apply the $\operatorname{scal}$ identity to $W_-$.* $\operatorname{scal}(R^2+R^\#)=\|\mathrm{Ric}(R)\|^2+6\|\mathrm{Alt}(R)\|^2$ for every symmetric $R$, with $\operatorname{scal}=2\operatorname{tr}$, gives
   $$\|\mathrm{Ric}(W_-)\|^2+6\delta^2=2\operatorname{tr}(W_-^2)+2\operatorname{tr}(W_-^\#),$$
   which is (GC)'s right-hand side. *(Proven, the identity is already established in this file.)*
3. Subtracting, $S=2\operatorname{tr}(W_-^2)+2\operatorname{tr}(W_-^\#)+\operatorname{tr}(P_-W^\#P_-)$. *(Proven; verified to $10^{-16}$ at ten points.)*
4. Bilinearity of $\#$ gives $W^\#=W_+^\#-2\,W_+\#W_-+W_-^\#$. *(Proven.)*
5. **(F1)** $\operatorname{tr}(P_-W_+^\#P_-)=0$. *(Verified to exact floating-point zero at all ten points.)*
6. **(F2)** $\operatorname{tr}(W_-^2)+\operatorname{tr}(W_-^\#)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(P_-(W_+\#W_-)P_-\bigr)$. *(Verified to $\le3\times10^{-15}$ at all ten points.)*
7. Combining 3–6: $S=\operatorname{tr}(P_-W_-^\#P_-)$, and rank-one $\#$-positivity, $(uu^{\mathsf T})\#(vv^{\mathsf T})=\tfrac12[u,v][u,v]^{\mathsf T}$, expands this to $\tfrac12\sum_{i,j}\mu_i\mu_j\|P_{E_-}[v_i,v_j]\|^2=\tfrac12G_1$. $\square$ *(modulo F1, F2)*

**So the slack is the $E_-$-compression of $W_-^\#$**, and $S\ge0$, i.e. (GC) itself, follows from bracket positivity alone. That is a cleaner proof of (GC) than the original.

***The structural payoff: the grading conditions are not a package.*** (F1) says $\tfrac12\sum_{a,b}\nu_a\nu_b\|P_{E_-}[u_a,u_b]\|^2=0$ with every $\nu_a>0$, so $P_{E_-}[u_a,u_b]=0$ for all $a,b$, i.e.
$$[E_+,E_+]\perp E_-\quad\text{holds automatically at every critical point, graded or not.}$$
It is a *consequence of criticality*, not part of the grading hypothesis. What distinguishes graded from ungraded is only the other condition, $[E_-,E_-]\perp E_-$, and $S=\tfrac12G_1$ measures exactly its failure. This corrects the earlier framing, which treated the three bracket conditions as one indivisible property: two of them come free, and the whole content of "ungraded" sits in the third. It also explains why $S$ classifies robustly while the bracket test does not, $S$ is measuring the one condition that carries information, and it does so without needing a clean $E_\pm$ split of the kernel.

**F2 is now derived, and the whole thing collapses onto two grading conditions.** Two further steps, both proven from ingredients already established in this file and each verified to $10^{-15}$ at the same ten points:

- **(A)** $\operatorname{tr}(W_+^2)+\operatorname{tr}(W_+^\#)=\operatorname{tr}(W_-^2)+\operatorname{tr}(W_-^\#)$. *Proof:* apply the $\operatorname{scal}$ identity separately to $W_+$ and to $W_-$; the right-hand sides are $\|\mathrm{Ric}(W_\pm)\|^2+6\|\mathrm{Alt}(W_\pm)\|^2$, and these agree because $\mathrm{Ric}(W)=0$ forces $\mathrm{Ric}(W_+)=\mathrm{Ric}(W_-)$ while $\mathrm{Alt}(W_+)=\mathrm{Alt}(W_-)$ holds for every Bianchi $W$ (already proven here). $\square$
- **(B)** $\operatorname{tr}(W_-^2)+\operatorname{tr}(W_-^\#)=\operatorname{tr}(W_+\#W_-)$. *Proof:* a Weyl operator has $\operatorname{tr}W=\operatorname{scal}/2=0$, so the full trace of criticality reads $\operatorname{tr}(W^2)+\operatorname{tr}(W^\#)=\theta\operatorname{tr}(W)=0$; expanding $W^\#$ bilinearly gives $\operatorname{tr}(W_+^2)+\operatorname{tr}(W_-^2)+\operatorname{tr}(W_+^\#)+\operatorname{tr}(W_-^\#)=2\operatorname{tr}(W_+\#W_-)$, and (A) halves it. $\square$

With (B), F2 becomes $\operatorname{tr}(W_+\#W_-)=\operatorname{tr}(P_-(W_+\#W_-)P_-)$, i.e. $\operatorname{tr}\bigl((1-P_-)(W_+\#W_-)(1-P_-)\bigr)=0$, verified at $\le2.4\times10^{-16}$. Since $W_+\#W_-=\tfrac12\sum_{a,i}\nu_a\mu_i[u_a,v_i][u_a,v_i]^{\mathsf T}\succeq0$, a vanishing compression forces every term, so

$$\textbf{F2}\iff[E_+,E_-]\subseteq E_-,\qquad\textbf{F1}\iff[E_+,E_+]\perp E_-.$$

**So the identity reduces exactly to two of the three grading conditions**, but they are **hypotheses, not consequences of criticality**, and the earlier claim otherwise was wrong. The corrected statement: *at any critical point where $[E_+,E_+]\perp E_-$ and $[E_+,E_-]\subseteq E_-$, the slack is $S=\tfrac12\sum_{i,j}\mu_i\mu_j\|P_{E_-}[v_i,v_j]\|^2$.*

***Refuted by [reviews/INDEX.md](reviews/INDEX.md)'s Reviewer 11, and the counterexample was inside this file's own table.*** A 60-seed hunt at $n=6$ produced 22 genuine critical points (Levenberg–Marquardt-polished to residual $\sim3\times10^{-16}$, clean spectra) violating both conditions at order one, $F_1$ reaching $0.62$. So does the already-catalogued $\delta^2=3/25$ violator: residual $8\times10^{-16}$, $F_1=0.360$, $F_2$ residual $0.240$, and $S/G_1=11.5$ against the claimed $0.5$. **The "nine of nine" evidence was a biased sample**, the tenth row of the same table breaks the pattern, and the spectral screen then in use is exactly what hid it. Two further corrections from the same audit: at generic critical points $S$ carries $F_1/F_2$ mass as well (points exist with $[E_-,E_-]$-into-$E_-$ mass $0.024$ yet $S=1.73$ against $G_1/2=0.017$), so $S$ measures strictly *more* than the third condition off the structured class; and the equivalences F1 $\iff[E_+,E_+]\perp E_-$, F2 $\iff[E_+,E_-]\subseteq E_-$ are themselves **confirmed**.

**What survives, and it is the substantive half.** Chain steps 1–4 and 7 and the lemmas (A) and (B) are **confirmed as genuine, non-circular theorems**, they hold at $10^{-15}$ *including at points where F1/F2 fail*, which is what rules out circularity. The (GC) inequality $S\ge0$ is untouched. So the identity is a real theorem about the structured class, and the reverse-compression route can still be built on it there; what it is not is a universal description of the slack.

**This also corrects the framing of the equality case.** Track 2 recorded "(GC) equality $\iff$ all three bracket conditions", treating them as one package. Two of the three are automatic, so the honest statement is: equality holds iff the *third* condition does, and that is the only one carrying information, which is precisely why $S$ classifies robustly where the three-condition bracket test does not. **Confidence:** high for steps 1–4 and 7 (algebra plus an already-proven identity); high that F1 and F2 hold as stated (exact zeros and $10^{-15}$ residuals at ten structurally unrelated points across $n=6,8,12$); the reduction is honest, the identity is now one lemma away, not a numerical coincidence. **Unreviewed.**

### The slack decomposition, the conditional identity repaired into an unconditional theorem

**Purpose.** Reviewer 11 refuted $S=\tfrac12G_1$ as universal while confirming the supporting lemmas (A) and (B) as genuine, non-circular theorems. Those two are enough to repair it, and the repaired statement is stronger than the one it replaces. Code: [scripts/review_r11_slack_decomp.py](scripts/lib/review_r11_slack_decomp.py).

**The theorem.** Substituting $2\operatorname{tr}(W_-^2)+2\operatorname{tr}(W_-^\#)=2\operatorname{tr}(W_+\#W_-)$, which is (A) plus (B), into $S=2\operatorname{tr}(W_-^2)+2\operatorname{tr}(W_-^\#)+\operatorname{tr}(P_-W^\#P_-)$ and expanding $W^\#=W_+^\#-2W_+\#W_-+W_-^\#$ gives, at **every** critical point with no hypotheses whatever,
$$\boxed{\;S=T_1+2T_2+T_3\;}$$
$$T_1=\operatorname{tr}(P_-W_+^\#P_-)=\tfrac12\!\sum_{a,b}\nu_a\nu_b\|P_{E_-}[u_a,u_b]\|^2,\quad
T_2=\operatorname{tr}\bigl((1-P_-)(W_+\#W_-)(1-P_-)\bigr)=\tfrac12\!\sum_{a,i}\nu_a\mu_i\|(1-P_{E_-})[u_a,v_i]\|^2,$$
$$T_3=\operatorname{tr}(P_-W_-^\#P_-)=\tfrac12\!\sum_{i,j}\mu_i\mu_j\|P_{E_-}[v_i,v_j]\|^2=\tfrac12G_1 .$$
Each is a compression of a PSD operator, by the rank-one identity $(uu^{\mathsf T})\#(vv^{\mathsf T})=\tfrac12[u,v][u,v]^{\mathsf T}$, so **each term is nonnegative unconditionally**.

**Verified to machine precision at every point tested**, structured and generic alike: the multi-block sphere products, $\mathbb{HP}^2$, $\mathbb{HP}^3$, $SU(3)$ bi-invariant (all with $T_1=T_2=0$), the $\delta^2=3/25$ violator ($0.92=0.36+0.48+0.08$) and the $\theta=0.900828$ witness ($0.30369=0.12712+0.05779+0.11878$), the two points that broke the conditional identity, and five generic Levenberg–Marquardt critical points at $n=6$ where F1/F2 fail at order one ($T_1\approx0.6$, $2T_2\approx1.1$–$1.7$). Worst deviation $5.7\times10^{-9}$, at the one point whose own criticality residual is $4.7\times10^{-8}$; everywhere else $\le3\times10^{-15}$.

**What it buys.**
1. **$S\ge0$, the (GC) inequality, now follows unconditionally from bracket positivity alone**, a cleaner proof than the original and with no hypotheses.
2. **$S\ge\tfrac12G_1$ always**, with equality exactly when $T_1=T_2=0$, i.e. when $[E_+,E_+]\perp E_-$ and $[E_+,E_-]\subseteq E_-$. The refuted identity is recovered as precisely that special case, which is why it held at the structured competitors and failed generically.
3. **The interpretation is now exact:** *the slack is the total bracket mass violating the three grading conditions, weighted $1,2,1$.* Each $T_k$ is the violation of one condition, $T_1$ of $[E_+,E_+]\perp E_-$, $T_2$ of $[E_+,E_-]\subseteq E_-$, $T_3$ of $[E_-,E_-]\perp E_-$.
4. **This vindicates the original equality characterisation.** Since all three terms are nonnegative, $S=0\iff T_1=T_2=T_3=0\iff$ all three grading conditions hold. So (GC)-equality $\iff$ graded, exactly as first recorded, and **my "two of the three are automatic" correction was the error**, not that characterisation. The audit's refutation of my correction restores it.

**Confidence.** **Settled. Gate 2 passed** ([reviews/INDEX.md](reviews/INDEX.md) Reviewer 12): confirmed at 21 structured points, both witnesses, and generic points at $n=6$ *and* $n=7$; and strengthened, (A) and (B) are identities of the whole Weyl space, not just of critical points, and the theorem is equivalent to the single identity $S-(T_1+2T_2+T_3)=-\operatorname{tr}(P_-(Q(W)-\theta W)P_-)$.

### The exact $\theta$ formula, and where the ungraded bound has to come from

**Purpose.** Turn the decomposition into a bound. Code: [scripts/review_r11_theta_formula.py](scripts/reviewers/r11/review_r11_theta_formula.py).

**The formula.** The slack definition rearranges, at every critical point, into
$$\theta\operatorname{tr}(W_-)=\|\mathrm{Ric}(W_-)\|^2+6\delta^2-\operatorname{tr}(W_-^2)-S,\qquad S=T_1+2T_2+T_3\ge0,$$
verified to $\le3\times10^{-16}$ at all 17 points tested. **Slack enters negatively**: for fixed Ricci, defect and trace data, being ungraded costs $\theta$ directly, which is exactly the shape the crux needs. What is missing is control of the other three terms.

**The measured picture.** Sorted by $\theta$, the four graded points occupy the top ($1.2360,1.1456,1.1156,1.0541$, all $S=0$) and thirteen ungraded points follow, with a clear if non-strict downward trend: $S=0.30\to\theta=0.90$; $S=0.57$–$0.67\to0.84$–$0.85$; $S=0.86\to0.80$; $S=0.92\to0.39$; $S=1.64$–$1.80\to\theta=0.055$–$0.13$. Non-strict because $S=4/7$ still carries both $0.720$ and $0.837$, consistent with the earlier refutation of a monotone $\Theta(S)$.

**The structural find: $\mathrm{Ric}(W_-)$ is essentially scalar.** Since $\mathrm{Ric}(W_-)\succeq0$ with $\operatorname{tr}\mathrm{Ric}(W_-)=2\operatorname{tr}(W_-)$, the trivial bound is $\|\mathrm{Ric}(W_-)\|^2\le4\operatorname{tr}(W_-)^2$. Measured, the ratio $\|\mathrm{Ric}(W_-)\|^2/4\operatorname{tr}(W_-)^2$ sits in $[0.083,0.169]$ across *both* classes, and at most points it is **exactly $1/n$**: $0.0833=1/12$ at the balanced $S^6\times S^6$ and at $\mathbb{HP}^3$, $0.125=1/8$ at $S^4\times S^4$, $\mathbb{HP}^2$, $SU(3)$ and the $3/25$ violator, $0.1667=1/6$ at $S^3\times S^3$. That is precisely the Cauchy–Schwarz floor, attained iff $\mathrm{Ric}(W_-)=\tfrac{2\operatorname{tr}(W_-)}{n}\,\mathrm{Id}$. The deviations are small and upward: $0.1432$ at the $\theta=0.900828$ witness, $0.1682$ at a generic $n=6$ point.

**What this says about the route.** The trivial PSD bound is lossy by a factor of $6$–$12$, so it cannot be used; but the true value clusters at the *opposite* end of the admissible range, at or just above the scalar floor $4\operatorname{tr}(W_-)^2/n$. Substituting the floor gives
$$\theta=\frac{4\operatorname{tr}(W_-)}{n}+\frac{6\delta^2-\operatorname{tr}(W_-^2)-S}{\operatorname{tr}(W_-)}\qquad(\text{exact when }\mathrm{Ric}(W_-)\text{ is scalar}),$$
so the ungraded bound reduces to two ingredients: **an upper bound on $\|\mathrm{Ric}(W_-)\|^2$ near the scalar floor rather than the PSD ceiling**, and **control of $\operatorname{tr}(W_-)$**. Both are now concrete, finite-dimensional questions about a PSD operator with known trace, rather than statements about the critical set.

**Confidence.** High for the formula (exact rearrangement, machine-verified). High for the measured ratios (several are exact rationals $1/n$). The near-scalarity of $\mathrm{Ric}(W_-)$ is an observation with a clear mechanism at symmetric points and small measured deviations elsewhere, **not proven in general, and the deviations are in the unhelpful direction**, so a bound must accommodate them. **Gate 2 pending.**

### Two proven bounds for the $\theta$ formula, and a trap in assembling them

**Purpose.** Supply the two ingredients the exact $\theta$ formula needs. Both are elementary; the second nearly pins the conjectured maximum. Verified with zero violations across the catalogue at $n=6,8,12$.

**Bound 1, $\lambda_{\max}(\mathrm{Ric}(W_-))\le\operatorname{tr}(W_-)$.** Work in an orthonormal frame diagonalising $\mathrm{Ric}(W_-)$. Then $\lambda_{\max}=\mathrm{Ric}(W_-)_{11}=\sum_{k\ne1}(W_-)_{(1k)(1k)}$, a partial sum of $W_-$'s plane-diagonal entries, all nonnegative, since $W_-\succeq0$, whose total is $\operatorname{tr}(W_-)$. $\square$ This halves the trivial estimate to $\|\mathrm{Ric}(W_-)\|^2\le\lambda_{\max}\operatorname{tr}\mathrm{Ric}(W_-)=2\operatorname{tr}(W_-)^2$.

**Bound 2, $t:=\operatorname{tr}(W_-)\le(r_+r_-)^{1/4}/\sqrt2\le\sqrt N/2$, and the conjectured maximizer nearly saturates it.** Since $\operatorname{tr}W=\operatorname{scal}/2=0$ we have $\operatorname{tr}(W_+)=\operatorname{tr}(W_-)=t$, and Cauchy–Schwarz on each part gives $t\le\sqrt{r_\pm}\|W_\pm\|$; multiplying and using $\|W_+\|\|W_-\|\le\tfrac12(\|W_+\|^2+\|W_-\|^2)=\tfrac12$ yields $t^2\le\sqrt{r_+r_-}/2$, and $r_++r_-\le N$ gives the uniform form. $\square$ At $n=12$ the ceiling is $\sqrt{66}/2=4.0620$ and the balanced $S^6\times S^6$ sits at $4.0452$, **within $0.4\%$**, with its pair-specific ceiling $(r_+r_-)^{1/4}/\sqrt2=4.0536$ closer still. The conjectured maximizer is essentially the extremal object for this inequality, which is a structural fact worth having on its own.

***The trap: floors are not ceilings, and assembling them gives no bound.*** Substituting *both* Cauchy–Schwarz floors, $\|\mathrm{Ric}(W_-)\|^2\approx4t^2/n$ (attained iff $\mathrm{Ric}(W_-)$ is scalar) and $\operatorname{tr}(W_-^2)\approx t^2/r_-$ (attained iff $W_-$ has flat spectrum), produces the expression $4t/n-t/r_-$, which reproduces $\theta$ **exactly** at every sphere product, balanced and unbalanced ($1.05409$, $1.14564$, $1.23603$, $0.70256$, all to five decimals), because both floors are attained there. It is nevertheless **not an upper bound**: it under-estimates at $\mathbb{HP}^2$ ($1.0359$ against $\theta=1.11555$) and at the $\theta=0.900828$ witness ($0.8860$ against $0.90083$), and over-estimates elsewhere. The reason is structural, one floor enters with a $+$ sign and the other with a $-$, so using both biases in opposite directions. Recorded because the agreement at four sphere products is seductive and means nothing.

**What the valid chain needs.** Using the two proven bounds honestly gives $\theta\le2t+6\delta^2/t-t/r_--S/t$, whose leading term $2t$ is worthless at $n=12$ ($\approx8.1$ against $\theta_0=1.236$). The weak link is Bound 1: the measured $\lambda_{\max}(\mathrm{Ric}(W_-))/t$ lies in $[0.167,0.384]$, hugging $2/n$, while the proven bound allows $1$. **So the open ingredient is a bound $\lambda_{\max}(\mathrm{Ric}(W_-))\le C\,t/n$.** The right normalisation is $K:=\lambda_{\max}n/(2t)$, since the $n$ eigenvalues of $\mathrm{Ric}(W_-)$ are nonnegative with sum $2t$, so their mean is $2t/n$ and $K\ge1$ always, with $K=1$ exactly when $\mathrm{Ric}(W_-)$ is scalar. Whether $K$ is bounded uniformly in $n$ is settled in the next section, it is not.

**Confidence.** High for both bounds (elementary proofs, zero violations). High for the trap (explicit counterexamples in both directions). The dimension-uniformity of $\lambda_{\max}n/t$ is **unresolved and the measured trend is unfavourable**, this is flagged rather than assumed. **Gate 2 pending.**

### The Ricci spread $K$, no uniform bound, but it is anti-correlated with $\theta$

**Purpose.** Settle whether $\lambda_{\max}(\mathrm{Ric}(W_-))\le C\,t/n$ holds dimension-uniformly, which the $\theta$-chain needs. Code: [scripts/review_r11_ricci_spread.py](scripts/reviewers/r11/review_r11_ricci_spread.py). Measured across every constructible critical point at $n=6,8,10,12,14,16$ plus generic Levenberg–Marquardt points at $n=6,8$.

**Answer: no, $K$ grows linearly, and the maximum is exactly $n/4$.** With $K:=\lambda_{\max}n/(2t)\ge1$, the measured maxima are $1.5,2.0,2.5,3.0,3.5,4.0$ at $n=6,8,10,12,14,16$, that is $K_{\max}=n/4$ on the nose, against the proven ceiling $K\le n/2$ from $\lambda_{\max}\le t$. So a dimension-uniform $C$ **does not exist**, and the best uniform statement available is
$$\lambda_{\max}(\mathrm{Ric}(W_-))\le t/2,$$
a factor-two improvement on the earlier proven bound, saturated by $S^2\times S^{n-2}$.

**But the growth sits exactly where it does no harm.** For the two-factor sphere products the spread is exactly $K=n/(2p)$ with $p\le q$ the smaller factor, $4,\,8/3,\,2,\,8/5,\,4/3,\,8/7,\,1$ across $p=2,\dots,8$ at $n=16$, so $K$ is maximal at the *most unbalanced* split and falls to $1$ at the balanced one. And $\theta$ runs the other way over the same list: $0.99745,\,1.14834,\,1.21376,\,1.24838,\,1.26773,\,1.27775,\,1.28087$. **$K$ and $\theta$ are anti-correlated: every point with large spread has small value, and every high-$\theta$ point has $K\approx1$**, i.e. $\mathrm{Ric}(W_-)$ essentially scalar. The same holds off the sphere family, $\mathbb{HP}^3$ and $\mathbb{HP}^4$ have $K=1$ exactly, while the multi-block products with a size-$2$ factor carry the large values.

**Why this is the right structure anyway.** Feeding $\|\mathrm{Ric}(W_-)\|^2\le\lambda_{\max}\operatorname{tr}\mathrm{Ric}(W_-)=4Kt^2/n$ into the exact formula gives
$$\theta\le\frac{4Kt}{n}+\frac{6\delta^2-\operatorname{tr}(W_-^2)-S}{t},$$
and at $K=1$ with $t$ at its proven ceiling $\sqrt N/2$ the leading term is $4t/n\le2\sqrt N/n\to\sqrt2$, **exactly the known asymptotic supremum of $\theta$**. So the chain has the right shape and the right constant in the regime that matters; what defeats a naive bound is only that $K$ is uncontrolled in the low-$\theta$ regime, where the conclusion is not needed.

**Consequence for the route.** Do not seek a uniform bound on $K$, it is false. Seek instead the **joint constraint**: a bound of the form $\theta\le F(K)$ with $F$ decreasing, or more usefully a proof that $K>1+\epsilon$ forces $\theta$ below $\sqrt{3/2}$ directly. The sphere-product family gives the exact template, $K=n/(2p)$ against $\theta=\theta_{p,n}$, and both are explicit there.

**Confidence.** High for $K_{\max}=n/4$ (exact rational values at six dimensions, attained by an identified family) and for $K=n/(2p)$ on two-factor sphere products (exact at every split tested). High for the anti-correlation as an observation across all points measured; it is not proven, and proving it is now the concrete target. **Gate 2 pending.**

### A valid $\theta$ bound that separates the two classes, the crux route, assembled

**Purpose.** Assemble the pieces into an inequality that is *proven* (not a fitted pattern) and test whether it does the crux's job. Code: the evaluation is a few lines on top of [scripts/review_r11_slack_decomp.py](scripts/lib/review_r11_slack_decomp.py) and [scripts/review_r11_ricci_spread.py](scripts/reviewers/r11/review_r11_ricci_spread.py).

**The bound.** From the exact formula $\theta t=\|\mathrm{Ric}(W_-)\|^2+6\delta^2-\operatorname{tr}(W_-^2)-S$, the single inequality $\|\mathrm{Ric}(W_-)\|^2\le\lambda_{\max}\operatorname{tr}\mathrm{Ric}(W_-)=4Kt^2/n$ (valid for any PSD operator, $K=\lambda_{\max}n/2t$) gives, at **every** critical point,
$$\boxed{\;\theta\;\le\;\frac{4Kt}{n}+\frac{6\delta^2-\operatorname{tr}(W_-^2)-S}{t}\;}$$
with $S=T_1+2T_2+T_3\ge0$ the slack and $t=\operatorname{tr}(W_-)$. Verified across 27 critical points at $n=8,12,16$: **zero violations**, and it is an *equality* wherever $\mathrm{Ric}(W_-)$ is scalar ($K=1$), the balanced sphere products, $\mathbb{HP}^2$, $\mathbb{HP}^3$, $\mathbb{HP}^4$, the $SU(3)$ bi-invariant and the $\delta^2=3/25$ violator all sit at slack exactly $0$.

**Its separation claim did not survive Gate 2.** [reviews/INDEX.md](reviews/INDEX.md)'s Reviewer 12 confirmed the inequality itself and every tabulated number digit-for-digit, and then **refuted the separation**: two genuine ungraded $n=8$ points (residual $5\times10^{-16}$) have RHS *above* $\sqrt{3/2}$ ($\theta=0.899120\to1.23020$, $\theta=0.859435\to1.23588$). The table below was a 27-point-catalogue artifact, and the crux statement over $(K,t,\delta^2,S)$ is **false as stated**. The table is kept for the record:

| point | $\theta$ | bound | $S$ | $K$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| $\delta^2=3/25$ violator, $n=8$ | $0.38730$ | $0.38730$ | $0.9200$ | $1.000$ |
| $SU(3)$ bi-invariant, $n=8$ | $0.83666$ | $0.83666$ | $0.5714$ | $1.000$ |
| $\mathbb{HP}^3$, $n=12$ | $0.85294$ | $0.85294$ | $0.6734$ | $1.000$ |
| $S^3{\times}S^3{\times}S^6$, $n=12$ | $0.80204$ | $0.97704$ | $0.8612$ | $1.200$ |
| $S^2{\times}S^2{\times}S^8$, $n=12$ | $0.70256$ | $1.04319$ | $0.3916$ | $1.667$ |
| $S^2{\times}S^2{\times}S^{12}$, $n=16$ | $0.70497$ | $1.13880$ | $0.3181$ | $2.154$ |
| $\theta=0.900828$ witness, $n=8$ | $0.90083$ | $\mathbf{1.21622}$ | $0.3037$ | $1.462$ |

**And it correctly fails to exclude the graded ones**, as it must: at the balanced $S^6\times S^6$ the bound returns exactly $\theta_0(12)=1.23603$, above $\sqrt{3/2}$. So the inequality passes the sanity filter at the top of [plan.md](plan.md) by construction rather than by luck, it sees the crossover because $S$ and $K$ do.

**What is now needed, and how much room there is.** The crux would follow from: *for every critical point with $S>0$, the right-hand side is $<\sqrt{3/2}$.* That is a statement about four scalars $(K,t,\delta^2,S)$ subject to the proven constraints $K\ge1$, $t\le(r_+r_-)^{1/4}/\sqrt2\le\sqrt N/2$, $\delta^2\le1/4$, $\operatorname{tr}(W_-^2)\ge t^2/r_-$, no longer a statement about curvature operators at all. *(The margin discussion that stood here is obsolete, the margin is not thin, it is negative at the refuting points above.)*

**Confidence.** High that the bound is valid, it is one PSD inequality applied to an exact identity, and it held at all 27 points with equality in the six scalar-Ricci cases. High for the tabulated values. **The crux statement itself is not proven**: what is shown is that a proven inequality separates the two classes on every point available, with one thin margin. **Gate 2 pending.**

### Where the assembled bound blocks, stated precisely

**A second proven Ricci bound, and it is weaker.** Per-index Cauchy–Schwarz on $\rho_i=\sum_{k\ne i}(W_-)_{(ik)(ik)}$ gives $\rho_i^2\le(n-1)\sum_{k\ne i}(W_-)^2_{(ik)(ik)}$, and summing yields
$$\|\mathrm{Ric}(W_-)\|^2\le2(n-1)\operatorname{tr}(W_-^2).$$
Valid at all 27 points (zero violations), but **the $K$-bound $4Kt^2/n$ is tighter at every one of them**, so this route does not improve the assembly. One by-product worth keeping: for two-factor sphere products the ratio is exactly $(n/2)/(n-1)$ at every split, i.e. $\|\mathrm{Ric}(W_-)\|^2=n\operatorname{tr}(W_-^2)$ identically on that family (checked at $n=12$ and $n=16$, all splits), it fails off the family ($\mathbb{HP}^2$ gives $0.536$ against the predicted $4/7$).

**The blocker, precisely.** The assembled bound $\theta\le4Kt/n+(6\delta^2-\operatorname{tr}(W_-^2)-S)/t$ is proven and separates the classes on every point available, but it **cannot be closed as stated**, because $K$ is not bounded uniformly: $K$ ranges up to $n/4$, so the leading term $4Kt/n$ ranges up to $t\le\sqrt N/2$, which grows with $n$. Feeding in only the proven constraints, $K\ge1$, $t\le(r_+r_-)^{1/4}/\sqrt2$, $\delta^2\le1/4$, $\operatorname{tr}(W_-^2)\ge t^2/r_-$, $S>0$, leaves the right-hand side unbounded. **So closing the crux needs one more ingredient: a constraint tying $K$ to the remaining data.** The empirical content of that missing constraint is exactly the anti-correlation already measured, large $K$ occurs only at small $\theta$, and on the sphere-product family it is explicit ($K=n/(2p)$ against $\theta_{p,n}$), which is the natural place to look for its general form.

**This is the same failure mode the project has hit before**, and worth naming as such: individually sharp bounds that are jointly lossy because their extremal configurations are incompatible. It appeared first when the Huisken $\operatorname{tr}(W^3)$ bound and the vertex-matrix $\langle W^\#,W\rangle$ bound summed to a $1.7$–$1.8\times$ overshoot, and again when the two Cauchy–Schwarz floors reproduced $\theta$ at four sphere products without bounding it. Here the $K$-bound is sharp exactly when $\mathrm{Ric}(W_-)$ is scalar and the $t$-bound is sharp exactly at the balanced sphere product, and no single critical point makes both sharp except the maximizer itself.

**Confidence.** High for the Cauchy–Schwarz bound and for its being uniformly weaker (explicit at 27 points). High for the blocker statement, which is a matter of the constraints admitting unbounded $K$, not an observation but a consequence of $K_{\max}=n/4$ being attained. **Gate 2 pending.**

### Family C's non-simple isotropy, the unbalanced quaternionic pairs carry no graded critical point

**Purpose.** P2(i), the last classical gap in the graded enumeration. Code: [scripts/review_r11_sp_classes.py](scripts/lib/review_r11_sp_classes.py).

**Result 1, $(\mathfrak{sp}(m),\mathfrak{sp}(j)\oplus\mathfrak{sp}(m-j))$ with $j\ne m-j$ carries no Ricci-flat critical point of the ideal-wise shape**, at $(m,j)=(3,1)$ and $(4,1)$, i.e. $n=12$ and $n=16$. With the single-Casimir screen's earlier rejection of the balanced quaternionic pairs and of $(\mathfrak{su}(2k),\mathfrak{sp}(k))$ in exact arithmetic, the quaternionic *Grassmannian* branch is empty.

**Result 2, but $Sp(m)/U(m)$ is not, and it completes family C.** Rebuilt correctly (see the voided attempt below), $(\mathfrak{sp}(m),\mathfrak u(m))$ **does** carry critical points, with ranks now matching theory exactly ($\dim\mathfrak k=4,9,16$; $\dim\mathfrak m=6,12,20$):

| $n$ | pair | $\theta$ | $\delta^2$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | $(\mathfrak{sp}(2),\mathfrak u(2))$ | $0.942809=\sqrt{8/9}$ | $1/9$ |
| 12 | $(\mathfrak{sp}(3),\mathfrak u(3))$ | $0.833333=5/6$ | $1/9$ |
| 16 | $(\mathfrak{sp}(4),\mathfrak u(4))$ | $0.774597=\sqrt{3/5}$ | $1/9$ |

Every member is **defective with $\delta^2=1/9$ exactly, the same defect as Fox**, and every one sits **below $\sqrt{3/2}$**, decreasing in $m$. So family C is now complete and consistent with the conjecture: it supplies defective critical points, none of them competitive. *(The line "the entire quaternionic branch is empty", written before this fix, was wrong and is corrected here.)*

**Gate 1, and it earned its place twice.** *(a) Positive control:* the same solver, fed the sphere-product splitting $\mathfrak k=\mathfrak{so}(p)\oplus\mathfrak{so}(q)$ with $\mathfrak m$ the mixed planes, returns $1.145644$, $1.236033$ and $1.228239$ at $S^4\times S^4$, $S^6\times S^6$ and $S^5\times S^7$, exact agreement with the closed form, so a "no critical point" verdict from it means something. *(c) Validity screen:* the projection ranks were checked against theory before the verdict was believed, $13/13$ and $24/24$ for $\mathfrak k$, $8/8$ and $12/12$ for $\mathfrak m$.

***And the screen voided the other half of the run.*** The $(\mathfrak{sp}(m),\mathfrak u(m))$ cases returned "no critical point" as well, but their projections are **wrong**: $\dim\mathfrak k$ came out $10,21,36$ against the correct $4,9,16$, with $\dim\mathfrak m=0$. The cause is a conceptual error, not a coding slip, $\mathfrak{sp}(m)$ was built as the centraliser of the left multiplications $I,J,K$, so intersecting it again with the centraliser of $I$ returns all of $\mathfrak{sp}(m)$. The correct construction needs the *right* multiplications: $\mathfrak{sp}(m)$ as the centraliser of $R_i,R_j,R_k$, and then $\mathfrak u(m)$ as the part of it commuting with a chosen left multiplication. **Rebuilding it that way fixes the ranks and produces the critical points tabulated in Result 2 above**, so the three "no critical point" verdicts were pure artifact, and had the rank check not been run they would have entered this file as findings. This is the third time in this project that an unverified "no solution exists" turned out to be a construction bug.

**Confidence.** **Gate 2 passed for both results** ([reviews/INDEX.md](reviews/INDEX.md) Reviewer 12: independent fixed construction, 9-digit agreement, ranks and controls confirmed). *One repo-hygiene defect it caught:* the fixed $Sp(m)/U(m)$ construction behind the table existed only in a session heredoc while the on-disk script still carried the broken pre-fix version, the corrected code is now written into [scripts/review_r11_sp_classes.py](scripts/lib/review_r11_sp_classes.py) as `sp_u_projections_fixed` (re-verified: ranks $4/6$ and $9/12$, $\theta=0.942809,0.833333$), with the broken branch kept and labelled so the false-negative episode stays reproducible.

Five of the twelve pairs are rejected outright by the consistency screen ($c_{\mathfrak k}<0$, or $2q\le p$, or $2q=p$ degenerate). *Scope, stated: the pairs with non-simple $\mathfrak k$ are screened rather than solved, since the two-eigenvalue dictionary does not strictly apply to them; the two with simple $\mathfrak k$ that survive ($E_6/\mathfrak{sp}(4)$, $E_7/\mathfrak{su}(8)$) are properly computed. Given the margin, the largest value is $12\%$ below the target and most are $60$–$95\%$ below, the distinction does not affect the conclusion.*

**P3(i): $J_5\ge0$ holds at every critical point tested, and the cross-term stays small.** Recomputed across 20 points at $n=6,8,12$ including the multi-block products, $\mathbb{HP}^2$, $\mathbb{HP}^3$, the $SU(3)$ bi-invariant, the $\delta^2=3/25$ violator, the $\theta=0.900828$ witness and three generic Levenberg–Marquardt saddles: **zero violations of $J_5\ge0$**. The reduced open statement is $|\langle X_{\mathrm{cross}},H_{\mathrm{cross}}\rangle|\le J_5^{\mathrm{diag}}$, and the measured ratio is $\le3.93\times10^{-2}$ (Reviewer 12's update, worst at its new $\theta=0.859$ point), a factor-$25$ margin. At every named competitor the cross term vanishes to $10^{-15}$ or better, confirming the isotropy argument that predicted it. This widens the earlier evidence base (which reached $0.27\%$ at generic $n=6$ saddles only) to the adversarial points, at the cost of a larger worst-case ratio.

**Confidence.** High for the exceptional screen at its stated scope. High for the $J_5$ numerics. **Neither is a proof**: $J_5\ge0$ off the commuting class remains the open grant, now with a quantified margin rather than a bare conjecture. **Gate 2 pending.**

### P4(i): Fox's mixed flat directions at second order

**Purpose.** The Fox first-order protection lemma is proven and the padded $\mathcal W_{n-4}$ flat is second-order safe with an $18\times$ margin, but the *mixed* directions of the equality manifold $\{F=0\}$, those whose support meets both the distinguished $4$-plane and its complement, rested on undirected $200$-direction fans. This targets them specifically, sampling only directions with at least $15\%$ of their Frobenius mass in mixed blocks.

**Result at $n=12$: no increase.** Over 100 mixed directions, the worst second-order coefficient $(\Phi(t)-\Phi(0))/t^2$ is $-1.8275$, i.e. every one of them decreases $\Phi=P-\kappa_n\delta^2$. Consistent with $\mathcal S^4(\alpha)$ being a local maximum of the penalized functional at the threshold dimension.

**And $n=8$ supplies the positive control.** There $\kappa_8=+0.712$ (the sign flips below the crossover), and the same test finds a clear increase, worst coefficient $+4.3291$, reproducing the known $n\le11$ escape from a completely different sampling. So the machinery detects increases when they exist, which is what makes the $n=12$ null result worth anything.

*A checkpoint worth noting:* $\Phi$ evaluates to exactly $\theta_0(n)$ at Fox in both dimensions ($1.145644$ at $n=8$, $1.236033$ at $n=12$), which is forced by the definition $\kappa_n=9(\sqrt{3/2}-\theta_0(n))$ together with $\delta^2(\mathcal S^4(\alpha))=1/9$, the two champions sit at the same $\Phi$ by construction. It is a useful arithmetic check that the operator and the constant were both built right.

**Confidence.** The $n=12$ result is directed numerical evidence with a working positive control, not a proof; the second-order argument on $\{F=0\}$ remains owed. **Gate 2 pending.**

### Unblocking P1, the Tachibana factor is the missing $K$-controller, and $\sqrt{3/2}$ is Fox's Ricci shape

**The idea.** The crux was blocked because the assembled $\theta$ bound has no constraint tying the Ricci spread $K$ to anything. But the repo already owns a **second exact identity in the same unknowns**: the lifted §3.3 master identity (Reviewers 9/10-confirmed), whose leading term carries the Tachibana factor $\sqrt2\sqrt{1-\operatorname{tr}\hat S^4}$ with $\hat S=\mathrm{Ric}(W_-)/\|\mathrm{Ric}(W_-)\|$. **That factor is exactly the missing $K$-controller**: a spread Ricci spectrum means a large fourth moment, which *lowers* the ceiling, the mechanism behind the measured $K$–$\theta$ anti-correlation. So the route is to use identities (I) (the exact $\theta$ formula, where $S$ enters negatively) and (II) (the §3.3 identity, where the spread enters negatively) **jointly**, eliminating $\|\mathrm{Ric}(W_-)\|^2$ between them.

**A structural fact found on the way, exact and striking.** At Fox, $\mathrm{Ric}(W_-)$ is scalar on its $4$-plane, so $\operatorname{tr}\hat S^4=1/4$ exactly and
$$\sqrt2\sqrt{1-\tfrac14}=\sqrt{3/2}.$$
**The crossover constant is the Tachibana factor evaluated at Fox's Ricci shape.** Verified at $n=8,12,16$: the leading factor equals $1.224745$ to six digits at every padding of Fox. This is a second independent explanation of why $\sqrt{3/2}$ is the threshold, from the analytic side rather than the idempotent-norm side, and it says the constant is not numerology: it is $\sqrt2\cdot\sqrt{1-1/4}$, the $4$-plane's fourth-moment signature.

**The granting-form candidate, tested.** Granting $J_5\ge0$ and the proven $J_4$ cap, dropping $\sqrt{1-e^2}\le1$ and the PSD term $\langle\mathrm{Ric}(W_-^2),\rho\rangle\ge0$, identity (II) yields
$$\theta\;\le\;\sqrt2\sqrt{1-\operatorname{tr}\hat S^4}\;+\;12\,\delta^2\lambda_{\max}(\rho)/\|\rho\|^2 .$$
Evaluated at 24 critical points across $n=8,12,16$: **valid at every one (zero violations)**, but **not yet separating**: no defective point lands below $\sqrt{3/2}$ by it, because the two dropped negative terms carry real weight (at Fox the identity closes only through them: leading $1.2247$ plus cap $0.8165$ against the true $\theta=1.2247$).

**The precisely-stated next step.** Identity (I) gives $\|\rho\|^2=\theta t+u+S-6\delta^2$ *exactly*, so substituting it into (II) replaces the granted denominator by exact data and makes the result **quadratic in $\theta$ with $S$ appearing at negative sign**: the reverse-compression inequality P1 wanted, obtained by pairing the two reviewed identities rather than inventing a new bound. What then remains is bounding two shape factors ($e^2$ from below, $\langle\mathrm{Ric}(W_-^2),\rho\rangle$ from below, the latter $\ge2\lambda_{\min}(\rho)u$ trivially), both finite-dimensional. This derivation is hand algebra on established identities and is the named continuation.

**Also recorded, ideas for the other two blockers.** *P4(ii):* the Hessian at $W^*$ block-diagonalises under the $O(p)\times O(q)$ isotypic decomposition, whose components stabilise in $n$, so its eigenvalues are rational functions of $n$ on finitely many families, fittable exactly from the computed dimensions and then provable by the held-out method that settled the trace identities. *P3:* the cross term $\langle X_{\mathrm{cross}},H_{\mathrm{cross}}\rangle$ vanishes with $[H,W]$, and $\|[H,W]\|$ is controlled by the spread of $\mathrm{Ric}(|W|)$, the same quantity the Tachibana factor prices, so the (I)+(II) elimination should bound it as a by-product.

**Confidence.** The candidate's validity is machine-checked at 24 points; the $\operatorname{tr}\hat S^4=1/4\Rightarrow\sqrt{3/2}$ identity at Fox is exact. The elimination program is stated, not executed. **Gate 2 pending.**

### The sharp (II)-side bound, a theorem modulo one grant, exact at Fox, separating every ungraded point tested

**The statement.** Since identity (II) is exact and $J_4\le24\delta^2\lambda_{\max}(\mathrm{Ric}(|W|))$ is proven, granting only $J_5\ge0$ gives, at every critical point,
$$\theta\;\le\;\sqrt2\sqrt{1-\operatorname{tr}\hat S^4}\,\sqrt{1-e^2}\;-\;\frac{\langle\mathrm{Ric}(W_-^2),\rho\rangle}{\|\rho\|^2}\;+\;\frac{12\,\delta^2\lambda_{\max}(\rho)}{\|\rho\|^2},$$
with $\rho=\mathrm{Ric}(W_-)$, $\hat S=\rho/\|\rho\|$, and $e$ the misalignment of $|W|$ with $\mathrm{Ric}\wedge\mathrm{Ric}$. **This is not a new conjecture, it is the reviewed §3.3 identity with one proven cap and one granted sign**, i.e. a theorem modulo the $J_5$ grant that P3 already carries.

**Behaviour at 15 points, $n=8,12$ ([the test script's output, zero violations]):**
- **Exact equality at every zero-defect critical point**, balanced and unbalanced spheres, multi-block products give bound $=\theta$ to $10^{-6}$, because $J_4=J_5=0$ there and the cap is exact.
- **Exact equality at Fox, in closed form.** Fox's data all collapse to radicals: $\operatorname{tr}\hat S^4=1/4$, $\sqrt{1-e^2}=2/3$, $B/\|\rho\|^2=1/\sqrt6$, cap $=2/\sqrt6$, assembling to $\sqrt{3/2}\cdot\tfrac23-\tfrac1{\sqrt6}+\tfrac2{\sqrt6}=\sqrt{3/2}$ exactly. **The bound is sharp at precisely the point the crux statement must not exclude.**
- **Every ungraded point tested lands strictly below $\sqrt{3/2}$**: the multi-block spheres at $0.888$–$1.071$, $SU(3)$ bi-invariant at $1.0757$, the $\delta^2=3/25$ violator at $0.9812$, the $\theta=0.900828$ witness at $1.0503$, $\mathbb{HP}^3$ at $1.0597$. ($\mathbb{HP}^2$, graded, gets bound $=\theta=1.1156$, also below, harmlessly.)

**Where ungradedness enters.** Not through $S$ explicitly but through $e$: the ungraded points have $\sqrt{1-e^2}\approx0.73$–$0.88$ against $\approx0.99$ at the balanced spheres, the misalignment of $|W|$ with $\mathrm{Ric}\wedge\mathrm{Ric}$ *is* the analytic shadow of the slack. The (I)–(II) elimination remains available to make that connection exact.

**The crux, restated one more level down.** What remains is: *for critical $W$ with $S>0$, the right-hand side above is $<\sqrt{3/2}$.* All four ingredients are Ricci-side data of $W_-$; the statement has a built-in equality case at Fox (which has $S=0$, so it does not obstruct); and on every available point the margin is $0.15$–$0.34$ except at $\mathbb{HP}^2$'s harmless $0.11$. This is the most constrained form the crux has taken: a sharpness analysis of one explicit functional around one closed-form equality case, in place of a search over the critical set.

**Stress-tested against Reviewer 12's adversarial points, and it survives where the assembled bound died.** At the two points that refute the assembled bound's separation, the sharp bound gives RHS $=1.073451$ ($\theta=0.859435$) and $1.088933$ (the new record $\theta=0.906672$), margins $0.15$ and $0.14$ below $\sqrt{3/2}$, against the assembled bound's $1.23588$ and beyond. The $e$- and $B$-terms, which the assembled bound discards, are exactly what absorb these points. **Confidence.** Validity inherited from reviewed components; separation now measured at 17 points *including every adversarial one available*, but still not proven. **Gate 2 pending** (the bound postdates Reviewer 12's launch).

### The alternative-embedding growth argument is false, P2's residue is real

**What was asserted.** The spin-embedding enumeration found $n=8$ uniquely, and the write-up added that "the same exponential-vs-linear growth argument applies to every non-vector irrep". That was an assertion, never checked, and it is **wrong**.

**Why it fails.** Spin representations grow exponentially ($2^{\lfloor k/2\rfloor}$), which is what confined $\dim(\mathrm{spin}_j)\dim(\mathrm{spin}_{N-j})=N$ to a single dimension. But for the *classical* families the minimal nontrivial irreducible dimension grows only **linearly** in the rank ($r+1$ for $\mathfrak{su}(r+1)$, $2r$ for $\mathfrak{sp}(r)$ and $\mathfrak{so}(2r)$) while the algebra's dimension grows quadratically. So the constraint $n\ge m(\mathfrak k_1)m(\mathfrak k_2)$ is satisfied by an unbounded family, not a finite one. Enumerated over all classical and exceptional types with $n\le200$ ([scripts/review_r11_altembed_growth.py](scripts/reviewers/r11/review_r11_altembed_growth.py)), candidates appear densely, $\mathfrak{so}(10)\times\mathfrak{so}(20)$ at $n=200$ with $\dim\mathfrak k=235$, $\mathfrak{sp}(5)\times\mathfrak{sp}(10)$ at $n=200$, $\mathfrak{su}(9)\times\mathfrak{sp}(11)$ at $n=198$, and many more at every scale down to $n=12$.

**What this costs and what it does not.** The enumeration only shows these are not excluded *by size*; it says nothing about whether any is a genuine symmetric-pair isotropy carrying a critical point, and the overwhelming majority will fail the (R1) consistency check exactly as the quaternionic families did. **But they must be excluded by that check, not by counting**, the closure of the graded enumeration therefore rests on a case analysis nobody has run, not on a growth argument. This is a genuine widening of P2's residue, found by testing my own assertion rather than by an audit.

**Confidence.** High for the refutation (explicit candidates, elementary dimension arithmetic). The scope of what remains, whether any surviving candidate is a real symmetric pair with a critical point above $\sqrt{3/2}$, is **open and larger than previously recorded**.

### P4(ii): the sphere pair's Hessian spectrum, in closed form, negative-definiteness reduced to four rational families

**Purpose.** $W^*$'s Hessian negative-definiteness was machine-verified dimension by dimension but never proven for general even $n$. The isotypic route predicted the eigenvalues would be rational functions of $n$ on finitely many families. They are, and there are only four.

**The spectrum.** Writing $m=n/2$ and normalising by $\theta_0(n)$, the full tangent-space Hessian at the balanced $S^m\times S^m$ has **exactly five distinct eigenvalues**, all rational in $m$:
$$\Bigl\{\,0,\;-\tfrac{3}{m-1},\;-\tfrac{3(m-3)}{m-1},\;-3,\;-\tfrac{3(m+1)}{m-1}\,\Bigr\}\cdot\theta_0(n),$$
with multiplicities $m^2$ (the kernel, $=$ the $O(n)$-orbit dimension $\binom n2-2\binom m2$), $(m-1)(m+2)$, and $\binom m2^2$ for the first three. Fitted on $n=6,8,10,12,14$ and then **predicted for $n=16$ before computing it**: the measured spectrum is $0^{\times64}$, $-0.428571^{\times70}$, $-2.142857^{\times784}$, $-3^{\times3160}$, $-3.857143^{\times1225}$, every value and both fitted multiplicities exact ($m^2=64$, $(m-1)(m+2)=70$, $\binom82^2=784$).

**The consequence.** For $m\ge4$ every nonzero family is strictly negative, $\tfrac3{m-1}>0$, $\tfrac{3(m-3)}{m-1}>0$, $3$, $\tfrac{3(m+1)}{m-1}>0$, all entering with a minus sign, so **negative semi-definiteness with kernel exactly the orbit holds for all even $n\ge8$, reduced from a computation per dimension to a statement about four explicit rational functions.** The small-$m$ degeneracies are visible and explain the recorded anomalies: at $m=4$ the families $-\tfrac3{m-1}$ and $-\tfrac{3(m-3)}{m-1}$ collide at $-1$ (multiplicities $18+36=54$, matching the measured $n=8$ row), and at $m=3$ the third family hits $0$ and merges with the kernel, which is exactly the doubled $n=6$ kernel ($18$ against orbit dimension $9$) that has been flagged as an exceptional-isomorphism artifact since the earliest Hessian work.

**What remains for a proof.** The eigenvalue *values* and the three fitted multiplicities now need derivation from the $O(m)\times O(m)$ isotypic decomposition of the tangent space rather than from fitting, the same route that turned the $L_W$ trace identities from fitted rationals into theorems, and with the same held-out-prediction evidence behind it. The reduction itself is complete: no further computation per dimension is needed.

**Confidence.** High for the closed form (five values and three multiplicity formulas, fitted on five dimensions and confirmed exactly on a held-out sixth, with the two known low-$m$ anomalies falling out as predicted degeneracies). The derivation from branching is not done. **Gate 2 pending.**

### P1 localised: the crux reduced to $(1-\operatorname{tr}\hat S^4)(1-e^2)\le\tfrac34$, superseded, see Reviewer 13 below

**What carries the separation.** Writing the sharp (II)-side bound as $\mathrm{RHS}=L\cdot E-B+C$ with $L=\sqrt2\sqrt{1-\operatorname{tr}\hat S^4}$, $E=\sqrt{1-e^2}$, $B=\langle\mathrm{Ric}(W_-^2),\rho\rangle/\|\rho\|^2$ and $C$ the defect cap, the separation is carried **entirely by the leading product $L\cdot E$**. Measured across 19 critical points at $n=8,12$:

- $L\cdot E\ge\sqrt{3/2}$ at **exactly six points, and every one is a sphere product** ($S^3\times S^5$, $S^4\times S^4$, $S^3\times S^9$, $S^4\times S^8$, $S^5\times S^7$, $S^6\times S^6$; values $1.2456$–$1.3484$), precisely the graded objects that are *supposed* to sit at or above the threshold.
- $L\cdot E<\sqrt{3/2}$ at **every ungraded point**, maximum $1.19523$ at the $SU(3)$ bi-invariant, and $1.0346$/$1.0932$ at Reviewer 12's two adversarial points.
- The remaining terms are nearly self-cancelling on the ungraded side: $C-B$ measures $-0.004$ at the record, $+0.039$ at the breaker, $-0.120$ at $SU(3)$, so $\mathrm{RHS}\approx L\cdot E$ there.

**The reduction.** Since $(L\cdot E)^2=2(1-\operatorname{tr}\hat S^4)(1-e^2)$, the crux becomes: **for every critical point with $S>0$,**
$$\bigl(1-\operatorname{tr}\hat S^4\bigr)\bigl(1-e^2\bigr)\;\le\;\tfrac34 .$$
Two shape parameters of the Ricci data and nothing else, $\operatorname{tr}\hat S^4$ the fourth moment of the normalised $\mathrm{Ric}(W_-)$ spectrum, $e$ the misalignment of $|W|$ with $\mathrm{Ric}\wedge\mathrm{Ric}$, both of them quantities Jäger's chain already works with. Measured maximum over ungraded points: $0.714$ against the required $0.75$, a $5\%$ margin; the sphere products sit at $0.78$–$0.91$, i.e. above, as they must.

**Why this is the right form.** It removes $\theta$, $S$, $t$, $K$ and $\delta^2$ from the statement entirely. The mechanism is visible: ungraded points cannot align $|W|$ strongly with $\mathrm{Ric}\wedge\mathrm{Ric}$, their $E$ runs $0.73$–$0.90$ against $0.95$–$0.996$ at sphere products, and that misalignment *is* the analytic shadow of the bracket mass measured by $S$. Making that link exact (an inequality $E\le f(S)$, or a direct bound on the product) is the remaining work, and it is now a statement about two scalars rather than about the critical set.

**Confidence.** High for the localisation (explicit at 19 points, with the six exceedances all identified and all graded). The two-parameter inequality is **measured, not proven**, with a $5\%$ margin at the tightest ungraded point, and the day's record is that unproven separation claims of exactly this shape have twice been refuted by a wider search. **Gate 2 pending; Reviewer 13 is auditing the parent bound.**

### Literature check, overdue, much of this round's work exists in Nienhaus 2023, and one "open" item is a published theorem

**How this was found.** Prompted by the observation that this round had produced no citations at all, a literature search was finally run. The repo's earlier rounds did substantial source work; this round did none, and the from-scratch results kept checking out, which hid the omission. What follows corrects the record.

**The primary source is [Nienhaus, *Towards Finding the Second Best Einstein Metric in Low Dimensions*, arXiv:2311.02404](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2311.02404)**, already cited in this file, but as merely "referencing the conjecture in passing." **That assessment was wrong.** The thesis contains:

- **Conjecture A, verbatim, and stated for critical points**, exactly the framing used throughout this project: *"Let $W\in\mathrm{Weyl}_n$ be a unit Weyl curvature operator that is a critical point of $P(R)=\langle R^2+R^\#,R\rangle$ among $\mathrm{Weyl}^1_n$. If either $n\ge12$ or $8\le n\le11$ and $W\notin SO(n).W_{\mathbb{CP}^2}$, we have $P(W)\le P(W^{\mathrm{crit}}_{\mathrm{sym}})$."* Attributed there to B. Wilking.
- **Proposition 2.25, the closed form for every sphere product**: $\theta_{k,l}=\sqrt2\sqrt{\tfrac{k-1}{k}\cdot\tfrac{l-1}{l}\cdot\tfrac{n-1}{n-2}}$ with $P(W_{S_{k,l}})=\theta_{k,l}$. Verified against this repo: it reproduces $\theta_0(n)=\sqrt{2(n-1)(n-2)}/n$ at $k=l$ and $1.228239$ at $S^5\times S^7$, both of which were derived here independently.
- **Chapter 4.2–4.4**: the irreducible decomposition of $\mathrm{Weyl}_n$ under $SO(k)\times SO(l)$ and under $\mathrm{Stab}(W_{\mathbb{CP}^2})$, used to compute the Hessian of the potential, **precisely the isotypic route named for P4(ii) here**, where the spectrum was instead fitted numerically.
- **Chapter 5, "Algebraically symmetric spaces"**, with sections on symmetric pairs and an "algebraic symmetry operator", the territory of this round's graded/symmetric-pair classification.

***And Theorem 4.19 is the localization inequality this project lists as an open problem (P5).*** Quoted: *"Let $10\le n\le11$. Then for any $W\in\mathrm{Weyl}^1_n\setminus U_{W_{\mathbb{CP}^2}}$ the potential satisfies $P(W)\le P(W^{\mathrm{crit}}_{\mathrm{sym}})=\theta_n$, where $U_{W_{\mathbb{CP}^2}}=\{W\in\mathrm{Weyl}^1_n\mid d(W,SO(n).W_{\mathbb{CP}^2})<\gamma_n\}$ with $\gamma_{11}=0.13$ and $\gamma_{10}=0.26$."* Two things about this are striking. It is proven for **all** unit Weyl operators, not merely critical ones, far stronger than what P5 assumed available. And its radius $\gamma_{11}=0.13$ sits right beside the $\rho\ge0.1$ this repo measured empirically for the same statement, without knowing the theorem existed.

**What this implies for strategy, and it is favourable.** For $n\ge12$ Conjecture A carries no $\mathbb{CP}^2$ exception, and Fox's value $\sqrt{3/2}$ lies *below* $\theta_0(n)$. So the natural route is: extend Theorem 4.19's method, the Chapter 4 isotypic machinery, from $n=10,11$ to $n\ge12$, and then dispose of the tubular neighbourhood $U_{W_{\mathbb{CP}^2}}$ using the local analysis at Fox, which this repo has already proven (the first-order protection lemma, the padded-flat second-order margin, the mixed-direction tests) and which Chapter 4.4 also supplies. **That is a concrete proof architecture built mostly from existing pieces**, and it is materially different from the from-scratch inequality-hunting this round pursued.

**Also located: [Petersen–Stanfield, arXiv:2508.11236](https://arxiv.org/html/2508.11236v1) (2025)**, computing curvature operators of *all* compact irreducible symmetric spaces: eigenvalues lie in $[0,1/2]$, there are **at most three distinct nonzero rational eigenvalues** with only the complex Grassmannians achieving three, and simple isotropy gives exactly one (their Theorem C, $\lambda=\tfrac14\dim M/\dim H$). This matches the spectra measured here, two eigenvalues at sphere products, three at $\mathbb{HP}^2$, and would have supplied the graded enumeration's classification data directly.

**Assessment.** Independent rederivation earned its keep, several results survived audits that a literature-only approach would not have stress-tested, and the sphere-product formula, the crossover constant and the $\mathbb{CP}^2$ competitor were all confirmed against the sources. But a chapter-by-chapter overlap with a 2023 thesis went unnoticed for a full round, and one item on the open-problems list is a published theorem. **The next work should start from Chapters 4 and 5 of arXiv:2311.02404, not from scratch.**

### The $n\le11$ restriction in Nienhaus Theorem 4.17/4.19 is a low-dimension obstruction, and the margin *grows* with $n$

**What the proof actually needs.** Reading the proof of [Nienhaus](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2311.02404) Theorem 4.17: for $W$ perpendicular to $\mathbb RW_{\mathbb{CP}^2}\oplus T_{W_{\mathbb{CP}^2}}(SO(n)\cdot W_{\mathbb{CP}^2})$, the function $f(\varphi)=\sqrt{2/3}\,P(\cos\varphi\,W_{\mathbb{CP}^2}+\sin\varphi\,W)$ expands as
$$f(\varphi)=\cos^3\varphi+3\cos\varphi\sin^2\varphi\,\alpha+\sin^3\varphi\,\gamma,\qquad \alpha=\sqrt{2/3}\langle Q(W),W_{\mathbb{CP}^2}\rangle,\ \gamma=\sqrt{2/3}P(W),$$
and Proposition 4.14 gives $\alpha\le\tfrac13$. The chain then yields the **dimension-free** bound
$$f(\pi/6)\;\le\;g_2(1/3)=\tfrac{5\sqrt3}{9}\approx0.9622504486 ,$$
