## The $23!!$ closure priced the wrong algorithm

**The closure at "Result 3" above, *exhaustive enumeration stops after degree 4, $19!!$ at degree 5, $23!!$ at degree 6*, is retired.** *Reviewer 175, and the correction is the same one that removed "infeasible" from the $n\ge12$ line of [plan.md](plan.md).*

**Degree six factorises through degree three, so the $23!!$ complete contractions are never enumerated.** A sextic invariant of $W$ is an inner product of two cubic covariants, and a cubic covariant is a **partial matching on the twelve indices of $W^{\otimes3}$**, at most $I(12)=140\,152$ of them, the involution number, checked as $a_{12}=a_{11}+11a_{10}=35\,696+11\cdot9496$. The Gram entries are then the pairings of the leftover free indices, $17\,020$ of them. **About $12$ MB, and $n$-independent: every $n\ge12$ at once.** *Against $23!!\approx3\cdot10^{11}$, which is what enumerating the sextics directly costs.*

**What made the closure wrong is that it enumerated the object it wanted instead of the object it is built from.** The cubic covariants are the natural coordinates, $\theta$ itself is cubic, and the sextic layer is a Gram matrix over them rather than a list to be generated. *The degree-$6$ dimension $89$ has since been obtained by plethysm regardless, so nothing downstream rested on the closure; what rested on it was the belief that the $n\ge12$ Gram is out of reach.*

## Diagram realisation, one seed per block

**Tried:** exhibiting each of the 184 covariants as an explicit Brauer-diagram combination, one at a time. **Abandoned before writing any of it:** that is 184 separate problems and the widest pairing alone runs to 33,177,600 terms (r258).

**What worked instead**, the structural route, in [run_diagram_realisation.py](scripts/runs/run_diagram_realisation.py) and [findings/brauer-pairing.md](findings/brauer-pairing.md). Semisimplicity of $B_{12}(12)$ makes each multiplicity space an irreducible cell module, so a single nonzero seed generates it under the diagram action, and the $\mathrm{Sym}^3(\mathrm{Weyl})$ projector stays inside $\nu(B_{12}(n))$ by SFT surjectivity.

**The wrong turn, kept because it is easy to repeat.** The first verification measured $\operatorname{span}\{\nu(D)v\}$ for a generic $v$ and compared it against $\sum_\lambda \dim\Delta_\lambda$. It failed at $(f,n)=(3,2)$, 7 against a prediction of 4, and the assert read as a refutation of the theorem. **The prediction was wrong, not the theorem.** A generic $v$ spreads across every isotypic and several copies of each, so the span it generates is $\sum_\lambda \min(\dim V_\lambda, \dim\Delta_\lambda)\cdot\dim\Delta_\lambda$; reproducing it needs the $O(n)$ dimensions as well.

The fix was to change the invariant rather than the code: $\dim\nu(B_f(n))$ carries the same content and equals $\sum_\lambda(\dim\Delta_\lambda)^2$ by semisimplicity plus the double centraliser, with no $O(n)$ dimensions anywhere.

**The lesson worth keeping:** *a failing assert in a freshly written check is evidence about the check at least as often as about the claim.* The failure here pointed at the theorem and the fault was in the predicted number.

**Found on the way, and it outranks the theorem:** [Rui's criterion](references/andersen-stroppel-tubbenhauer-brauer-semisimplicity/notes.md), $B_f(n)$ semisimple over a characteristic-zero field iff $n \ge f-1$, is the **binding threshold of the whole route**, reading $n \ge 11$ at $f = 12$. The record had carried only the Lehrer–Zhang slack ($r = 6 \le n$, six dimensions). The real margin is **one**.

## 2026-08-31, step 8 chooses the Peirce route, and Gate 2 refutes the cycle's own closure of it

**Step 8 ran on Fable at the user's election.** The outward sweep found the field empty of the missing coupling, the 2025–26 second-kind literature is global Bochner work throughout, and [Bettiol–Kummer–Mendes](references/bettiol-kummer-mendes-2021-convex-curvature/README.md) confirms route A's closure ambiently, curvature-operator conditions escaping exact semidefinite description already at $n\ge5$. Three sources filed. What the sweep actually turned up was **inside [references/](references/)**: Krasnov–Tkachev's Prop 6.7, transcribed cycles ago, flagged in its own notes as machinery the project had never used, and never used.

**The grading was wrong, and the reason generalises.** Route P was graded *attackable $3$, untried here* while [fence-posts.md](findings/fence-posts.md) already carried a closure of the fusion rule, as **prose**, under the name of the tool, rather than as a numbered post. A fence-post *table* scan missed it and an outward literature search could not see it. *Step 1's "search the record" gate never fires on a route chosen at step 8, because by the time an item reaches step 1 the route is the plan's chosen direction and the search runs on the item's sub-objects instead.* The skill now requires grepping the findings by the route's own mechanism at the moment it is proposed, and numbering every proven negative.

**What the cycle derived, and it survived Gate 2 intact.** The exact jet of a cubic at a critical point of its restriction to the sphere, and the orbit identity $B(X^2\!\cdot\!W)=(X\!\cdot\!W)\circ(X\!\cdot\!W)$ obtained by differentiating equivariance twice, which makes the fusion rule and the fourth-order inequality *identities* along the orbit tangent, with no maximality hypothesis anywhere. Both reviewers derived it independently, and r287 supplied the sharper reason: the orbit corrector is the **stationary point** of the concave quartic functional, so stationarity rather than maximality is what forces the supremum to $0$. *The cycle's own argument, "local maximality caps the sup at 0", bounds the supremum from below only, and was insufficient as written.*

**What Gate 2 refuted was the cycle's conclusion.** Excess was $0$ at all six symmetric test points, and that was read as closing route P. It closes nothing: excess is $\dim A(\tfrac12)$ minus the orbit tangent, the orbit tangent is largest exactly where isotropy is smallest, and every test point was a maximally symmetric homogeneous model. A non-graded maximiser has *less* symmetry, hence *more* excess for the same $A(\tfrac12)$, **the instrument could only ever have returned "vacuous" at the points where it was computable.** Both reviewers reached this independently. *This is the record's own most expensive recurring error, committed again: a structural claim read off the symmetric points is a claim about their symmetry.* Route P is re-scoped rather than closed, and the live question is now sharp, does a non-graded maximiser have positive excess?

**A contradiction the record had carried as unresolved is closed on the way.** The fusion rule does not "track primitivity": it is the third-order maximality condition, and its failure at $S^3\times S^3$ says exactly that $S^3\times S^3$ is not a local maximum, consistent with $\lambda_{\max}=\tfrac12$ there, since second order is degenerate and third order decides. Both reviewers refuted the point directly from the definition, exhibiting an ascending curve while $\min\operatorname{spec}(\tfrac\theta2-L_W)=-9.5\times10^{-16}$. **The calculus is strictly stronger than the second-order tool where both are computable.** That $S^3\times S^3$ is where it bites is forced: it is the unique degenerate sphere product.

**A number that reached the brief and was wrong.** The reported supremum $1.653$ at $S^3\times S^3$ was a sampled maximum of a *constrained surrogate*, the projection deleted precisely the $\ker B$ component that makes the true supremum $+\infty$. Both reviewers independently reached $1.7129$ by ascent for the surrogate, and both noted the real answer is infinite. The script was corrected mid-review to report $\max\lvert T(z,z,z)\rvert$ and the $\ker B$ component instead.

**The second falsifier, F2, produced a derivation rather than a verdict.** Both curvature operators carry the *same* sectional curvatures on their diagonals in any frame, so Schur–Horn couples the two spectra, the third piece of information [post F33](findings/fence-posts.md) demands. Majorization alone is inert on $p_3$ ($t^3$ is neither convex nor concave); the support bounds repair it, and the resulting bound has slack in closed form, $\tfrac92M_+\lVert M_{\mathrm{off}}\rVert^2+\tfrac32m\lVert\mathring W_{\mathrm{off}}\rVert^2$, **exactly the off-diagonal mass**. It is therefore sharp on the diagonal family, where the conjecture is already granted, and loses $\approx3.2\times$ at padded $W_{\mathbb{CP}^2}$, where half the Frobenius mass of both operators is off-diagonal at every $n$. Gate 2 owed; recorded as a measurement.

**And the first version of that falsifier measured my own basis choice.** It reported the bound overshooting by $2.9\times$ *at the sphere products*, where it is in fact exactly tight, the loss was entirely an arbitrary completion of the $\psi_k$ block, the one piece of basis freedom left once the $\varphi_{ij}$ are fixed. Caught by the screen that reproduces the record's own $\theta$, plus asking what the residual freedom was. A route-closing negative was one step from the record on the strength of it.

## 2026-08-31, a reviewer's refutation was applied unvalidated, and half of it is inverted

**Reviewer 287's structural argument against the vacuity inference does not stand, and its own table refutes it.** It reasons that excess $=\dim A(\tfrac12)-\dim(\text{orbit tangent})$ is unfindable at the tested points because "the orbit tangent is large precisely when the isotropy group is small, i.e. at the *most* symmetric points", and that a non-graded maximiser, "having less symmetry, hence a *smaller* orbit tangent", carries more excess. **Both halves run backwards.** Most symmetric means *large* isotropy and therefore a *small* orbit; smaller isotropy gives a *larger* orbit tangent, $\tfrac{n(n-1)}2=66$ at trivial isotropy against $36$ at $S^6\times S^6$, which makes excess strictly *harder* to carry. And the single row in the reviewer's own table that has excess is $S^3\times S^3$, isotropy $6$ of $15$: among the **most** symmetric points tested, not the least.

**The verdict it supported survives anyway, on the other reviewer's reasoning.** Excess $=0$ *is* Morse–Bott nondegeneracy, which the record already proved at all six points, so the measurement re-derived a known theorem and says nothing about a *degenerate* maximiser, and nothing excludes a maximiser from being degenerate. That alone is enough to refuse the closure of route P, so the conclusion in the record is unchanged; the reason under it is now correct.

**What let it through is the shape the skill warns about.** A refutation arrives feeling like the humble reading, and this one was folded into four files and a commit before being checked, against the rule that a filed verdict is evidence rather than authority, and that refutations carry the *heavier* burden because nobody reopens a closed route. It was caught only when the next item's grading rationale, inherited verbatim from the reviewer, made a prediction that contradicted the same table it came from. *The arithmetic that settles it is one line and was available the whole time.*

## F4's diagonal half: the symmetry defect written out on the diagonal locus, and the near-miss that preceded it

**What was taken.** V1 is gated on F4, the falsifier hunt on $\{$critical, $S=0$, $\Delta>0\}$, so the cycle took F4. The plan asks for a numerical search; the first move was instead to ask what $\Delta$ *is* on the half of that set where everything is explicit.

**What came out.** On the diagonal locus the Petersen–Wink density collapses to $g_{ab}=2\lVert M_a-M_b\rVert^2-4M_{ab}^2$, so $\Delta=0$ says exactly that every positive edge joins twins, the components of the positive graph are twin cliques and every entry across them is nonpositive. Criticality then cancels both quadratic terms and leaves $g_{ab}=2(s_a+s_b)-4\theta M_{ab}$, whose nonnegativity caps every entry of a diagonal critical point by its own two row norms. Traced over the positive eigenspace this reads $\theta\lVert M\rVert_1=\sum_ad_a^+s_a-\tfrac12\Delta$: route R10's conversion of defect into $\theta$ deficit, exact, on that locus. All of it is Lemma L68 in [findings/diagonal-half.md](findings/diagonal-half.md).

**The near-miss, and what caught it.** The coordinate-free lift looked new for about twenty minutes. It was tested first through $\mathrm{Ric}(W^2)$, which is exact at every diagonal critical point, the ungraded $C_5$ blow-up included, so not a symmetry artefact, and fails by $O(1)$ at every $\mathbb{CP}^m$. Replacing the carrier with $\sum_\alpha\lambda_\alpha^2R_{\gamma\alpha}$ restored it at every $\mathbb{CP}^m$ and at odd $n$, under random rotations inside degenerate eigenspaces, and it failed on non-critical controls exactly as it should. **That general identity is already in [findings/bounds.md](findings/bounds.md), written in the same symbols**, together with the observation that bounding its $Q_\gamma$ term is the transportation class Reviewers 67/68 ceilinged. It was found by grepping the record for the mechanism rather than for the name, before anything was written up as new. What survives as possibly unrecorded is one step: $Q_\gamma=2(W^\#)_{\gamma\gamma}$ per row, which at a critical point pins $Q_\gamma$ exactly instead of relaxing it into that class, the record's "criticality contributes nothing" is scoped to two contractions and not to this. Gate 2 owed.

**The falsifier hunt itself.** Solving the $n\times n$ criticality equation from triangle-free seed graphs, cycle blow-ups, Petersen, Grötzsch, circulants, random maximal triangle-free, reproduces the recorded ceiling $0.670820$ exactly at $n=10$ from independent seeds, and reproduces the recorded $0.173439$ at $n=12$. At $n=12$ it also turns up a critical point at $\theta=0.716134$ with $\Delta=16.3998$ and twelve distinct rows, above the recorded ceiling and still a factor $1.71$ below $\sqrt{3/2}$. **V1 is not falsified on this half**, and its measured margin there is now larger than the plan recorded.

**What the cycle learned about V1's statement.** V1 drops the non-diagonality hypothesis that the live target carries, which widens it onto the diagonal locus, where the conjecture is granted. Post F22 says why the hypothesis was dropped: diagonality is decided by $\ker\Phi_W$, which carries no information about $\theta$. So the widening is deliberate and its cost is now measured rather than assumed: the diagonal half is capped at $0.716134$ in everything searched, and its structure is Lemma L68.

## I19 opens on the non-diagonal half and the margin collapses at once

**Where the target's remaining half lives.** The live target's $\Delta>0$ part had a measured ceiling of $0.670820$ (the $C_5$ blow-up) and then $0.716134$ (a diagonal $n=12$ point found earlier the same day), both diagonal, and the plan graded route R10 on a margin of $1.71\times$ to $\sqrt{3/2}$. Both figures were artefacts of never having searched off the diagonal locus.

**The handle that made the non-diagonal search possible.** $S=0$ says $\mathfrak m$ is totally isotropic for the Cartan 3-form, and at the isotropy cap every such $\mathfrak m$ is $SO(n)$-conjugate to a symmetric pair's, so $\mathfrak{so}(n)=\mathfrak p\oplus\mathfrak m$ is a grading. The block-diagonal Weyl operators for that grading form the fixed-point set of conjugation by $\Lambda^2(\mathrm{diag}(I_p,-I_q))$, so **symmetric criticality applies** and a critical point of $P$ restricted there is critical in $\mathcal W_n$. Measured rather than assumed: the space is $\mathrm{Ad}(s)$-invariant to $10^{-15}$ and the full gradient carries exactly zero mass off it. Dimension $155$ at $n=8$, $395$ at $n=10$, with the sphere product recovered inside to $3\times10^{-15}$.

**Two methods failed before one worked, and the reasons are worth keeping.** Least squares with a numerical Jacobian costs one Jacobian, $155$ to $395$ evaluations of $Q$, per step, so a sweep never finishes; a first attempt burned $100$ minutes of CPU and printed nothing. Power iteration $W\mapsto\Pi(Q(W))/\lVert\cdot\rVert$ costs one evaluation per step and is exact on its control, but converges only to **attracting** fixed points, and $3$ of $40$ starts converged, all to sphere products with $\Delta=0$. A falsifier is a saddle, so that null was uninformative, fence post F13's shape again. What worked is the exact Jacobian $DQ(W)[H]=WH+HW+2\,\mathrm{sharp\_bilin}(W,H)$, with both constants pinned from the definition rather than from a name.

**What it found immediately.** Twelve distinct critical points at $n=8$ from $30$ starts, four of them with $S=0$ and $\Delta>0$, topping out at $\theta=1.088948$, against a previous ceiling of $0.716134$ on that set. Screened: unit norm, full $\mathcal W_n$ residual $5\times10^{-16}$, Ricci, Bianchi and trace all $10^{-16}$, $S_{\mathfrak{mmm}}=1.4\times10^{-28}$, Casimir total exactly $4(n-1)$, trivial kernel, five distinct positive eigenvalues, $\Delta=1.512231$. Two siblings sit at the cap $\dim\mathfrak m=16$.

**Non-diagonality is evidence rather than certificate, and the distinction is load-bearing.** [Lemma L37](findings/target.md)'s frame-independent test returns $\dim\ker\Phi_W=8=n$, exactly the threshold, so it proves nothing either way, the certificate only bites below $n$. The frame minimisation returns $0.373$ against $0.000$ at a diagonal control and $0.837$ at $\mathbb{CP}^4$, which is a global search, so a nonzero value is strong evidence and not a proof.

**What it costs the plan.** The margin to $\sqrt{3/2}$ falls from $1.71\times$ to $1.12\times$, so route R10's two section 1 items regrade from $6$ to $3$: a lossy estimate can no longer win there, and the instruments that are equalities at $\Delta=0$ now have twelve per cent of room rather than seventy-one. The stall trigger does **not** fire, no witness above $\sqrt{3/2}$, but the hunt has moved to $n=10$, where a witness above the threshold would kill the route outright.

**Same day, upgraded: the non-diagonality is certified rather than evidenced.** The Plücker obstruction settles what the other two instruments could not, the witness's two-dimensional eigenspace at $\lambda=-0.302413$ contains no decomposable bivector, $\min\lVert\omega\wedge\omega\rVert=0.5000$, with $\mathbb{CP}^4$ returning $0.5$ and a diagonal control returning $0.0$. A plane meeting the Grassmann cone only at the origin cannot be spanned by coordinate $2$-planes in any frame, so no search is involved. *The lesson is about instrument order*: the frame minimisation and the $\ker\Phi_W$ count were both reached for first and both came back inconclusive, while the certified test was one table row away in [diagonality.md](findings/diagonality.md), which lists exactly which of the three is sufficient and which is a search.

## Four commits mislabelled `derivation`, and the drift the trailer was meant to catch

**What happened.** Working V3 after Gate 2 handed it a mechanism, four consecutive commits carried `Deliverable: derivation`. Only one of them was one, and its derivation was wrong.

| commit | labelled | what it actually was |
|---|---|---|
| the isotypic branching reduction | derivation | genuinely derived, and **false**: $L_e$ is scalar on irreducibles, not isotypes. A reviewer caught it; the numerics that "verified" it did not |
| the closed form $\tfrac{p-2}{2(p-1)}$ | derivation | **fitted from three data points** against a two-parameter guess |
| the mechanism at fixed $\mathfrak p$ | derivation | two points compared. Measurement, `none` |
| the block-graph separation | derivation | about five points measured. Measurement, `none` |

**The test that would have caught each is one line and is in the skill**: *could the reported statement be wrong if the code had a bug?* For three of the four, yes.

**Why the trailer failed.** It is filled in by the same judgement that did the work, at the moment that judgement is most invested. Nothing in the mechanism resists a cycle writing `derivation` because the result *feels* derived, the branching reduction genuinely was derived, and its neighbours inherited the label by association. The drift is not from computing where deriving was possible; it is from computing *after* a derivation, and letting the derivation's label cover the measurements that followed it.

**What survives, restated at its true strength.** The repaired reduction, $L_e$ block-diagonal by isotype, one $m\times m$ block per isotype, is a derivation and stands. The closed form is a fit, and is now labelled one in [findings/bounds.md](findings/bounds.md); what a derivation must explain is its **$q$-independence**, since Ricci-flatness ties the block values as $x=-qz/(p-1)$ so $q$ enters the operator and has to cancel. The mechanism and the separation are measurements over a handful of points and are cited as such.

## 2026-09-01, the R12 cycle: one theorem, ten reviewers, and a vocabulary that did not compose

**What was attempted.** Route R12, the isotype census with a Morse–Bott endgame, chosen by the user at the previous step 8. The cycle worked C1, B1, B3, C3 and C2, and spawned reviewers r305 through r320.

**The one durable result.** [Lemma L69](findings/graded-half.md): for $n\ge12$, every pair-graded critical point with $\theta\ge\sqrt{3/2}$ is a two-factor sphere product with both factors $\ge5$, and each is Morse–Bott nondegenerate. Its new step is analytic and covers every $n$ at once, $\lVert W\rVert^2\le\frac16$ reduces to $\frac1{p-1}+\frac1{q-1}-\frac1{n-1}\le\frac13$, impossible at $p=4$ for every $n$, and at $p=5$ giving $n^2-7n-54\ge0$, i.e. $n\ge12$. **Its cited proof step was wrong**, "an equivariant graded point is the Weyl operator of a compact symmetric space" is nowhere established, and was replaced by a one-dimensional-commutant argument that four reviewers verified and extended to $\mathfrak u(3),\mathfrak u(4),\mathfrak u(5)$.

**What was closed, and the shared reason.** C3 lost four routes: the mass route (post F38), the $\mathfrak p$-internal cross-block (post F39), slice-uniqueness, and the equivariance successor. **All four failed for one reason**, they separate the graded loci using a quantity attached to a *grading*, and those are not functions of the point: a critical point carries several inequivalent gradings, $\lVert A\rVert^2$ spanning $[0.319,0.809]$ across the $n=8$ witness's eight, and the violating direction's block decomposition running $0.17$ to $0.79$. C2's original premise died at the threshold and was repaired twice, but its attack route turned out to be the record's own $\Pi$-bound, closed years back as a tautology.

**Six claims of this cycle's own were withdrawn**, and the pattern in them is worth more than any of them. *The census-dimension argument* used $\theta\le\theta_0$, which is the conjecture. *The nesting* $(C)\subsetneq(A)\subsetneq(B)$ was false at both links. *The $\dim E_+$ bound* was refuted by padding, generically. *The kernel synthesis* restated a definition. *The $\lambda_{\min}$ repair* was a rediscovery. *The rebuttal of r308* rested on a relative-defect test that a control could not fail. **Four of the six were findable by querying the record by number rather than by vocabulary**, which is a rule the record already carries.

**What the cycle bought that was not a correction.** The three senses of "graded", pair, sign, slice, with the witnesses separating them ($\mathbb{CP}^2$ one way, the $n=8$ witness the other) and the labelling pass showing no result is internally mis-stated while the results still do not compose. The $\mathbb Z_2$-grading enumeration with its $n\ne8$, where triality adds $\mathfrak{spin}(7)$ and $\mathfrak{sp}(1)\oplus\mathfrak{sp}(2)$. B1's finding that $H_A$ leaves $\mathcal W_n$, so census values are compression Rayleigh quotients. That the balanced split is the unique symmetric pair admissible in Lemma L23's family, the cap being two inequalities pinching, $(p-q)^2/4$ and $m$. And the diagonal cushion's fitted form $1+\frac1{2(n-3)(n-4)}$, which converges to $1$ and leaves the stronger conjecture sharp, **fitted rather than closed: its source wrote it with a question mark over the equals sign, and Gate 2 ([r677](reviews/REVIEW_r677.md), [r678](reviews/REVIEW_r678.md)) confirms a census bounds the infimum from above only. The minimising family that would let it be derived was lost in the fold-in.**

**Cost.** Ten reviewers, roughly 2.3M subagent tokens, a machine saturated at 1100% CPU for much of the session, one 6.65 GB memory blowout that killed every agent, fourteen immortal wait-loops from a self-matching `pgrep`, and five orphaned workers burning 4.5 cores for up to fifteen hours before being found.

**State at the close.** C2 at grade 3 with two standing repairs and no attack on the complement; C3 at 0 with four closures; B1 and B3 done; F5 and I19 untouched. Three structural debts recorded: results.md is 33 results behind the index, 827 script files are unindexed, and the pre-r287 validation backlog is unenumerated.

## 2026-09-02, R15's opening cycle: the SRG family, closed form, and Lemma L71's first external test

**What was attempted.** I26, R15's first sub-step, chosen by the user from the step-8 sweep. The question: does any strongly regular graph solution of the diagonal criticality equation saturate Lemma L70? Either none does, corroborating [Lemma L71](findings/bounds.md) from outside its proof, or one does and Lemma L71 is false.

**How it went.** Entirely by hand, under the analysis-only rule, with one arithmetic control.

The item's own first move was to pin the normalisation, and that earned its place immediately: [DGK](references/deninger-grundhoefer-kramer-2023-srg-quadratic/notes.md)'s equation is this record's diagonal criticality *verbatim*, with no conversion factor, but DGK impose no norm and this record works at $\lVert W\rVert=1$, so none of their $\theta$ values was quotable and the scale-free ratio had to be built from scratch.

The derivation then went in four steps: the two-eigenvalue ansatz is forced; zero row sums fix $b=-ak/(v-1-k)$; expanding $N^2$ on $\{I,A,J\}$ closes because of the SRG identity; and the edge/non-edge condition reduces to $k(k-\lambda-1)=(v-k-1)\mu$, **the graph identity itself**, so the family is unconditional. That gave [Lemma L74](findings/diagonal-half.md).

**The control worked and was classified honestly.** The octahedron returned $5/\sqrt{60}=0.645497$, which the record already catalogues at $n=6$. Queried by *number* against the value table, per the standing rule, and recorded as **agreement rather than discovery**, an independent route reaching a known point.

**The answer.** Because the solution is diagonal its $\Lambda^2$ eigenvalues are the matrix entries, so $\lambda_{\max}/\lvert\lambda_{\min}\rvert=(v-1-k)/k$, and saturation forces $k=1$, not strongly regular. **No SRG solution saturates, unconditionally in the parameters.** Lemma L71 predicts exactly that, and DGK's family is mostly *not* sphere products, so the test was one the lemma's proof never saw.

**What it cost.** One cycle, no computation beyond arithmetic. The literature did the expensive part: the family, its classification and its existence results were all published, and the record's own step-8 sweep found them only because the search went after citations of a lemma this project had re-derived from scratch.

## 2026-09-02, I26's answer refuted twice and repaired: the saturating SRG members are the balanced sphere products

**What was attempted.** Gate 2 on the entry above, two cold reviewers on identical briefs ([r339](reviews/REVIEW_r339.md), [r340](reviews/REVIEW_r340.md)).

**How it went.** Both refuted the answer, independently, on the same three counts. Saturation of [Lemma L70](findings/bounds.md) needs $\lambda_{\max}/\lvert\lambda_{\min}\rvert=n/(n-2)$, the entry used [Lemma L73](findings/bounds.md)'s $n-2$, a different quantity. Criticality is odd in $M$, so the family carries both signs and the ratio is $w/k$ or $k/w$; the entry read one branch. And "$k=1$ is not strongly regular" concluded nothing, because the branch it came from was the wrong one. Verified by hand before the record was touched.

**The repair is stronger than the withdrawn claim.** Saturation forces $k=v/2$ or $k=(v-2)/2$, so the saturating members are exactly $K_{m,m}=\mathrm{SRG}(2m,m,0,m)$ and $2K_m=\mathrm{SRG}(2m,m-1,m-2,0)$, complements of each other, one point up to sign, with $\theta=\theta_0(2m)$, the balanced sphere product and nothing else, at every even $n$. That is Lemma L71's prediction read off an infinite family its proof never saw. Two by-products: every conference graph gives $\theta=0$ exactly, and the family sits *on* Lemma L73's bound at the cocktail-party graphs.

**A second error caught in passing.** The octahedron had been quoted as $\mathrm{SRG}(6,4,2,3)$; $\mu=4$. The wrong $\mu$ fails the graph identity and survived because $\mu$ cancels out of the edge condition, a parameter a formula does not consume is a parameter no check on that formula can see.

**What it cost.** Two reviewers and the hand verification. The lesson, check a new claim against the record's own theorems, by the quantity's name, before recording it, is filed in [skill-proposals.md](.claude/skill-proposals.md).

## 2026-09-02, I27 worked: the pinned programme at a fixed spectrum, and the two-eigenvalue stratum closed

**What the item asked for and what it produced.** I27 asked whether the fixed-spectrum pinned class collapses to something a human can compute. It does, and the reason is one line of representation theory rather than a solver: $G=S_{m_1}\times\cdots\times S_{m_d}$ permuting indices inside eigenvalue classes leaves the constraint set stable and $\theta$ untouched, the set is convex, so averaging a maximiser over $G$ loses nothing. That is [Lemma L104](findings/bounds-relaxations.md), and the $3N$ equalities become $3d$ in $\binom{d+2}3$ variables, ten at three distinct eigenvalues.

**The rank was the part the derivation could not close, and the reviewers closed it.** Two dependencies exist among the $3d$ equalities and only two, so the rank is $3d-2$ and the feasible set has dimension $\binom{d+2}3-3d+3$. The session's argument that no third dependency exists appealed to r331's completeness theorem and was not a proof; both reviewers supplied one, by the same route independently, the row equations force the multiplier polynomial $\varphi_i$ to factor as $m_i(x-\nu_i)(\beta-\kappa x)$, a two-parameter family.

**And they refuted the clause the session added on top of it.** *"So $\max\theta$ is a genuine maximisation, never forced"* is false in both available ways, both at $d=2$ and both because the variable count is the **admissible** multisets rather than $\binom{d+2}3$: with a class of multiplicity $2$ the type $\{i,i,i\}$ is absent, the feasible set is a point and $\theta$ is forced ($n=8$, multiplicities $(26,2)$); with a class of multiplicity $1$ the system is infeasible at every $n\ge5$, which gives free the corollary that **no Weyl tensor has a two-valued spectrum with a simple eigenvalue**.

**The theorem neither the item nor the brief asked for.** Both reviewers, independently of each other and of anything in the brief, solved the $d=2$ programme in closed form and found that its two upper facets are $t_{112}\ge0$ and $t_{222}\ge0$; the first is the $\Pi$-bound, the second is [Lemma L23](results.md)'s dimension cap $r\le n(n-2)/4$, **obtained from $T\ge0$ together with $t_{112}=0$, and not from $T\ge0$ alone**, as this line said. *Gate 2 on [L105](findings/bounds-relaxations.md): off the locus $\theta=(n-1)w$ the constraint $t_{222}\ge0$ caps $\theta$ rather than $r$, and $r>n(n-2)/4$ stays feasible at smaller $\theta$, $T\ge0$ alone gives only $r\le8$ at $n=6$ against the true $r\le6$.* One rises in $r$, the other falls, and they cross at $r=n(n-2)/4$ with value exactly $\theta_0(n)$. **That closes Conjecture A on the whole two-eigenvalue stratum at every $n\ge5$, with no subalgebra, graded or saturation hypothesis**, [Lemma L105](findings/bounds-relaxations.md). *The session validated it by a third route before recording it: deriving the two branch multipliers as the polynomials $(x-u)(x+w)$ and $(x-u)^2$ that annihilate the other variables, then computing the crossing and the equality case by hand.*

**A session claim refuted by the record it cited.** The session offered a mechanism for r332's observation that the fixed-spectrum LP is exact at catalogued spectra and loose at generic ones: small $d$ makes the feasible segment short. [r342](reviews/REVIEW_r342.md) killed it with the record's own measurement, the $S^3\times S^3$ segment runs $\theta\in[\sqrt{10}/18,\sqrt{10}/3]$, a factor of six, and is exact anyway. The mechanism is **which facet binds**, not how long the segment is, and the corrected statement is in [bounds.md](findings/bounds.md).

**The grading statement I15 wants, proved at $d=2$.** $t_{112}=0$ says $\langle[E_{\max},E_{\max}],E_{\min}\rangle=0$, i.e. $E_{\max}$ is a subalgebra, which is why the $\Pi$-bound saturates on the *whole* subalgebra family, a correction [post F40](findings/fence-posts.md) already carries from an earlier audit and which this facet now explains. The balanced product is the unique point where **both** facets bind, $E_{\max}$ a subalgebra and $E_{\min}$ bracket-orthogonal to itself: the two halves of a symmetric pair.

**A housekeeping lapse that had recurred at scale.** Eleven reviewers, 314, 329–338, including the completeness theorem (331), the hull reading (337) and the $S$-matrix (338), all cited constantly across the record, had **no row in [reviews/INDEX.md](reviews/INDEX.md) at all**, so a reader coming to the index top-down could not see that they existed. Rows added for all eleven with their verdicts. *The skill names this exact failure and it had happened again in the interval since.*

## 2026-09-02, re-filed from bounds.md by the sort

## The product route's status was rewritten three times in one cycle
*From findings/bounds.md. Belongs in ATTEMPTS.md because it records the order in which post F28 was closed, scoped and closed again, and the methodological rule already stated by the skill, rather than any mathematics of the bound.*

*This claim was recorded three times in one cycle, closed, then scoped, then closed again. The first closure was right by accident, the scoping used a step the same review had just named as the weak point, and only the slack identity settles it. The rule the record should carry is the one the skill already states: evaluate a proposed bound at the conjectured extremiser before adopting it, and if it is tight there it is the original problem.*

**The theorem stands and two of its sentences did not.** [DERIVE-sp3](reviews/DERIVE-sp3.md)'s LP half, the $d=3$ feasible set is four-dimensional and compact, so $\theta^\ast$ sits at a vertex with at least four of the ten $t_{ijk}$ zero, was confirmed step by step by both reviewers, each re-deriving it. What failed was written around it: the bracket reading $t_{ijk}=0\iff\langle[E_i,E_j],E_k\rangle=0$ was stated unconditionally when it needs the $t$ to be realisable, and "the maximum of at most $210$ linear solves" omits the feasibility filter, so the unfiltered maximum exceeds $\theta^\ast$ and a fence post read off it would mean nothing. **The unconditional form had already been copied into [plan.md](plan.md)**, which is where it was repaired first.

**The parameter count that motivated the whole item was wrong, and the replacement is better.** The note argued that isolating a type at $d=3$ is nine homogeneous conditions on nine parameters and so generically forces the zero multiplier. That is false as an argument: [Lemma L104](findings/bounds-relaxations.md)'s two dependencies satisfy those conditions identically, so the multiplier image has dimension $3d-2$ rather than $3d$, and the criterion is that every type is isolable exactly when $3d-2=\binom{d+2}3$, true at $d\le2$, false above. [r344](reviews/REVIEW_r344.md) then removed "generically" altogether: a row multiplier is a **line** in the $(X,Y)$ plane, where $P_{jj}$ sits on $Y=X^2$ and $P_{jk}$ is the meet of the tangents at $\nu_j,\nu_k$; a line carries at most $d$ pair-points if tangent and at most two otherwise, while isolation needs $\binom{d+1}2-1$. **So $d=2$'s isolability is the arithmetic accident $3-1=2$**, and the session's own claim that L105's device does not generalise was too strong, annihilating a row's whole support is six conditions on a seven-dimensional space, always solvable, and duality then gives the closed-form $\theta$ per named support.

**The finding that reframes the item is [post F43](findings/INDEX-traps.md), and it is agreement rather than discovery.** [Theorem B of DERIVE-t11](reviews/DERIVE-t11.md) is the *complete* per-row condition at every $d$, and the same file's §5 records its $n=12$ witness passing every row of it at $\theta=1.2917>\theta_0(12)$. Both facts were on the record and neither had been put beside the other: **no per-row inequality can close $d\ge3$**, so the remaining content is cross-row coupling and the vertex route exists for that reason rather than for the parameter count. *A successor naming a new per-row bound has not proposed a route.*

What bites is (B), $t_{133}>0$ when $\nu_2>0$ and $\nu_2+\nu_3>0$, $t_{113}>0$ when $\nu_2<0$ and $\nu_1+\nu_2<0$, each removing $84$, with (C) removing a further $28$ once $\theta>0$. ## 2026-09-02, I14's decomposition, the group that was wrong, and a recorded coincidence explained

**The decomposition holds and the group named for it did not.** The derivation ran the argument on $\Gamma\cap SO(n)$, where $\chi_{[n]}$ is trivial and therefore $\chi_S=\chi_{S^{\mathsf c}}$: complementary blocks carry the *same* character and fuse. With block sizes drawn from $\lvert S\rvert\in\{0,2,4\}$ a fusion needs $n\le8$, and it happens at exactly three dimensions, $n=4$ (a $4$-set with the trivial block), $n=6$ (a $4$-set with a pair block), $n=8$ (two complementary $4$-sets into one block of size four). **Both reviewers found it independently and both gave the same free repair**: $\circ$ is $O(n)$-equivariant, so the full diagonal sign group serves and its even-subset characters are distinct at every $n$. [r345](reviews/REVIEW_r345.md) went further and proved block-diagonality by a support argument on the structure constants, needing no representation theory at all, which is the form now recorded as [Lemma L120](findings/second-order.md).

**The screen sat exactly where the proof failed.** The derivation's character count was verified at $n=4,\dots,8$; $n=6$ is one of the three dimensions where the isotypic claim is false. *A screen that tests totals cannot see a fusion, because fusing two blocks changes no dimension.*

**And the dimension identity was oversold by its own author.** It was written up as the note's real check, on the grounds that the two sides come from unrelated routes. It factors as $\tfrac{n(n-3)}2\big[1+\tfrac{(n-1)(n-2)}6+(n-1)\big]$, tests the three block totals only, is blind to which relation cut each block, and **closes verbatim at $n=4,6,8$ where the structure is wrong**. Recorded as transcription insurance.

**The result the brief did not ask for.** Both reviewers derived the $4$-set block in closed form, independently of each other, and their radicands are algebraically identical: with $A,B,C$ the three opposite-pair sums of the $4$-subset, the block is $\tfrac12G$ with $G\mathbf 1=(A+B+C)\mathbf 1$, so first Bianchi cuts it to $\mathbf 1^\perp$ automatically and it is **traceless**, spectrum $\pm\tfrac12\sqrt{A^2+B^2+C^2-AB-BC-CA}$. [Lemma L24](findings/second-order.md) then gives a necessary condition at every maximiser, one per $4$-subset.

**Half of it is agreement and the classification matters.** At $S^p\times S^q$ only the $(2,2)$-split $4$-subsets are nonzero and the value is $\tfrac{n-2}{2(p-1)(q-1)}$, which is [Lemma L26](findings/nondegeneracy.md), already on the record. What is new is that L26's dangerous summand *is* the $4$-set block, the extension to an arbitrary diagonal $M$, the second eigenvalue, and the per-$4$-subset inequality.

**A coincidence the record had given up on now has a cause.** [second-order.md](findings/second-order.md) reported $\dim E(\tfrac12)=18$ at $S^3\times S^3$ against a nine-dimensional orbit and called the other nine directions *an eigenvalue coincidence with no group origin*. They are the nine $(2,2)$-split $4$-subsets, $\binom32^2=9$ of them, each contributing one $+\tfrac12$ eigenvector, since $\mu=\tfrac2{n-2}=\tfrac12$ at $n=6$. The padding-invariant $\tfrac23$ and $\tfrac35$ at $S^2\times S^4$ and $S^2\times S^6$ are $4$-set eigenvalues too, so their padding-invariance is structural rather than accidental.

**An attribution dispute settled in both directions.** [plan-diagfam](reviews/plan-diagfam.md) filed as a verification-loop candidate the record's attribution of $(p-2)/(2(p-1))$ to the diagonal restriction, a screen having found it in a non-diagonal pair block. Both are right: the value tops each within-factor pair block *and* occurs inside $\mathcal D_n$.

## 2026-09-02, the approved Jacobi run, and the note it refuted was the one that asked for it

**The run was authorised to test a hypothesis and killed the hypothesis's foundation instead.** [DERIVE-sp3b](reviews/DERIVE-sp3b.md) claimed two grading families sit at four-zero vertices of the $d=3$ pinned polytope, and asked whether they were the only Jacobi-consistent supports. The enumeration ([run_jacobi_closure_d3.py](scripts/runs/run_jacobi_closure_d3.py), seconds, approved) returned $121$ of $210$ consistent, and, incidentally, **no full grading among them**. That last line is impossible if a $\mathbb Z_3$-grading were a four-zero vertex, which is how the error was found.

**The error, and it is elementary.** $\langle[X,Y],Z\rangle$ is **totally antisymmetric** on $\mathfrak{so}(n)$, so $T_{abc}$ depends only on the multiset and a type vanishes unless *every* reading permits it. For a $\mathbb Z_m$-grading the invariant form pairs $\mathfrak g_a$ with $\mathfrak g_{-a}$, so the nonvanishing condition is $a+b+c\equiv0\pmod m$, symmetric, as it has to be. **The note used $a+b\equiv c$**, which is not symmetric, and read its whole table off it.

**And the real obstruction is worse than the wrong table.** Over $\mathbb R$ with a positive-definite inner product, a grading needs $2a\equiv0\pmod m$ for every part. At $m=2$ every part qualifies, so a symmetric pair is a genuine real orthogonal grading. At $m=3$ only $a=0$ does: the $\omega$ and $\bar\omega$ eigenspaces of an order-$3$ automorphism are complex conjugates with a **single** real form, so an order-$3$ element of $SO(n)$ gives $\mathfrak{so}(n)=\mathfrak g_0\oplus\mathfrak m$, two real parts and not three. *The Reeder reading that preceded it was fine and its warning, that the $\mathfrak{so}(n)$ statement lives in Levy and Vinberg, still stands; what was wrong was the elementary step after it.*

**What was withdrawn.** The $\mathbb Z_3$ family as a vertex; the six candidate multiplicity triples at $n=12$; and the conclusion drawn from them that [DERIVE-t11](reviews/DERIVE-t11.md)'s witness $(30,20,16)$ is excluded because its multiplicities are distinct. **That exclusion was reported to the user as a result and is now retracted.** The $SO(p)\times U(q)$ centraliser count is correct as complex dimensions and simply says nothing about a real three-eigenvalue spectrum.

**The first negative control tested nothing, and the run said so.** It used $\{111,112,113,122\}$, described as "$E_1$ nearly an ideal", and it passed, correctly, because $E_1$ is an ideal only if five types vanish, which no four-subset can do. The replacement is hand-verified: at $\{111,112,122,123\}$ the table forces $[E_1,E_2]=0$ while requiring $[[E_1,E_1],E_2]\neq0$, a flat contradiction. **The script now refuses to report its enumeration unless both controls behave**, which is the change worth keeping.

**What the $121$ is worth.** The index inclusion is necessary only, so $121$ is an upper bound on the admissible supports; and LP feasibility is a separate filter that has not been applied, so the list is a candidate list rather than an answer. The next cut is the intersection with [r343](reviews/REVIEW_r343.md)'s (B) and (C) sign cuts, which needs no approval.

## 2026-09-02, Gate 2 on the $d=3$ enumeration: the Jacobi filter is not a bound

**Both reviewers refuted the same step, and one produced a counterexample.** The index inclusion the enumeration tests is **strictly stronger** than what Jacobi implies: Jacobi gives a subspace inclusion, while the test compares the two sides' *support upper bounds*, and passing between them needs the left side to attain its bound. [r348](reviews/REVIEW_r348.md) exhibits $\mathfrak{so}(4)=\mathfrak{su}(2)\oplus\mathfrak{su}(2)$ with $E_1=\langle A_1,A_2\rangle$, $E_2=\langle A_3,C_1,C_2\rangle$, $E_3=\langle C_3\rangle$. Jacobi holds identically, the test fails, because $[E_1,E_1]$ is a *proper* subspace of $E_2$ whose bracket with $E_2$ misses $E_3$ although $[E_2,E_2]$ hits it. **So $121$ is a filter's output, not an upper bound on admissible supports.**

**A second frame error, independent of the first.** A vertex has *at least* four active constraints, so its vanishing set may have five or more members, and [Lemma L105](findings/bounds-relaxations.md)'s own $d=2$ optimum is exactly such a degenerate vertex. An enumeration that builds the bracket table from a four-subset and declares it exact cannot see them.

**The emphasis in the note was inverted.** Of the nine row identities, exactly three pass the Jacobi filter, and they are precisely the three with **quadratic** right-hand sides, the six with the clean $\Pi$-bound reading, the only six whose right-hand side was proved nonzero, cut nothing beyond Jacobi. So the $121\to118$ step rested on three conditions never shown nonzero, one of which degenerates at $\theta=0.6335$ at the $n=12$ witness, well inside the $\Pi$-bound $1.4078$.

**Two errors of fact, both mine.** "Three of the nine were already excluded by Jacobi" should read six, $3$ is the count that are Jacobi-*consistent*, hence the count that cut anything; the number $118$ was right and the sentence was not. And "vanishing exactly at $\Pi$-saturation" is false when $\nu_2<0$, where the degeneracy sits at $\theta=(n-1)\lvert\nu_2\rvert$, strictly inside the bound.

**The reviewers differed on one number and a recount settled it.** [r347](reviews/REVIEW_r347.md) kept $110$; [r348](reviews/REVIEW_r348.md) withdrew it to $112$. Recomputing from scratch, six Jacobi-rejected, three Jacobi-consistent, and those three exactly the quadratic ones, **r348 is right**. *The number that matters is neither: it is $179$, the bound the row identities prove without any realisability assumption.*

**And the counting argument for the orbit was wrong.** "$\binom n2$ pair blocks and $\binom n2$ orbit directions, one per block" conflates $\dim\mathfrak{so}(n)$ with the orbit dimension; at $S^3\times S^3$ the isotropy is $\mathfrak{so}(3)\oplus\mathfrak{so}(3)$ and the orbit is $9$-dimensional, so six of fifteen blocks carry none. **The conclusion survives by linearity**, each $[\rho(E_{jk}),M]$ lies in its own block, so the whole orbit lies in their sum whatever the isotropy is, and that argument is stronger than the one it replaces. Corollary kept from [r347](reviews/REVIEW_r347.md): the isotropy algebra of a diagonal critical point is spanned by coordinate rotations.

**What Gate 2 handed back as a positive lead.** $2a\equiv0\pmod m$ means the real orthogonal gradings of $\mathfrak{so}(n)$ are exactly the elementary-abelian-$2$ ones, so $\mathbb Z_2\times\mathbb Z_2$ stays live; its aligned form gives a **six-zero degenerate vertex**, which is the $d=3$ analogue of the balanced product's degeneracy at $d=2$.

## 2026-09-02, the $\mathbb Z_2\times\mathbb Z_2$ vertices, and the witness exclusion withdrawn twice over

**The positive half of the retraction, worked out.** A real orthogonal grading needs $2a\equiv0$ in the grading group, so the real orthogonal gradings of $\mathfrak{so}(n)$ are exactly the elementary-abelian-$2$ ones, which is why $\mathbb Z_3$ failed and $\mathbb Z_2\times\mathbb Z_2$ does not. A pair of commuting involutions splits $\mathbb R^n=V_1\oplus\cdots\oplus V_4$, and the four graded pieces are $\bigoplus_i\mathfrak{so}(V_i)$ together with the three pairings of $\mathrm{Hom}$ spaces, of dimensions $n_1n_2+n_3n_4$, $n_1n_3+n_2n_4$, $n_1n_4+n_2n_3$.

**Six zeros, uniformly.** Merging two of the four pieces to get three eigenspaces can be done six ways, and every one gives exactly six vanishing types, in one of two patterns depending on whether the merged eigenspace contains $\mathfrak g_{00}$. Six against a feasible dimension of four is a **degenerate vertex**, the $d=3$ analogue of the balanced product's degeneracy at $d=2$, and the first such analogue this programme has that survives scrutiny. Read structurally, the first pattern says $E_1\oplus E_2$ and $E_1\oplus E_3$ are both subalgebras.

**It does not shorten the list, and that is now the pattern of the whole item.** At $n=12$ the splittings give $74$ distinct multiplicity triples with every multiplicity at least three. Neither Jacobi nor $\mathbb Z_2\times\mathbb Z_2$ reduces $d=3$ to a handful of named algebras, and the enumeration stays long.

**The retracted exclusion is now wrong twice over.** The withdrawn note argued that [DERIVE-t11](reviews/DERIVE-t11.md)'s witness $(30,20,16)$ was excluded because its three multiplicities are distinct. The *argument* was withdrawn when the $\mathbb Z_3$ table fell; the *conclusion* is withdrawn now, because those multiplicities **are** realised by a $\mathbb Z_2\times\mathbb Z_2$ grading of $\mathfrak{so}(12)$, $V$-dimensions $(0,2,2,8)$ give grade dimensions $(30,16,16,4)$, and merging two pieces reaches $(30,20,16)$; eighteen splittings do it. *This is a statement about multiplicities alone: whether any Weyl tensor carries that spectrum, and whether it is critical, is untouched.*

## 2026-09-02, Gate 2 on I25 and the $\mathbb Z_2\times\mathbb Z_2$ vertices: three refutations, all agreed

**The competitor step was even-$n$ only, and the screen could not see it.** I25 claimed $\theta\ge\theta_0(n)$ at a maximiser because the balanced sphere product is a competitor. **$S^{n/2}\times S^{n/2}$ does not exist at odd $n$**, where the record puts the diagonal maximum at $\Theta_n$, strictly below $\theta_0(n)$, $0.9428$ against $0.9798$ at $n=5$, and [Lemma L71](findings/bounds.md) says no critical point saturates there. [r349](reviews/REVIEW_r349.md) went further: the first inequality *fails* at $S^{(n-1)/2}\times S^{(n+1)/2}$. Substituting $\Theta_n$ repairs everything, and at even $n$, the conjecture's range, nothing changes.

**The screen was vacuous exactly where the claim was false.** It evaluated the closed forms for $m$ and $h$ at $n=5,6,8,12,20,50$ and compared them; at the odd entries those formulas describe **no object**. *This is the second time in one session that a screen was run at dimensions where the structure it was testing does not hold, and the first time the lesson was filed it was about characters coinciding at small $n$. The general shape is the same: a formula evaluates wherever its symbols do, and that is not evidence the thing exists.*

**"Not derived" was wrong twice, and both halves were already on the record.** The counting bound $q\ge1/(m(h+m))$ was dismissed as weaker than $3$; at the balanced product $m(h+m)=4/n^2$ exactly, so it reads $q\ge n^2/4=36$ at $n=12$, the true negative multiplicity, hence **sharp**. And three negatives is proved: [Lemma L35](findings/stratum-two-negative.md) gives $q\le2\Rightarrow\theta\le\sqrt{3/2}$, and $\theta_0(n)^2-\tfrac32=(n^2-12n+8)/(2n^2)>0$ **exactly when $n\ge12$**, the conjecture's own threshold. *The note attacked a route the plan item never took.*

Relation (C) at $a=\arg\min$ makes $\mathbb E_{\mu_a}[\lambda_b\lambda_c]<0$ while $T$'s vanishing on repeated indices keeps the support off $a$, so a second negative index exists.

**Three errors in the $\mathbb Z_2\times\mathbb Z_2$ note.** *(i)* Not every such grading is a splitting: an involution lifts to $g$ with $g^2=\pm I$, and $g^2=-I$ gives the $\mathfrak u(m)$-type, which no splitting reproduces, so the $74$ triples are a **lower** bound and [r349](reviews/REVIEW_r349.md) exhibits two the census misses at $n=12$ itself. *(ii)* **"Degenerate vertex" is refuted**: six conditions on a four-dimensional affine set generically cut the **empty** face, so the count over-determines rather than certifying a vertex, and the $d=3$ analogue of the balanced product's degeneracy is not established. *(iii)* The structural reading was false, the note concluded $E_1\oplus E_2$ and $E_1\oplus E_3$ are subalgebras, but $\{123\}$ is **absent** from the zero set, so $\langle[E_1,E_2],E_3\rangle\ne0$ and $E_1\oplus E_2$ is not closed.

**What survives.** The six-zero count, re-derived by [r350](reviews/REVIEW_r350.md) from the group alone so it covers every grading rather than only the splittings; the witness realisation, **understated** rather than overstated, since the eighteen splittings include six of $\{2,2,4,4\}$ with no empty summand; and I25's two bounds at even $n$, sharp and attained.

**Four further findings from [r349](reviews/REVIEW_r349.md), none of them in [r350](reviews/REVIEW_r350.md), all verified before folding.** *(i)* The odd-$n$ failure is a **counterexample**, not just a broken step: $S^6\times S^7$ at $n=13$ has $m=0.104031297$ against the claimed floor $0.104154339$, and it saturates the $\Pi$-bound, reproducing the record's $\Theta_{13}$ exactly, so the inequality fails identically at every odd $n$. *(ii)* **The sharpness clause was circular.** At even $n=6,8,10$ it is outright false, since $\theta_0(n)<\sqrt{3/2}$ and padded $W_{\mathbb{CP}^2}$ attains that; at even $n\ge12$ attainment would follow only if the balanced product is the maximiser, which is the conjecture. What is proved is that the bound values equal *that point's* own eigenvalues. *(iii)* The $\mathbb Z_2\times\mathbb Z_2$ completeness gap is real at $n=12$ itself: anticommuting quaternionic structures on $\mathbb H^3$ give a grading with dimensions $(21,15,15,15)$, $\mathfrak g_{00}=\mathfrak{sp}(3)$, realised by none of the $27$ splittings, whose merges $(36,15,15)$ and $(30,21,15)$ are absent from the census. *(iv)* The correct structural reading of the six zeros: $E_1$ is the isotropy algebra of a symmetric pair with $\mathfrak m=E_2\oplus E_3$.

**A process fault worth naming: both files under review were edited while the reviewers were working**, folding in the first report before the second landed. The verdicts were formed beforehand so nothing was lost, but a reviewer reading a file that moves under it cannot be relied on to be reviewing what the record will hold. *Fold after both reports are in, not between them.*

## 2026-09-02, the pair block: a closed form verified against its own generating code, and wrong

**The form was wrong by a factor of two and $222$ exact checks did not see it.** In $(M\#X)_{\alpha\beta}=-\tfrac14[\operatorname{tr}(A_\alpha MA_\beta X)+\operatorname{tr}(A_\alpha XA_\beta M)]$ the two traces are equal, so the $-\tfrac14$ collapses to $-\tfrac12$; the recorded entries were the symmetrised half plus exactly half the true sharp half. Both reviewers proved the corrected block from the structure constants independently: $L|_{\{j,k\}}=\tfrac12[\operatorname{diag}(M_{ji}+M_{ki})-M_{jk}\mathrm{Id}+M^{(jk)}]$, needing **diagonality alone**, not criticality, not Ricci-flatness.

**Why the screen was blind.** It compared the formula against *the implementation that produced it*, on **random diagonal matrices that are not Weyl tensors**. Two objects carrying the same convention error agree perfectly; and the one structural test that exposes it, preservation of the Ricci cut, is invisible on inputs that do not satisfy Ricci-flatness. Both reviewers checked against [Q_full](scripts/lib/adversarial_check1.py), the definition of record, at the same $222$ blocks and found the discrepancy at once. *The record's own convention rule says to quote the implementation rather than restate it, and to run both when a report indicts code; the failure here was checking a restatement against itself.*

**The decisive argument is normalisation-free, and the session verified it by hand.** The recorded form has row sums $\tfrac14(M_{ji}+M_{ki}-M_{jk})$, varying with $i$, so $\mathbf 1$ is not an eigenvector and the block does not preserve the Ricci cut, contradicting [Lemma L120](findings/second-order.md). Only the coefficient $\tfrac12$ gives constant row sums $-\tfrac12M_{jk}$. *This needs only Ricci-flatness and no convention at all, which is why it settles the matter rather than the numerics.*

**The $\sigma_i$ were an artefact.** No orientation sign appears in the unsorted basis $f_i=e_{ji}\odot e_{ki}$; the $\sigma_i\sigma_m$ belongs to the sorted basis. Spectrum-neutral, so it costs no result, but the $16\%$ failure that first exposed it was the screening code using sorted bivectors while the text described unsorted ones, and that mismatch went unnoticed because the sign was absorbed as a discovery rather than investigated as a discrepancy.

**What the corrected block turns out to be.** With $\Delta^{(jk)}$ the weighted graph Laplacian of the sectional matrix $M$, rows and columns $j,k$ deleted, $L|_{\{j,k\}}=-\tfrac12\Delta^{(jk)}-\tfrac12M_{jk}\mathrm{Id}$, and the Ricci cut is exactly the Laplacian's own $\mathbf 1^\perp$. So [Lemma L24](findings/second-order.md) on the non-diagonal directions is $\lambda_{\min}(\Delta^{(jk)}|_{\mathbf 1^\perp})\ge-(\theta+M_{jk})$, one condition per pair, **a spectral condition on graph Laplacians of the sectional matrix**, which is a considerably better object than the block it came from.

**An open attribution closes**: $(p-2)/(2(p-1))$ is now proved to top the within-factor pair block, settling the verification-loop candidate. Within-factor blocks at a sphere product carry no orbit direction, since $M_{ji}=M_{ki}$ there, which is why six of the fifteen blocks at $S^3\times S^3$ are orbit-free.

**Containment**: the wrong form never left [reviews/DERIVE-df1.md](reviews/DERIVE-df1.md), and [Lemma L120](findings/second-order.md) and [Lemma L121](findings/second-order.md) are undisturbed.

## 2026-09-02, I12: the right lemma, the wrong theorem, and the correction the plan had already written down

**The character lemma is right and is now [Lemma L123](findings/second-order.md).** Both reviewers re-derived it before reading the note: a zero-diagonal $R$ has no trivial-character component, $\Gamma$ acts on each character space by a scalar so bilinearity alone puts $R_\chi\circ X$ in $\chi\chi_X$, the trace pairing is $\Gamma$-invariant so distinct isotypics are orthogonal, and $\chi\chi_X=\chi_X$ forces $\chi=1$. **It is more general than the use it was found for**, it holds for any single character space, so it also transports [Lemma L122](findings/second-order.md)'s pair block to an arbitrary frame, and it survives a Weyl projection.

**I12 as stated is refuted, and the lemma is not what fails.** [Lemma L24](findings/second-order.md) requires $X\perp W$. Off the eigenframe that hypothesis **fails**, because $W$'s own component lies in the very $4$-set plane the test direction is drawn from: $\langle X,W\rangle=\langle X,R\rangle$, which this session measured at up to $0.243$ and nonzero at all $45$ directions in a rotated frame. The corrected criterion is $\langle X,L_eX\rangle\le\tfrac12(1+c^2)$ with $c=\langle X,W\rangle$, sharp at $X=W$, giving $A^2+B^2+C^2-AB-BC-CA\le\theta^2(1+\rho^2)^2$ with $\sum\rho^2\le1$ across the $\binom n4$ subsets.

**The plan item had the correction and the derivation threw it away.** [plan-maximizer](reviews/plan-maximizer.md)'s I12 route has the projection $N'=N-cW$ as its step 2, and its predicted theorem carries $-\theta c^2/2$ in the numerator and $1-c^2/8$ in the denominator with $c=\langle N,W\rangle$; step 5 names it "the projection correction". The note read that as an unnecessary fudge constant and wrote *"the route's step-5 constant is therefore not needed"*. **It was the missing term.** *A route's own predicted constant is a claim about the mathematics, and discarding one because a cleaner statement is in reach is how a hypothesis goes missing.*

**Two corrections conflated.** The character lemma kills the $L_R$ cross-term; the projection defect is a different correction with a different source. Proving the first and announcing the second discharged is the shape of the error.

**The screen could not have caught it, for two reasons worth separating.** It measured $\langle X,L_RX\rangle$, the quantity that really is zero, and never compared $\Sigma$ with $\theta^2$ in a rotated frame. And at sphere products $c=0$ anyway, so **no sphere-product screen could ever expose this defect**; [r353](reviews/REVIEW_r353.md) supplies a hand witness at $n=4$ where a two-plane rotation makes the $4$-set entry $(\alpha-\gamma)/2\ne0$, noting that single-plane rotations do not produce it.

**Scope corrections banked from the same audit.** [Lemma L121](findings/second-order.md) holds under diagonality alone, verified from the structure constants, the record states it for a diagonal *critical* point, and the wider scope is what lets it apply to $\operatorname{diag}(M)$ off the eigenframe. [Lemma L122](findings/second-order.md)'s bracketed form is diagonality-only too, **but its Laplacian rewriting and the identification of the Ricci cut with $\mathbf 1^\perp$ both need Ricci-flatness**, so the scope line is corrected. And $\operatorname{diag}(M)\in\mathcal W_n$ in every frame, since Ricci-flatness reads $\sum_bM_{ab}=0$ on frame-diagonal entries alone, which puts the whole split inside the Weyl space and supplies exactly the Ricci-flatness L122 needs. **L122's bound is attained** by the orbit direction, so its content is that the orbit minimises the Rayleigh quotient on $\mathbf 1^\perp$, strict only in orbit-free blocks.

## 2026-09-02, a universal quantifier refuted by the record's own relations, and a fence post walked into from the side

**P4 claimed that *any* contraction pairing each structure constant with itself loses Jacobi's content. The counterexamples are relations (B) and (C).** Because $c$ is totally antisymmetric there are no distinguished bracket slots, so every such contraction is $\Sigma_{gd}[x]=\sum_{ab}x_{ab}c_{abg}c_{abd}$: at $x\equiv1$ it is $2(n-2)\delta_{gd}$, at $x_{ab}=\lambda_a$ it is $-2\lambda_g\delta_{gd}$, and at $x_{ab}=\lambda_a\lambda_b$ it is $2(W^\#)_{gd}$, **the backbone of every recorded spectral bound**. Verified here at $S^3\times S^3$: the $\lambda_a\lambda_b$ shadow matches $2(W^\#)_{gg}$ to machine precision, spread $[-0.53,0.47]$, plainly not a multiple of the identity. *Squaring forces the Killing form only in the unweighted case, and the real mechanism is that the Killing collapse returns $2(n-2)$ times the **trace** of whatever it is applied to.*

**And [post F18](findings/bounds-relaxations.md) was scoped for exactly this slip.** Its heading reads *"only the **unweighted** generator sum is inert … the very next weight returns $\theta$ itself"*. This cycle restated the unscoped form from a different direction and did not recognise it. **A fence post that names a trap protects only against the approach it was written for**; the trap here is the unweighted-to-weighted generalisation, and it is worth reading F18 by its mechanism rather than by its subject.

**The phrase used to describe the escape was wrong too.** "Pair across different index slots", but the escape terms displayed alongside it pair over the *same* slots with different third indices. The real distinction is **same-triple versus different-triple**.

**What survives is PLAUSIBLE and unproved.** Two repairs are on offer: by Schur only an ad-invariant weight forces the Killing form, and a same-triple pairing returns a marginal of $T$, hence a definition rather than a constraint. Neither is proved, so **I15 is not settled**, and the [r331](reviews/REVIEW_r331.md) citation over-claimed, r331 proves completeness at *linear order in $T$* and says so.

**The vacuity check was vacuous.** The contraction collapses because relation (A) is $g$-independent, and what emerges is $\operatorname{tr}(W^\#)=-\lVert W\rVert^2$, which follows from (B) at **every** Weyl tensor. So the four sphere-product checks could not have failed whatever the claim was, the third such screen this session that could not have detected its own error.

**Post F44 is scoped rather than withdrawn, and the correct statement is sharper.** $R$ reaches a single-character criterion through two channels the first version missed: the bound is $\kappa=\theta/2$ and $\theta$ depends on all of $W$, and **which directions are admissible is $R$'s doing** since $\langle X,W\rangle=\langle X,R\rangle$ off the eigenframe. *The first version conceded the second channel two paragraphs below its own box.* The replacement, proved and screened: **$L_{\operatorname{diag}(M)}$ is exactly the character-block-diagonal part of $L_W$ and $L_R$ exactly the off-block part**, so $R$ is off-block, not invisible. And the blindness is **per-frame**: the sectional function $\{\operatorname{diag}(M_F)\}$ over all frames determines $W$, so "mix characters or leave Rayleigh quotients" omitted a third route, **vary the frame**, which is what I12 does.

**Two citation defects repaired**: the convention line was attributed to [conventions.md](findings/conventions.md), which carries no such statement, it lives in [adversarial_check1.py](scripts/lib/adversarial_check1.py); and I15 cited F44 for a question about the signs of $c$ in the spectral eigenframe, conflating that with a coordinate frame's off-diagonal part.
