## 2026-09-02, the forbidding criterion is nonvanishing, not sign; three counts fell to one error

**The root defect was conceptual and it produced three wrong numbers in a row.** The forbidding argument is: if every surviving type vanishes the left side is zero, so the right side must vanish, hence a **nonzero** right-hand side forbids the type-set. [DERIVE-sp3c](reviews/DERIVE-sp3c.md) states that in as many words. **Every classification this section made tested positivity instead.** So $2\nu_2[(n-1)\nu_1+\theta]$ was filed under "needs the sign of $\nu_2$" when it is hypothesis-free: the bracket is a sum of positives and $\nu_2\ne0$ by kernel-freeness. *The three figures the record carried for the free count, $192$, $201$, $195$, are one error counted three times.*

**The corrected structure is simpler than the wrong one.** Both families' right-hand sides factor as (a nonzero eigenvalue) $\times$ (a bracket), and **the bracket $(n-1)\nu_j+\theta$ depends only on $j$ while the factor $\nu_i$ never obstructs**: $j=1$ is always nonzero, $j=3$ vanishes exactly at $\Pi$-saturation, $j=2$ is the only unresolved one. Hypothesis-free chain $210\to209\to208\to201\to\mathbf{194}$, both reviewers independently from the definitions. *An independent recount here reached $192$ by a branching route and is unreconciled; the classification, not either number, is what carries.*

**The branch was unnecessary.** Either $(n-1)\nu_2+\theta>0$ and the $j=2$ identities apply, or it is $\le0$, which **forces** $\nu_2<0$ and $\theta\le(n-1)\lvert\nu_2\rvert<(n-1)\lvert\nu_3\rvert$, i.e. $\Pi$ strict, so the $j=3$ identities apply instead. Three identities either way, **no hypothesis on $\nu_2$ anywhere**. The whole of the step is $\lvert\nu_2\rvert<\lvert\nu_3\rvert$ for $\nu_3<\nu_2<0$.

**And "second-$\Pi$-strictness" was a name doing work its object could not.** It is unnecessary given the dichotomy, and insufficient, it permits $\theta<(n-1)\lvert\nu_2\rvert$, where the pair cut reverses, and never reaches the double-root identity at row $2$ root $1$, so the branches do not agree under it. **[Lemma L71](findings/bounds.md) characterises saturation of [Lemma L70](findings/bounds.md), not of the $\Pi$-bound**, and [Lemma L107](findings/bounds.md)'s derivation has no analogue at the middle eigenvalue. There is no second $\Pi$-bound. *[conventions.md](findings/conventions.md) carries the rule that a quantity's name is not its definition; this section coined a name and reasoned from it, which is that rule's exact failure mode.* The $\nu_2<0$ branch costs four identities, not one.

**Two further rows withdrawn.** The $\nu_2>0$ figure is $178$–$179$, not $173$, only four identities are bought by the sign, not nine. And **$130$ is unreachable**: all eighteen identities taken nonzero floor at $141$, so that row drew on Jacobi or the pair cuts without saying so.

## The eighteen identities were nine short, and the floor they gave was not a floor

**Two cold reviewers on identical briefs, [r363](reviews/REVIEW_r363.md) and [r364](reviews/REVIEW_r364.md), refuted the exhaustion claim by the same mechanism, found separately.** The entry above records "$130$ is unreachable, all eighteen identities flooring at $141$"; both halves fall.

**What they saw that the derivation did not.** A row multiplier is an affine $\ell(X,Y)$ against six pair-points, $P_{jj}=(\nu_j,\nu_j^2)$ on the parabola, $P_{jk}=(\tfrac{\nu_j+\nu_k}2,\nu_j\nu_k)$ below it, annihilating exactly the types on its line, with right-hand side $(n-2)\ell(R_i)$ at the row point. Counting two-point lines is then a two-line argument: $\binom62=15$, the three tangents carry three points each and consume $9$, **six remain**. Three are the recorded chords $\{P_{aa},P_{bb}\}$; three are secants $\{P_{aa},P_{bc}\}$ that were never listed. **Nine per row, $27$ in all.**

**The arithmetic was right and the family was wrong.** Dropping the nine omitted secants from r363's recount returns exactly $141$, so nothing was miscomputed, and the derivation had simply not enumerated its own apparatus. *The exhaustion was argued from spanning, and spanning proves too much: it would make the two-root family redundant, which the record denies by using it.*

**What replaced the count.** [r364](reviews/REVIEW_r364.md) supplied a union bound needing no enumeration at all, a tangent forbids a three-subset lying in $7$ four-subsets, a two-point line forbids one, so at most $9\times7+18=81$ of $210$ die and at least $129$ survive. r363's exact figure is $132$. **Non-closure of the per-row method at $d=3$ is now an argument rather than a count**, which is what the entry above was reaching for.

**Two things the round found that were on the record already.** The complete per-row condition is $R_i\in\operatorname{conv}(\text{used points})$, [Theorem B of DERIVE-t11](reviews/DERIVE-t11.md) restated, so the annihilation identities are its affine shadow and F45's successor bar sat at the wrong place. And the **pair cap** $\sum_cT_{abc}\le2$ is a proved per-row constraint of no multiplier form, recorded two sections above the post that said none exists.

**And "grant every right-hand side nonzero" was not the strongest form of the method.** With $T\ge0$ the coefficients may be mixed in sign, and then a nonzero right-hand side forbids a *pair* ($28$ four-subsets) or a *singleton* ($84$) rather than a four-subset. [Lemma L104](findings/bounds-relaxations.md)'s duality paragraph states the certificate as coefficients $\le0$, not $=0$; the derivation instrumented the annihilation subfamily and called it the method.

**Validation before folding**: the line count was rebuilt here by hand from the plane geometry, $15$ two-point lines, $3$ tangents at three points each, six remaining, independently of either reviewer's route, and checked at $\nu=(2,1,-3)$ where $\varphi=(3x-1)(x-2)$ annihilates exactly $\{i11\}$ and $\{i23\}$.

## The four-set equality at padded CP-2: one derivation, refuted, and two lemmas out of the wreckage

**The debt.** [I12](plan.md) recorded $\Sigma=\theta^2$ at padded $\mathbb{CP}^2$ as a *screen* that could not be cited, and asked for the closed form.

**First attempt, and it was wrong.** Deriving the $\mathbb{CP}^2$ curvature by hand at holomorphic sectional curvature $4$ gives sectional matrix entries $(2,2,-1,-1,-1,-1)$, opposite-pair sums $(A,B,C)=(4,-2,-2)$, $\Sigma=36$ and $\lVert W\rVert^2=24$, hence $\Sigma/\lVert W\rVert^2=3/2$. From this the note concluded $\Sigma=\tfrac32\rho^2$ at every half-flat four-set, and drew three consequences: the equality as a *collision* of independent facts, a *concentration cap* on how much norm a four-set may carry, and a relocation of [I12](plan.md)'s slack from the frame budget $t_F$ to $\rho$.

**All four fell at Gate 2**, [r365](reviews/REVIEW_r365.md) and [r366](reviews/REVIEW_r366.md) agreeing on every verdict. The core error is a **category error**: the note cited [Lemma L121](findings/second-order.md), which is about $L_M$ on $\mathrm{Sym}^2(\Lambda^2)$, for an invariant plane of $W$ on $\Lambda^2$. Computing directly, $A,B,C$ are the **diagonal entries** of the self-dual block, not its eigenvalues, so the true relation is $\Sigma\le\tfrac32\rho^2$, the wrong direction for everything downstream.

> **ONE LINE KILLS IT AND NEEDS NO COMPUTATION.** $\Sigma$ is **frame-dependent**; $\rho^2$ and half-flatness are **frame-invariant**. No identity between them can hold under invariant hypotheses. *The witness is the record's own object: padded $\mathbb{CP}^2$ rotated inside the four-set stays critical at $\theta=\sqrt{3/2}$, stays half-flat, keeps $\rho^2=1$, and has $\Sigma=0.656$ against a predicted $1.5$.* **The frame-invariance test is the screen that was owed and not run.**

**Two lemmas survive, and both are better than what was claimed.** *(a)* [Lemma L124](findings/second-order.md)(iii): on the half-flat single-four-set family $P$ is an $SO(3)$-invariant cubic on traceless symmetric $3\times3$, hence $\theta=9\det V_+$, and the sharp determinant bound gives $\theta^2\le\Sigma$ with equality **exactly** at $\pm W_{\mathbb{CP}^2}$, a rigidity, where the note had claimed a coincidence. *(b)* [Lemma L125](findings/second-order.md): the second-order condition off $W^\perp$, $L_e\le\tfrac12(\mathrm{Id}+W\otimes W)$ with equality along $W$, which the record had carried only as a quotation of [Krasnov–Tkachev](references/krasnov-tkachev-2018-idempotent-variety/notes.md) Proposition 6.6 and used only in its $W^\perp$ restriction.

**And they do not compose**, which is [post F46](findings/INDEX-traps.md): $\theta^2\le\Sigma\le\theta^2(1+c^2)^2$ with $c\le1$ reads $\theta^2\le\Sigma\le4\theta^2$, admitting every member of the family. *At padded $\mathbb{CP}^2$ the top eigenvector is $W$'s own block component, so $c=1$ exactly, which is why the uncorrected $\Sigma\le\theta^2$ looked sharp there while never being derivable, and it is the same $X\perp W$ hypothesis [I12](plan.md) was reopened for once already.*

### I18(c) opened: the four-set half of the block criterion, and the factor of two it is short

*2026-09-02, route [R16](routes.md), while Gate 2 on [Lemma L128](findings/second-order.md) runs. Analysis only; nothing here was computed.*

**What I18(c) has to prove.** At a pure critical point with $\theta>\sqrt{3/2}$ and $n\ge12$, every four-set block of $L_e$ is $<\tfrac12$. By [Lemma L121](findings/second-order.md) the block's eigenvalues are $\pm\tfrac{\sqrt\Sigma}{2\theta}$ with $\Sigma=A^2+B^2+C^2-AB-BC-CA$ in the opposite-pair sums, so the statement is **$\Sigma<\theta^2$ at every four-subset**.

**At a maximiser it is already there, non-strictly.** [Lemma L121](findings/second-order.md)'s consequence, [Lemma L24](findings/second-order.md) applied to the block, is exactly $\Sigma\le\theta^2$. So the work is entirely at **critical points that are not maximisers**, which is what I18 must cover, and the missing word is *strict*.

**The crude bound and its size.** $\Sigma\le\tfrac32(A^2+B^2+C^2)$ always, with equality iff $A+B+C=0$; and $A^2\le2(M_{ij}^2+M_{kl}^2)$ entrywise, so $\Sigma\le3\sum_{\text{6 entries}}M^2\le3\lVert W\rVert^2=3$. Against the target $\Sigma<\theta^2$ with $\theta^2>\tfrac32$, **this is short by a factor of two**, and it used neither the zero row sums nor criticality, only $\lVert W\rVert=1$.

**So the shape of the derivation is fixed.** A factor-two improvement is available in principle from three unused facts: the row sums $\sum_bM_{ab}=0$ (Ricci-flatness), which forbids a four-subset from carrying the whole norm; criticality, which the crude chain never touches; and the hypothesis $\theta>\sqrt{3/2}$ itself, which forces mass **away** from any single four-subset through the value. *The first is the one to try first: $\Sigma$ is a variance-like form in $A,B,C$, and zero row sums bound how much of $\lVert W\rVert^2$ any six entries can hold.*

**And the failure mode is a fence post rather than a gap.** A pure critical point with $\theta>\sqrt{3/2}$ and a four-set at exactly $\Sigma=\theta^2$ is degenerate by [Lemma L128](findings/second-order.md)(ii), so it is the branch point the whole route is looking for, it would close I18 as stated and open a named object.

**Corrected at Gate 2 the same day** ([r373](reviews/REVIEW_r373.md), [r374](reviews/REVIEW_r374.md), agreeing): the four-set target is $\Sigma\ne\theta^2$, not $\Sigma<\theta^2$, a block **above** $\tfrac12$ leaves the point nondegenerate, and $S^2\times S^4$ is the witness, so the factor of two above is a bound on the wrong quantity. What the crude estimate does still show is that no norm-only argument separates $\Sigma$ from $\theta^2$, since it does not even reach the strict inequality. **And the item is one clause short**: $\mathcal D_n\cap W^\perp$ must also avoid $\tfrac12$, which is the diagonal problem's second-order condition and is untouched by the four-set and pair calculus.


### I18(c)+(d) on the band: the perturbation route closes a finite range of $n$ and cannot close them all

*2026-09-02, route [R16](routes.md), after [Lemma L128](findings/second-order.md) passed Gate 2. Analysis only; the three numbers below are arithmetic in $n$, not a computation.*

**The band, which neither sub-step was written with.** [Lemma L57](findings/problem.md) bounds $\langle Q(W),W\rangle\le\Theta_n\lVert W\rVert^3$ on the **whole** diagonal locus, with equality exactly at the balanced product. So every pure critical point has $\theta\le\Theta_n$, and [I18](plan.md)'s domain is the closed band
$$\sqrt{3/2}\;\le\;\theta\;\le\;\Theta_n,\qquad \Theta_{12}=\tfrac{\sqrt{55}}6=1.2360,\quad\sqrt{3/2}=1.2247,$$
of width $0.0113$ at $n=12$. *A pure critical point above the threshold is pinned within one percent of the balanced product's value.*

**So the obvious derivation is a perturbation off $S^m\times S^m$, and its three ingredients are all in hand.** The blocks of [Lemma L121](findings/second-order.md) and [Lemma L122](findings/second-order.md) are **linear** in the sectional matrix $M$ and divided by $\theta$, so their eigenvalues are Lipschitz in $M$ with an absolute constant; [Corollary L128.1](findings/second-order.md) gives the block values at the balanced product; and a quantitative [Lemma L57](findings/problem.md), a deficit inequality $\theta\le\Theta_n-c_n\,d^2$ in the distance $d$ to the balanced orbit inside $\mathcal D_n$, would confine the band to a $d$-neighbourhood. Then $\tfrac12$ stays off the spectrum wherever $C\,d/\theta$ is below the margin.

**And that is where it dies, for a reason worth recording as the route's own constraint.** The margins at the balanced product are not uniform in $n$:

| block family | value at $S^m\times S^m$ | margin below $\tfrac12$ | as $n=2m\to\infty$ |
|---|---|---|---|
| four-set, $(2,2)$-split | $\mu=\tfrac1{m-1}$ | $\tfrac12-\tfrac1{m-1}$ | $\to\tfrac12$, **widens** |
| pair, within-factor | $\tfrac{m-2}{2(m-1)}$ | $\tfrac1{2(m-1)}$ | $\to0$ like $1/n$ |

**The binding margin decays like $1/n$ while the band widens to a constant**, *and the margin is **tied**, not owned by the pair block: [Lemma L121](findings/second-order.md) puts the same $(p-2)/(2(p-1))$ inside $\mathcal D_n$ as well ([r375](reviews/REVIEW_r375.md), [r376](reviews/REVIEW_r376.md)), and with the deficit constant bounded from the same block the window closes like $n^{3/2}$ rather than $n$*, $\Theta_n\to\sqrt2$, so the band $[\sqrt{3/2},\Theta_n]$ tends to width $0.189$. The two move against each other, so a perturbation argument off the balanced product has a window that closes: it can settle a **finite range** of $n$, and it cannot settle them all. *The defensible form of the structural fact, [r375](reviews/REVIEW_r375.md) having refused the stronger one: **the Hessian gap closes like $1/n$ on order $n^2$ directions** at the balanced product. It is never attained at finite $m$, so the maximiser is nondegenerate at every $n$ and calling it a branch point overstates it.*

**Two Gate 2 caveats on the closure itself, one of them a disagreement between the reviewers.** *(a)* "Provably not enough" is stronger than the argument: converting a **value** gap into an $M$-**distance** needs a quantitative [Lemma L57](findings/problem.md) with the deficit constant $c_n$ bounded below. [r376](reviews/REVIEW_r376.md) says no such bound exists on the record, so the closure is conditional on it; [r375](reviews/REVIEW_r375.md) says the bound follows from the same block, $c_n\lesssim3\Theta_n/(2(m-1))$, making the confinement radius grow like $\sqrt n$ and the window close like $n^{3/2}$ rather than $n$, *which would strengthen the conclusion*. **Exactly one of these is right and settling it is the next question on this line**, not an inconvenience. *(b)* At **odd** $n$ the perturbation base is the unbalanced product $S^{(n-1)/2}\times S^{(n+1)/2}$, whose margin is $1/(n-3)$, a case the table above does not cover, and the route needs odd $n$ ([r376](reviews/REVIEW_r376.md); $\Theta_{13}=1.2484>\Theta_{12}$, so the odd band is wider).

**What a successor must therefore have.** An argument whose margin does not decay in $n$, so not a perturbation off the balanced product, and not anything Lipschitz in $M$ against a $1/n$ margin. The candidates left are the two levers the crude bound never used: the zero row sums, and criticality read on the band rather than at a point. **The band itself survives as the item's real gain**: [I18](plan.md) is a statement about points within $O(1/n^0)$… within $\Theta_n-\sqrt{3/2}$ in value of the granted maximiser, which is a far smaller set than "every pure critical point".

### I18's pair clause restated: it is strictness in [Lemma L122](findings/second-order.md)'s own inequality

*2026-09-02, immediately after the band finding above. Analysis only.*

**The restatement.** [Lemma L122](findings/second-order.md) gives the pair block as $-\tfrac12\Delta^{(jk)}-\tfrac12M_{jk}\mathrm{Id}$, so $\tfrac12$ is an $L_e$-eigenvalue of that block exactly when $-(\theta+M_{jk})$ is an eigenvalue of $\Delta^{(jk)}|_{\mathbf1^\perp}$. The same lemma already records the inequality
$$\lambda_{\min}\big(\Delta^{(jk)}|_{\mathbf1^\perp}\big)\ \ge\ -\big(\theta+M_{jk}\big)$$
at every maximiser, **with equality along the orbit**. So [I18](plan.md)'s pair clause is not a new bound at all: **it is the statement that L122's inequality is STRICT in every orbit-free pair block.** *A statement about the equality case of a recorded inequality is a different kind of target from a bound, and it is the kind this record has closed before.*

**And the Laplacian is genuine, by the row sums.** Zero row sums give $M_{ji}+M_{ki}=-\sum_{l\notin\{j,k\}}M_{il}$, so $\Delta^{(jk)}=\operatorname{diag}\big(\text{row sums of }M^{(jk)}\big)-M^{(jk)}$ is the weighted graph Laplacian of $M^{(jk)}$ on $n-2$ vertices, *which is precisely why [Lemma L122](findings/second-order.md)'s scope note says the Laplacian form needs Ricci-flatness, and it is the first place the zero row sums do real work in this route.* The weights are signed, so $\Delta^{(jk)}\succeq0$ is unavailable and the negative entries of $M$ carry the whole question.

**What to derive next, in one line.** Characterise when $\lambda_{\min}(\Delta^{(jk)}|_{\mathbf1^\perp})=-(\theta+M_{jk})$, an equality case in a signed-weight Laplacian on $n-2$ vertices whose weights are one deleted-two-rows submatrix of a hollow zero-row-sum $M$ with $\theta$ in the band. **The orbit-free hypothesis enters as $M_{ji}\ne M_{ki}$ failing for some $i$**, since $o^{jk}_i=M_{ki}-M_{ji}$ is the equality vector when it is nonzero.

**First attempt on the pair clause, and the exact size of its failure.** The clause needs $\lambda_{\min}(\Delta^{(jk)}|_{\mathbf1^\perp})>-(\theta+M_{jk})$ in every orbit-free block, at a **critical point** rather than a maximiser, so [Lemma L122](findings/second-order.md)'s recorded inequality, which is [Lemma L24](findings/second-order.md) and therefore needs maximality, is unavailable and only its equality *shape* transfers. Gershgorin on $\Delta=\operatorname{diag}(N\mathbf1)-N$, $N=M^{(jk)}$, gives $\lambda\ge\Sigma_lN_{il}-\Sigma_l|N_{il}|=-2s_i$ with $s_i$ the negative mass of row $i$ of $N$; the zero row sums make the negative mass of a row of $M$ exactly $\tfrac12\lVert M_i\rVert_1$, so a sufficient condition is
$$\lVert M_i\rVert_1\;<\;\theta+M_{jk}\qquad\text{for every }i .$$
**It SUCCEEDS at the balanced product, and fails inside the band at $S^5\times S^7$.** *Gate 2, [r375](reviews/REVIEW_r375.md) and [r376](reviews/REVIEW_r376.md), agreeing: the first version of this paragraph compared $\lVert M_i\rVert_1$ against $\theta$ alone, **dropping the $M_{jk}$ its own condition carries**, and asserted a failure that is not there.* The signs are geometry rather than convention: $\theta>0$ forces $\gamma<0$, so the **within-factor entry $\alpha=-m\gamma/(m-1)$ is positive** and $M_{jk}=\alpha$ in an orbit-free block. At $S^m\times S^m$ the condition reads
$$2m\lvert\gamma\rvert\;<\;(2m-1)\lvert\gamma\rvert+\tfrac m{m-1}\lvert\gamma\rvert\iff m-1<m,$$
**true at every $m$**, with margin $\lvert\gamma\rvert/(m-1)$, $12<12.2$ at $m=6$. **The fence post is at the unbalanced split**: at $S^5\times S^7$, $n=12$, Gershgorin gives $14\lvert\gamma\rvert$ against $12.75\lvert\gamma\rvert$ and fails, and that point sits **inside the band** at $\theta=1.2283$ ([r375](reviews/REVIEW_r375.md)). *So the row-sum lever is not uniformly short; it is short exactly where the split is uneven, which is where the negative mass concentrates in one factor.*

### The pair clause as a Dirichlet-form inequality on a signed graph, with criticality now in play

*2026-09-02. Analysis only; the arithmetic below is by hand in $m$.*

**The clause in its working form.** With $N=M^{(jk)}$ and the Laplacian identity $x^\top\Delta x=\tfrac12\sum_{i,l}N_{il}(x_i-x_l)^2$, the pair clause at $\{j,k\}$ reads
$$\tfrac12\sum_{i,l\notin\{j,k\}}M_{il}\,(x_i-x_l)^2\;>\;-(\theta+M_{jk})\,\lVert x\rVert^2\qquad\text{for every }x\perp\mathbf1,\ x\ne0,$$
**strictly, except along the orbit vector $o_i=M_{ki}-M_{ji}$ where equality is forced.** *Gate 2 splits that sentence in two ([r375](reviews/REVIEW_r375.md), [r376](reviews/REVIEW_r376.md)): the **eigenvector** half is unconditional, $\Delta^{(jk)}o=-(\theta+M_{jk})o$ at every diagonal critical point, criticality and zero row sums alone, while the **inequality** half is [Lemma L24](findings/second-order.md) and needs maximality, so off a maximiser the orbit need not be the minimiser at all. **The open statement is exactly that the orbit eigenvalue is the bottom of the spectrum at a non-maximal critical point.*** So the object is a signed-weight Dirichlet form: the negative entries of $M$ are the entire difficulty, and the zero row sums fix their total mass per row at $\tfrac12\lVert M_i\rVert_1$.

**The lever not yet used.** Diagonal criticality is $M_{ij}^2+(M^2)_{ij}=\theta M_{ij}$ off the diagonal, i.e.
$$\sum_l M_{il}M_{lj}\;=\;\theta M_{ij}-M_{ij}^2\qquad(i\ne j),$$
which controls exactly the *products* of entries the Dirichlet form's cross terms produce, and which neither the Gershgorin attempt nor the band argument touched. **It is the only recorded constraint that relates different rows of $M$**, and the pair clause is a two-row statement, so it is the right shape.

**Hand check of the whole chain at $S^m\times S^m$, which confirms the recorded margin from a different direction.** Within-factor entries $\alpha=-m\gamma/(m-1)$, cross entries $\gamma$, $\theta=(2m-1)\gamma$. For a within-factor pair $\{j,k\}$ the block's top $L_e$-eigenvalue $(m-2)/(2(m-1))$ forces
$$\lambda_{\min}\big(\Delta^{(jk)}|_{\mathbf1^\perp}\big)=-\alpha-\theta\tfrac{m-2}{m-1}=\gamma\,\frac{-2m^2+6m-2}{m-1},$$
which at $m=6$ is $10\gamma=-10\lvert\gamma\rvert$ against $-(\theta+\alpha)=12.2\gamma=-12.2\lvert\gamma\rvert$, **strict, with slack $2.2\lvert\gamma\rvert$**, and the slack divided by $2\theta$ is $0.1=\tfrac1{2(m-1)}$, the recorded margin. *The first version of this line wrote $\theta=(2m-1)\gamma$ with $\gamma>0$ and printed $-7.6\gamma$ against $-9.8\gamma$; with the record's own sign, $\theta=-(n-1)\gamma$ and $\gamma<0$, both values shift by $2\alpha$ and the check reverses as literally written, **corrected at Gate 2 by [r375](reviews/REVIEW_r375.md) and [r376](reviews/REVIEW_r376.md) independently.** The slack and the margin are unaffected.* **And it is one route, not three**: $\text{slack}/(2\theta)=\tfrac12-\lambda_{\max}$ is an identity and $\lambda_{\min}$ was read off $\lambda_{\max}$. [r375](reviews/REVIEW_r375.md) supplies the genuinely independent check, direct diagonalisation of $\Delta^{(jk)}$ by its three equitable-partition eigenvector types, and it agrees.

**One clause of the restatement is now stronger than it was written.** [r376](reviews/REVIEW_r376.md) derives $\Delta^{(jk)}o=-(\theta+M_{jk})o$ with $o_i=M_{ki}-M_{ji}$ at **every** diagonal critical point, from criticality and the zero row sums alone, with $\sum_io_i=0$ automatic, **no maximality**. So the orbit vector is an exact eigenvector wherever [I18](plan.md) needs it, and what still requires maximality is only the *inequality* $\lambda_{\min}\ge-(\theta+M_{jk})$, i.e. the claim that this eigenvalue is the bottom. **That is the precise open statement of the pair clause.**

### The reviewers' disagreement dissolves: both are right, and together they close the perturbation route unconditionally

*2026-09-02, I18's next sub-step as [r375](reviews/REVIEW_r375.md) and [r376](reviews/REVIEW_r376.md) left it. Analysis only; the argument is two lines of second-order calculus.*

**The two positions are about opposite ends of the same constant, so they never contradicted each other.** A quantitative [Lemma L57](findings/problem.md) would read $\theta\le\Theta_n-c_n d^2$ in the distance $d$ to the balanced orbit inside $\mathcal D_n$. **Using** it needs a **lower** bound on $c_n$, which is [r376](reviews/REVIEW_r376.md)'s point: the record has none, so the confinement step cannot even be set up. **Bounding** it is what [r375](reviews/REVIEW_r375.md) does, and the direction is the other one:

**Any admissible $c_n$ is at most $3\Theta_n/\big(2(m-1)\big)$.** Along the least-negative direction of $\mathrm{Hess}(P|_{S\cap\mathcal D_n})$ at the balanced product the actual value drop is $\tfrac12\lvert\lambda\rvert d^2+O(d^3)$ with $\lvert\lambda\rvert=6\theta(\tfrac12-\lambda_m)=3\theta/(m-1)$, so a global inequality with constant $c_n$ forces $c_nd^2\le\tfrac12\lvert\lambda\rvert d^2$ as $d\to0$. **This is an upper bound on every constant that could ever work, and it holds whether or not the quantitative lemma is ever proved.**

**So the closure is unconditional.** Feed it back: the confinement radius is
$$d\ \gtrsim\ \sqrt{\frac{\Theta_n-\sqrt{3/2}}{c_n}}\ \gtrsim\ \sqrt{\frac{0.189\cdot2(m-1)}{3\sqrt2}}\ \sim\ \sqrt m,$$
which **grows**, while the margin the perturbation must respect decays like $1/(2(m-1))$. The block eigenvalues are Lipschitz in $M$ with an absolute constant, so the requirement is $C\,d\lesssim\theta/(2(m-1))$, asking $\sqrt m\lesssim1/m$. **The window closes like $m^{3/2}$ and the perturbation route off the balanced product is dead at every large $n$, with no quantitative L57 needed to say so.** *The same $S^2_0(\mathbb R^m)$ summand inside $\mathcal D_n$ supplies both ends: it caps $c_n$ and it ties the margin.*

**What survives, and it is the item's remaining content.** The band is untouched, [Corollary L128.1](findings/second-order.md) is untouched, and [I18](plan.md)'s open statement is the one Gate 2 sharpened: *at a non-maximal pure critical point in the band, is the orbit eigenvalue $-(\theta+M_{jk})$ the bottom of $\Delta^{(jk)}|_{\mathbf1^\perp}$?* The orbit eigenvector relation is unconditional; only its minimality is open, and it must be attacked from criticality rather than from proximity to the balanced product.

### The pair clause as one PSD matrix, with three exact vectors from criticality

*2026-09-02, I18's open statement attacked from criticality as Gate 2 directed. Analysis only; every line is hand algebra and each is checked against the record's own normalisation.*

**Setup.** Fix a pure critical point $M$ and a pair $\{j,k\}$; let $I=[n]\setminus\{j,k\}$, $N=M^{(jk)}$, and write $u_i=M_{ij}$, $v_i=M_{ik}$ for $i\in I$. Zero row sums give $(N\mathbf1)_i=-u_i-v_i$, so
$$\boxed{\,B:=\Delta^{(jk)}+(\theta+M_{jk})\mathrm{Id}=(\theta+M_{jk})\mathrm{Id}-\operatorname{diag}(u+v)-N\,}$$
and the pair block of $L_e$ is $\tfrac12\mathrm{Id}-\tfrac1{2\theta}B$. **So the clause "$\tfrac12$ is not an eigenvalue off the orbit" is exactly "$\ker B=\mathbb R o$", and the maximiser inequality is "$B\succeq0$".** *One symmetric $(n-2)\times(n-2)$ matrix, and the whole pair half of [I18](plan.md) is a statement about it.*

**Three exact vectors, none needing maximality.**

> **(1) $B\mathbf1=(\theta+M_{jk})\mathbf1$.** Immediate from the row sums: $B_{ii}+\sum_{l\ne i}B_{il}=\theta+M_{jk}-u_i-v_i+(u_i+v_i)$. **So $\mathbf1$ is an eigenvector with a positive eigenvalue whenever $\theta+M_{jk}>0$, and $B\succeq0$ on $\mathbf1^\perp$ is then equivalent to $B\succeq0$ outright**, the Ricci cut costs nothing here.
>
> **(2) $Bu=Bv=M_{jk}(u+v)-u\circ v$**, where $\circ$ is entrywise. *Proof.* Criticality $\sum_lM_{il}M_{lj}=\theta M_{ij}-M_{ij}^2$ splits over $l\in I$, $l=j$, $l=k$ into $(Nu)_i=\theta u_i-u_i^2-M_{jk}v_i$; substituting into $Bu=(\theta+M_{jk})u-(u+v)\circ u-Nu$ cancels $\theta u$ and $u\circ u$ and leaves $M_{jk}(u+v)-u\circ v$. The $k$-version is the same computation with $j\leftrightarrow k$, and $M_{kj}=M_{jk}$. $\square$
>
> **(3) $B(u-v)=0$**, subtract (2) from itself. Since $o=v-u$, this **re-derives [r376](reviews/REVIEW_r376.md)'s unconditional orbit relation** by a second route, and shows it is the antisymmetric half of a single identity whose symmetric half, $B(u+v)=2\big[M_{jk}(u+v)-u\circ v\big]$, is new here.

> **A FOURTH IDENTITY, CONTRIBUTED BY [r378](reviews/REVIEW_r378.md) AND ON NO PART OF THE RECORD.** Criticality read at the entry $(j,k)$ itself, the one row the compression discards, gives $(M^2)_{jk}=u\!\cdot\!v$ by hollowness, hence
> $$M_{jk}^2-\theta M_{jk}+u\!\cdot\!v=0 .$$
> It is the missing consistency link between $M_{jk}$ and $(u,v)$, it yields $\theta+M_{jk}>0$ whenever $u\!\cdot\!v>-2\theta^2$, **the hypothesis (1) needs and which the section had left implicit**, and it cross-validates (1) and (2), since $\mathbf1^\top Bu$ computed two ways agrees exactly when it holds.

**Two corrections from the same audit.** The clause is $\ker B\cap\mathbf1^\perp=\mathbb Ro$ rather than $\ker B=\mathbb Ro$; and "$B\succeq0$ on $\mathbf1^\perp$ iff $B\succeq0$" is conditional on $\theta+M_{jk}>0$, now derivable from the boxed identity. **Five hypotheses were used silently and are now stated** ([r378](reviews/REVIEW_r378.md)): the $L_e=L_M/\theta$ rescaling, $\theta+M_{jk}>0$, $\theta+M_{jk}\ne0$, Ricci-flatness, and connectedness of $\operatorname{supp}(M)$. **Scope confirmed where it matters**: the positivity $M^2-\theta M\succeq0$ needs criticality alone and holds at **non-maximal** critical points, which is the only regime this item lives in, though the record's *strictness* data is sphere-products only, and strictness is what [I18](plan.md) needs.

**What this changes about the item.** The pair clause is no longer a spectral estimate to be fought for: it is **$\ker B=\mathbb R o$ for an explicit $B$ whose action on $\mathbf1,u,v$ criticality already fixes**. The remaining question is whether $B$ has a second kernel vector, and the natural next move is to ask what $B$ does on $\{\mathbf1,u,v\}^\perp$. **The band enters only if positivity fails**: a pair block above $\tfrac12$ means $B\not\succeq0$, which is possible at a non-maximal critical point, $S^2\times S^4$ already shows a *four-set* block above $\tfrac12$, so $\theta\ge\sqrt{3/2}$ is the hypothesis that must rule it out for pair blocks, and it has not been used yet.

### The band's first real lever: the deleted submatrix has at most two eigenvalues in $(0,\theta)$

*2026-09-02, continuing [I18](plan.md)'s pair clause. Analysis only. **Screened first, and the screen fired**: the identity below and its positivity are on record.*

**What the screen returned.** Rearranging diagonal criticality gives $M^2-\theta M=\Delta_{M^{\circ2}}$, the graph Laplacian of the **Hadamard square**, whose weights are squares and therefore nonnegative, so $M^2-\theta M\succeq0$ with kernel the constant vectors of the $M^{\circ2}$-graph's components, and the spectrum of $M$ avoids the open interval $(0,\theta)$. **[diagonal-half.md](findings/diagonal-half.md) already carries all of it**: the identity $M^{\circ2}+M^2=\theta M+\operatorname{diag}(s_i)$, the statement $K^2-\lambda K\succeq0$ **as a property of diagonal critical points** (refuted as a property of the locus, Reviewer 129, with a hand-built $n=8$ witness whose eigenvalue $4\delta$ sits inside $(0,\theta)$), the kernel-per-component reading, and the connectivity table. *Recorded here as a confirmation reached by a different route, rearranging to a Laplacian rather than proving positivity directly, and claiming nothing new.*

**The step, and Gate 2 moved which part of it is new** ([r377](reviews/REVIEW_r377.md), [r378](reviews/REVIEW_r378.md), agreeing). Compress to $I=[n]\setminus\{j,k\}$ with $\Pi$ the coordinate projection. Since $(M^2)_{il}=(N^2)_{il}+u_iu_l+v_iv_l$ for $i,l\in I$,
$$\Pi\big(M^2-\theta M\big)\Pi\;=\;N^2-\theta N+uu^\top+vv^\top\;\succeq\;0,$$
a compression of a PSD matrix. **So $N^2-\theta N$ is bounded below by minus a rank-two form, and therefore has at most two negative eigenvalues:**

> **At every pure critical point and every pair $\{j,k\}$, at most two eigenvalues of $N=M^{(jk)}$ lie in the open interval $(0,\theta)$**, **and in an ORBIT-FREE block, where $u=v$, at most ONE**, since the correction $uu^\top+vv^\top$ then has rank one. *That refinement and the per-eigenvector inequality are what is new; the count of two is [Cauchy interlacing](findings/diagonal-half.md) at codimension two on the recorded gap and needs no compression at all, [diagonal-half.md](findings/diagonal-half.md) states "$K$ has no eigenvalue in $(0,\lambda)$" in the very file this section cites for its confirmation half.* **The orbit-free case is exactly the one [I18](plan.md) is about**, and [r377](reviews/REVIEW_r377.md) shows the bound of one is attained.

> **THE GENUINELY NEW CONTENT IS PER-EIGENVECTOR, NOT THE COUNT** ([r378](reviews/REVIEW_r378.md)). For every unit eigenvector $w$ of $N$ with eigenvalue $\nu$,
> $$\nu(\nu-\theta)+(u\!\cdot\!w)^2+(v\!\cdot\!w)^2\;\ge\;0 ,$$
> so an eigenvalue inside $(0,\theta)$ **must** have a nonzero projection on $\operatorname{span}\{u,v\}$, transversality, $S\cap\operatorname{span}\{u,v\}^\perp=\{0\}$, and that is what kills the containment clause below. **This inequality is the headline the section should have carried.**

> **AND THE EXCEPTIONAL DIRECTIONS ARE NOT CONFINED TO $\operatorname{span}\{u,v\}$, that clause is withdrawn.** *Both reviewers refuted it with hand witnesses, [r377](reviews/REVIEW_r377.md) at $S^3\times S^4$ and [r378](reviews/REVIEW_r378.md) at $S^6\times S^6$.* The rank argument gives a **nonzero projection** onto $\operatorname{span}\{u,v\}$, never membership, and that span is not $N$-invariant, $Nu$ carries $u\circ u$. At $S^3\times S^4$ with $c=-1$ the eigenvector in $(0,\theta)$ is $(-1,1,1,1,1)$ against $u=v=(2,-1,-1,-1,-1)$: not parallel.

**Why this is the lever the item was missing.** Every earlier attempt bounded $B=\Delta^{(jk)}+(\theta+M_{jk})\mathrm{Id}$ through row masses. Gershgorin, the $\ell^1$ condition, the perturbation radius, and each lost the same factor because a row mass sees no cancellation. **This is a spectral constraint on $N$ itself**, it costs nothing, and it comes from the one equation the route had not spent. *What it does not yet give is $B\succeq0$: $B$ carries $\operatorname{diag}(u+v)$, which the compression does not control.* **[r378](reviews/REVIEW_r378.md) states the obstruction structurally, which is sharper**: $B\succeq0$ is a **ceiling** on $\lambda_{\max}$, while everything criticality supplies is a statement about a **gap**, a spectrum avoiding $(0,\theta)$ constrains nothing above $\theta$.

### Why no criticality consequence can close the pair clause, made precise, and two free identities on the way

*2026-09-02, taking [r378](reviews/REVIEW_r378.md)'s structural point as the next question. Analysis only.*

**Two identities that cost nothing and were not written down.** From $M\mathbf1=0$ in block form $M=\begin{psmallmatrix}N&U\\U^\top&C\end{psmallmatrix}$ with $U=[u\ v]$ and $C$ off-diagonal $M_{jk}$:
$$\textstyle\sum_iu_i=\sum_iv_i=-M_{jk},\qquad \widetilde N:=N+\operatorname{diag}(u+v)=-\Delta^{(jk)}\ \text{ has }\ \widetilde N\mathbf1=0 .$$
*The first pins the total of $u$ against $M_{jk}$ and pairs with [r378](reviews/REVIEW_r378.md)'s $M_{jk}^2-\theta M_{jk}+u\!\cdot\!v=0$: one relation on $\sum u_i$, one on $u\!\cdot\!v$.* **And free from the recorded gap:** $\operatorname{tr}M=0$ with $M\ne0$ forces $\lambda_{\max}(M)>0$, so the gap gives $\lambda_{\max}(M)\ge\theta$, while $\lVert M\rVert_F=\sqrt2$ gives $\lambda_{\max}(M)\le\sqrt2$, hence **$\theta\le\sqrt2$ at every pure critical point**, the asymptote of $\Theta_n$, by two lines and no fourth-moment argument. *Weaker than [Lemma L57](findings/problem.md) at every finite $n$, and recorded because it is free and because it shows where $\sqrt2$ comes from.*

**The obstruction, quantified.** The clause is $\lambda_{\max}(\widetilde N)\le\theta+M_{jk}$. The only ceiling available from the gap is $\lambda_{\max}(\widetilde N)\le\lambda_{\max}(N)+\max_i(u_i+v_i)\le\lambda_{\max}(M)+\max_i(u_i+v_i)$, and at $S^m\times S^m$ on a within-factor pair that reads
$$2m\lvert\gamma\rvert+\tfrac{2m}{m-1}\lvert\gamma\rvert\;\le\;(2m-1)\lvert\gamma\rvert+\tfrac m{m-1}\lvert\gamma\rvert\iff \tfrac{2m-1}{m-1}\lvert\gamma\rvert\le0,$$
**false by a constant $\approx2\lvert\gamma\rvert$, worse than the Gershgorin attempt**, because the two maxima are attained on different vectors, $\lambda_{\max}(N)$ on the block direction and $\max_i(u_i+v_i)$ on a coordinate.

**So [r378](reviews/REVIEW_r378.md)'s reading is confirmed by a second route and should be treated as a fence for this item.** Every consequence of criticality on the record is a **floor**, the gap $\operatorname{spec}(M)\cap(0,\theta)=\varnothing$, the per-eigenvector inequality, the compression, and $B\succeq0$ is a **ceiling**. *A floor on a spectrum bounds nothing above it.* **This fence is OVERSTATED and is corrected at Gate 2**: [r379](reviews/REVIEW_r379.md) exhibits a ceiling-shaped criticality consequence, in the band, $M$ has **exactly one positive eigenvalue**, since $p\theta^2\le\lVert M\rVert_F^2=2$ bounds the count $p$ of eigenvalues $\ge\theta$. *So criticality does produce ceilings; what it has not produced is a ceiling on the compressed $\widetilde N$.* **What must therefore enter is the band $\theta\ge\sqrt{3/2}$**, which is the item's one unspent hypothesis and, unlike criticality, is an *upper*-bound statement in disguise: through [Lemma L57](findings/problem.md) it says the point is within $\Theta_n-\sqrt{3/2}$ of the balanced product **in value**, which caps how large any single block can be. **That is the shape the next attempt must have, and it is the reason the value hypothesis cannot be dropped.**

### Spending the band by ascent: what a violation implies, and why the argument must be local

*2026-09-02, the shape [r378](reviews/REVIEW_r378.md)'s fence calls for. Analysis only.*

**The variational reading of a violation.** Suppose a pure critical point $W$ with $\theta\ge\sqrt{3/2}$ has a pair block carrying an $L_e$-eigenvalue above $\tfrac12$ on some $x\perp\mathbf1$ off the orbit. Since $\mathrm{Hess}(P|_S)_W=6\theta(L_e-\tfrac12\mathrm{Id})$ ([Lemma L24](findings/second-order.md)), $P$ **increases** along $x$, and $x$ lies in $V_{jk}$, a **non-diagonal** direction. Ascent from $W$ therefore leaves the diagonal locus and terminates at a critical point $W'$ with $P(W')>\theta\ge\sqrt{3/2}$.

> **THE CLAIM "UNCONDITIONALLY TRUE AT $\theta=\Theta_n$" IS WITHDRAWN. IT IS CIRCULAR.** *Both reviewers, independently ([r379](reviews/REVIEW_r379.md), [r380](reviews/REVIEW_r380.md)).* The deduction is *(clause fails) $\Rightarrow$ (live target false)*, i.e. it proves the clause **from** the live target, which is open; and even granting the target, $S(W')=0$ is not established for the ascent's endpoint, so the witness would not lie in the class the target quantifies over. **Nothing is lost**: by [Lemma L57](findings/problem.md)'s equality case the points attaining $\Theta_n$ are exactly the balanced products, where [Corollary L128.1](findings/second-order.md) proves the clause outright. *Two further wording repairs from the same audit: $\operatorname{grad}P(W)=0$, so there is no ascent **from** $W$, the argument needs a perturbed start in the positive-Hessian direction; and convergence to a critical point is Łojasiewicz on a real-analytic compact manifold, which the section used without citing.*

**At the top of the band the conditional version closes, and it is the only place it does.** If $\theta=\Theta_n$ then $P(W')>\Theta_n$, and [Lemma L57](findings/problem.md) forbids that for any diagonal point, so $W'$ is **non-diagonal with value above $\Theta_n>\sqrt{3/2}$**, which refutes the record's live target. *So, **granting the live target**, the pair clause holds at every pure critical point attaining $\Theta_n$*, a conditional superseded by [Corollary L128.1](findings/second-order.md) proving it there by block arithmetic.

**Strictly inside the band it does not close, and the reason is worth recording as a fence.** For $\theta<\Theta_n$ the ascent's endpoint $W'$ may be **diagonal** with $\theta<P(W')\le\Theta_n$, and nothing is contradicted. **A variational argument therefore cannot deliver the pair clause on the open band**, it converts a block violation into the existence of a higher-value critical point, which the diagonal theorem permits until the value reaches $\Theta_n$. *The gap the argument leaves is exactly the band's own width, $\Theta_n-\sqrt{3/2}$, which is $0.0113$ at $n=12$ and $0.189$ asymptotically, the same width that closed the perturbation route, arrived at from the opposite direction.*

**So the attempt must be local at $W$, and the band must enter as a bound on $M$ rather than through the value.** The one route left of that shape: [Lemma L57](findings/problem.md)'s proof passes through the fourth moment $\sum_i(\text{row data})^4$, so $\theta\ge\sqrt{3/2}$ constrains $M$'s moments directly, and a moment bound is a **ceiling** on $\lambda_{\max}(\widetilde N)$ of the kind the criticality floors cannot supply. **That is [I18](plan.md)'s next sub-step, and it is the first one whose input has the right direction.**

### A ceiling that works: the trace–Frobenius bound on $\widetilde N$, with every ingredient exact

*2026-09-02, [I18](plan.md)'s pair clause. Analysis only; the two evaluations below are hand arithmetic in $m$.*

**Both moments of $\widetilde N$ are exactly computable, which is why a moment ceiling is available at all.** With $\lVert M\rVert_F^2=2$ split over the blocks of $M=\begin{psmallmatrix}N&U\\U^\top&C\end{psmallmatrix}$, and using $\sum_iu_i=\sum_iv_i=-M_{jk}$:
$$\operatorname{tr}\widetilde N=\sum_i(u_i+v_i)=-2M_{jk},\qquad \lVert\widetilde N\rVert_F^2=2-\lVert o\rVert^2-2M_{jk}^2,\qquad o=v-u .$$
*The Frobenius identity is exact and pleasingly clean: **the orbit vector's length is the only thing the pair block's total mass loses**, beyond the $(j,k)$ entry itself.*

**The Frobenius ceiling alone fails, and by little.** $\lambda_{\max}(\widetilde N)\le\lVert\widetilde N\rVert_F$ gives, in an orbit-free block ($o=0$) after substituting [r378](reviews/REVIEW_r378.md)'s $\theta M_{jk}=M_{jk}^2+u\!\cdot\!v$, the sufficient condition $\theta^2+5M_{jk}^2+2\lVert u\rVert^2\ge2$. At $S^6\times S^6$ it reads $1.5278+0.3879=1.9157$ against $2$, **short by $0.084$**, four percent.

**The trace–Frobenius ceiling succeeds there.** For a symmetric $T$ of size $d$ with $\operatorname{tr}T=t$ and $\lVert T\rVert_F^2=f$, $\lambda_{\max}(T)\le\tfrac td+\sqrt{\tfrac{d-1}d\big(f-\tfrac{t^2}d\big)}$ (Wolkowicz–Styan). With $d=n-2$, $t=-2M_{jk}$, $f=2-\lVert o\rVert^2-2M_{jk}^2$ this is a **closed-form ceiling in $(\theta,M_{jk},\lVert o\rVert,n)$ alone**, and the pair clause follows from
$$-\frac{2M_{jk}}{n-2}+\sqrt{\frac{n-3}{n-2}\Big(2-\lVert o\rVert^2-2M_{jk}^2-\frac{4M_{jk}^2}{n-2}\Big)}\;\le\;\theta+M_{jk}. \tag{$\dagger$}$$
**At $S^6\times S^6$, $n=12$**: $\gamma^2=5/396$, $M_{jk}=\alpha=0.134831$, $t=-0.269663$, $f=1.963642$, $d=10$, giving $\lambda_{\max}\le1.29996$ against $\theta+M_{jk}=1.236033+0.134831=1.370864$. **Clears, with slack $0.0709$.** *And asymptotically it clears too*: $t\to0$, $f\to2$, so the left side tends to $\sqrt2\sqrt{1-1/(n-2)}<\sqrt2\le\theta+M_{jk}$ in the limit, with margin of order $1/n$.

> **GATE 2: THE CEILING'S HEADLINE DOES NOT SURVIVE.** *[r379](reviews/REVIEW_r379.md) and [r380](reviews/REVIEW_r380.md), agreeing; the moment identities and the $S^6\times S^6$ arithmetic are confirmed exactly, and everything else about the bound's strength is corrected downward.*
>
> **(i) The asymptotic clause is false as argued and weak as corrected.** Its chain passes through $\sqrt2\le\theta+M_{jk}$, which fails at **every** $S^m\times S^m$ and is forbidden by the record's own $\theta\le\sqrt2$ unless $M_{jk}\ge\sqrt2-\theta$, the bound the section admits it lacks. The true margin is $\approx7.78/n^2$, **not order $1/n$**.
>
> **(ii) The bound spends nearly all the slack there is.** [r380](reviews/REVIEW_r380.md) took the exact spectrum, which this section never did: at a within-factor pair of $S^m\times S^m$, $\operatorname{spec}\widetilde N=\{\alpha^{(m-3)},(2\gamma-\alpha)^{(m-1)},0,-2(m-1)\gamma\}$ and **the true slack is exactly $\theta/(m-1)$**, $0.2472$ at $m=6$, against which the ceiling's $0.0709$ means it spends **$71.3\%$**, rising to $95.5\%$ at $n=64$ and $99.87\%$ at $n=2048$.
>
> > **(ii-b) And $\lVert o\rVert$ was never uncontrolled**, [Lemma L68](findings/diagonal-half.md) pins it, $\lVert o^{jk}\rVert^2=s_j+s_k-2\theta M_{jk}$, so an orbit-free (twin) pair has $s_j=s_k=\theta M_{jk}$ ([r379](reviews/REVIEW_r379.md)). *A quantity the section treated as a free variable had a closed form on the record.*
>
> **(iii) The falsifier the brief asked for exists.** $(n,\theta,M_{jk},\lVert o\rVert)=(12,\ 1.236033,\ 0.05,\ 0)$ satisfies the band, [r378](reviews/REVIEW_r378.md)'s identity, the Frobenius budget and the row sums, and **fails $(\dagger)$ by $0.0436$**. In closed form $(\dagger)$ holds iff $M_{jk}\ge M^*(n,\theta)$, and at the band's bottom $M^*\to0.169$, an absolute constant against an $M_{jk}$ that decays like $1/n$. **So $(\dagger)$ cannot be proved from the band alone.** *[r379](reviews/REVIEW_r379.md) goes further and removes the existence question: eliminating $\lVert o\rVert$ through [Lemma L68](findings/diagonal-half.md) turns $(\dagger)$ into $s_j+s_k\ge\sigma_{\min}(\theta,M_{jk},n)$, and summing over a perfect matching against $\sum_ls_l=\lVert M\rVert_F^2=2$ forces $\theta^2\ge2-12/n$, so **$(\dagger)$ is inconsistent with the normalisation on all but an $O(1/n)$ fraction of the band from $n=30$ up**, the usable fraction being $0.571$ at $n=40$ and $0.032$ at $n=400$. $(\dagger)$ demands $\theta\ge\Theta_n(1-O(1/n))$, which is the conclusion rather than a hypothesis.*
>
> **(iv) And it is structurally blind outside orbit-free blocks.** $\widetilde No=(\theta+M_{jk})o$ makes the clause an **equality** wherever $o\ne0$, so no trace–Frobenius bound can ever establish it there, at the cross pair of every $S^m\times S^m$ the true slack is $0$ and $(\dagger)$ overshoots. **$\lVert o\rVert=0$ is a hypothesis of $(\dagger)$, not a free variable in it.**

**The diagnosis, corrected.** In an orbit-free block $u\!\cdot\!v=\lVert u\rVert^2\ge0$, so [r378](reviews/REVIEW_r378.md)'s identity $\theta M_{jk}=M_{jk}^2+\lVert u\rVert^2$ forces **$M_{jk}>0$** and pins $M_{jk}=\tfrac12\big(\theta\pm\sqrt{\theta^2-4\lVert u\rVert^2}\big)$, *so the sign was never the question.* **And the remaining gap is not a floor on $M_{jk}$ either** ([r379](reviews/REVIEW_r379.md)): $(\dagger)$ asks for $\theta\ge\Theta_n(1-O(1/n))$, i.e. for the conclusion. **A successor needs a third moment or the eigenvector structure**, the first two moments are spent.

**Why this is the first attempt of the right shape.** $(\dagger)$ is a **ceiling** on $\lambda_{\max}(\widetilde N)$ built only from the first two moments, both of which criticality and the row sums pin exactly; it is not a row-mass bound, so it does not lose the factor Gershgorin and the $\lambda_{\max}+\max\operatorname{diag}$ split both lost. **What it still needs is the band**: $(\dagger)$ is an inequality in $\theta$, $M_{jk}$ and $\lVert o\rVert$, and proving it in general requires lower bounds on $\theta+M_{jk}$, for which $\theta\ge\sqrt{3/2}$ is available and $M_{jk}$ is not yet controlled. **And Gate 2 has now shown that one inequality in four scalars is not enough**, the band does not imply it, and outside orbit-free blocks nothing of this shape can.

### The rank-one split, from the ceiling Gate 2 handed back, the closest attempt yet, and still short

*2026-09-02, using [r379](reviews/REVIEW_r379.md)'s correction that criticality does supply ceilings. Analysis only.*

**The structure the band gives.** In the band, $p\,\theta^2\le\lVert M\rVert_F^2=2$ with $\theta^2\ge\tfrac32$ forces $p\le\tfrac43$, so **$M$ has exactly one eigenvalue $\ge\theta$ and every other eigenvalue is $\le0$**, the recorded gap plus the norm, nothing else. Hence
$$M=\lambda_1ww^\top-K,\qquad K\succeq0,\ \ \theta\le\lambda_1\le\sqrt2 ,$$
and compressing, $\widetilde N=\lambda_1(\Pi w)(\Pi w)^\top-\Pi K\Pi+\operatorname{diag}(u+v)$. Subadditivity of $\lambda_{\max}$ then gives a **ceiling of a new kind**, one that sees the eigenvector structure the moments could not:
$$\lambda_{\max}(\widetilde N)\;\le\;\lambda_1\big(1-w_j^2-w_k^2\big)+\max_i\,(M_{ij}+M_{ik}).$$

**Two things it does that the trace–Frobenius ceiling could not.** On $(\Pi w)^\perp$ the rank-one term vanishes and $x^\top\widetilde Nx\le\max_i(u_i+v_i)\lVert x\rVert^2$, which at $S^m\times S^m$ is $\tfrac{2m}{m-1}\lvert\gamma\rvert$ against $\theta+M_{jk}$, clearing for every $m\ge2$ with room, since $2m\le2m^2-2m+1$. **So at most one direction can ever violate the pair clause**, and it is the rank-one direction. *That is a genuine structural reduction and it survives whatever happens to the numeric ceiling.*

**And where it still falls short.** At $S^6\times S^6$: $\lambda_1=2m\lvert\gamma\rvert$, $\lVert\Pi w\rVert^2=1-\tfrac1m$, so the bound reads $2(m-1)\lvert\gamma\rvert+\tfrac{2m}{m-1}\lvert\gamma\rvert=12.4\lvert\gamma\rvert$ against $\theta+M_{jk}=12.2\lvert\gamma\rvert$, **short by $0.2\lvert\gamma\rvert$, one and a half percent**, against a true $\lambda_{\max}=10\lvert\gamma\rvert$. *The closest any attempt has come, and it fails for a nameable reason: $\lambda_{\max}(A+B)\le\lambda_{\max}A+\lambda_{\max}B$ is attained only when the two maximisers coincide, and here $\Pi w$ and the coordinate maximising $u_i+v_i$ are far apart.* **The fix must pair the two terms on a common vector rather than bound them separately**, i.e. estimate $\lambda_1(x\cdot\Pi w)^2+\sum_i(u_i+v_i)x_i^2$ jointly, which is where the next attempt should start.

**Status of [I18](plan.md)'s pair clause after four attempts.** Perturbation (fenced, margin decay), variational ascent (fenced, circular), trace–Frobenius (fenced, inconsistent with the normalisation on most of the band), rank-one split (short by $1.5\%$, and it reduces the problem to **one** direction). *Each fence is a different mechanism and each was found by Gate 2 rather than by the attempt itself, which is the pattern the loop's second step exists to produce.*

### The joint estimate clears, and by a wide margin, the first attempt that does

*2026-09-02, the fix the rank-one split named. Analysis only; the arithmetic below is by hand at $m=6$ from closed forms in $m$.*

**The estimate.** Split $x=c\,\hat w+y$ with $\hat w=\Pi w/\lVert\Pi w\rVert$, $y\perp\hat w$, $c^2+\lVert y\rVert^2=1$, and keep the two terms on the **same** vector instead of maximising them separately:
$$x^\top\widetilde Nx\;\le\;\underbrace{\big(\lambda_1\lVert\Pi w\rVert^2+q\big)c^2}_{\text{rank-one, on }\hat w}\;+\;2\lvert c\rvert\sqrt{1-c^2}\,\lVert D\hat w\rVert\;+\;(1-c^2)\,\mu^+,$$
with $D=\operatorname{diag}(u+v)$, $q=\hat w^\top D\hat w$, $\mu^+=\max_i(u_i+v_i)$. *The cross term is what the separate bound threw away, and it is negative-going: the vector maximising the diagonal part is nearly orthogonal to $\hat w$, so $c$ cannot be $1$ and the diagonal cannot be $\mu^+$ at once.*

**Every ingredient is closed-form at $S^m\times S^m$**, within-factor pair, $g=\lvert\gamma\rvert$, $\alpha=mg/(m-1)$:
$$\lambda_1\lVert\Pi w\rVert^2=2(m-1)g,\qquad q=-\frac\alpha{m-1},\qquad \mu^+=2\alpha,\qquad \lVert D\hat w\rVert^2=\frac{2\big[(m-2)\alpha^2+mg^2\big]}{m-1}.$$

**At $m=6$, $n=12$.** $\lambda_1\lVert\Pi w\rVert^2=10g$, $q=-0.24g$, $\mu^+=2.4g$, $\lVert D\hat w\rVert=2.1689g$, so the bound is $g\big[7.36c^2+2.4+4.3378\,c\sqrt{1-c^2}\big]$, maximised at $c\approx0.97$ with value
$$\lambda_{\max}(\widetilde N)\;\le\;10.35\,g\qquad\text{against}\qquad \theta+M_{jk}=12.2\,g .$$
**Clears with slack $1.85g$**, against the true $\lambda_{\max}=10g$, so the estimate is within $3.5\%$ of the truth. *The separate bound gave $12.4g$ and failed by $0.2g$; keeping the two terms on one vector recovers a factor of nine in the margin.*

**Why this is a different instrument from the three that were fenced.** It is not a moment bound, it uses the eigenvector $w$, which is what [r379](reviews/REVIEW_r379.md) said a successor would need, and it is not a perturbation, since nothing about proximity to the balanced product enters its derivation. **What it needs to become a theorem is bounds on four scalars at an arbitrary pure critical point in the band**: $\lambda_1\lVert\Pi w\rVert^2$, $q$, $\lVert D\hat w\rVert$ and $\mu^+$. *Three of them are row data of $M$ against the top eigenvector, which [Lemma L68](findings/diagonal-half.md)'s row masses $s_i$ and the identity $\theta M_{jk}=M_{jk}^2+\lVert u\rVert^2$ already speak to.* **Verified at one point only, and stated as such**, the balanced product at $n=12$, with the general bounds owed.

### The joint estimate in closed form: the pair clause follows from one scalar inequality

*2026-09-02, same line. Analysis only; the maximisation below is exact, not numerical.*

**The maximisation is a $2\times2$ eigenvalue and needs no calculus.** Writing $x=(c,\sqrt{1-c^2})$, the joint estimate's right-hand side is the quadratic form of $\begin{psmallmatrix}a&k\\k&b\end{psmallmatrix}$ with
$$a=\lambda_1\lVert\Pi w\rVert^2+q,\qquad b=\mu^+=\max_i(M_{ij}+M_{ik}),\qquad k=\lVert D\hat w\rVert,$$
so its maximum is $\tfrac{a+b}2+\sqrt{\big(\tfrac{a-b}2\big)^2+k^2}$ exactly. *This reproduces the $10.35\,g$ found numerically at $m=6$ to every digit, which is the check that the closed form is the same object.*

**Hence the clause reduces to one inequality in four scalars.** With $T=\theta+M_{jk}$, and provided $a<T$ and $b<T$, the requirement $\tfrac{a+b}2+\sqrt{(\tfrac{a-b}2)^2+k^2}\le T$ is equivalent to
$$\boxed{\;\lVert D\hat w\rVert^2\;\le\;\big(T-a\big)\big(T-b\big)\;}$$
, **a product of the two slacks against the cross term.** *At $S^6\times S^6$: $T-a=2.44g$, $T-b=9.8g$, product $23.91g^2$ against $k^2=4.70g^2$, clear by a factor of five, where every earlier attempt was failing by a few percent.*

**And one of the two side conditions is already general.** $b<T$ is $\max_i(M_{ij}+M_{ik})<\theta+M_{jk}$, which at every $S^p\times S^q$ reduces to $2m\le2m^2-2m+1$ and holds for all $m\ge2$, *it is the same statement the rank-one split proved on $(\Pi w)^\perp$, so that work is reused rather than repeated.*

> **GATE 2: THE BOXED REDUCTION IS REFUTED AT AN ARBITRARY IN-BAND POINT, BY TWO INDEPENDENT FAILURE MODES.** *[r381](reviews/REVIEW_r381.md) and [r382](reviews/REVIEW_r382.md), agreeing; the closed form, the equivalence and every $S^6\times S^6$ figure are confirmed exactly, and the generalisation is not.*
>
> **(1) Every cross pair of every $S^p\times S^q$.** There $D=\tfrac{2g}{?}\mathrm{Id}$-like and $a-T=g/(m-1)>0$ in closed form, so the side condition $a<T$ fails and $(T-a)(T-b)<0<k^2$. **The clause is TRUE there**, $\lambda_{\max}(\widetilde N)=T$ exactly, so the *method* fails, not the statement. The mechanism is the one already fenced against the trace–Frobenius ceiling: $\widetilde No=To$ forces **zero slack** wherever $o\ne0$, and no strict bound can prove an equality. **The section states no hypothesis $o=0$ and needs one**, *the same omission Gate 2 corrected one round earlier, repeated.*
>
> **(2) Within-factor pairs of $S^5\times S^q$, $q\ge34$, with BOTH side conditions holding** ([r382](reviews/REVIEW_r382.md)). So $o=0$ does not rescue it either: the reduction is insufficient in its own regime, at genuine in-band pure critical points.

> **AND THE METHOD'S DOMAIN IS GENERICALLY EMPTY, WHICH IS THE FINDING THAT ENDS THIS LINE** ([r382](reviews/REVIEW_r382.md)). $B(u-v)=0$ holds at **every** pure critical point and **every** pair, so $\widetilde No=To$ and $\lambda_{\max}(\widetilde N)\ge T$ whenever $u\ne v$: **in every non-orbit-free block the clause is the statement that $T$ is exactly the top eigenvalue, with no slack at all.** A strictly lossy estimate can never certify an equality, and generically no pair is orbit-free, at $S^6\times S^6$, $36$ of the $66$ pairs are cross pairs, and a screen over all in-band $S^p\times S^q$ with $p,q\le40$ has **$664/664$ cross pairs failing**. *The bound is confined to the blocks where it is not needed most.*

**Where the $3.5\%$ goes, measured** ([r382](reviews/REVIEW_r382.md)): $68.3\%$ is the PSD drop $z^\top Mz\le\lambda_2\lVert z\rVert^2$, **irremovable**, since $M\mathbf1=0$ pins $\lambda_2=0$; $20\%$ the diagonal relaxation; $10.2\%$ the relaxation's $c$ missing the true maximiser; $1.5\%$ Cauchy–Schwarz. *So the dominant loss is structural rather than technical, and sharpening the other three could not have saved it.*

**Four corrections and two free gains from the same audit.** *(i)* "$b<T$ is already general" is doubly wrong: it was checked at sphere products only, and it is in fact a **consequence** of the clause, since $b=\max_i\widetilde N_{ii}\le\lambda_{\max}\widetilde N$, so it can carry no weight. *(ii)* "The cross term is negative-going" is **backwards**: it is a positive cost the joint bound pays. *(iii)* The twin-swap needs $M_{jk}\ge0$, which follows from $M_{jk}(\theta-M_{jk})=\lVert u\rVert^2$ but was assumed. *(iv)* **$\lambda_1$ is simple in the band as a corollary**, not a hypothesis, and the rank-one split spends only $\theta>1$, so most of the band is still unspent. **Gains:** both reviewers independently found the sharpening $k\to k_\perp=\sqrt{\lVert D\hat w\rVert^2-q^2}$, since $y\perp\hat w$, cutting the $S^6\times S^6$ error from $3.52\%$ to $1.96\%$ at no cost; and [r382](reviews/REVIEW_r382.md) contributes a **sum companion to [Lemma L68](findings/diagonal-half.md)**, $4M_{jk}^2-2\theta M_{jk}-(s_j+s_k)\le0$, off the record and **exactly the lower bound on $\theta+M_{jk}$ this line said it lacked**, it gives $T\ge(5\theta-\sqrt{\theta^2+8})/4\ge0.7604$ in the band, tight to $1.3\%$ at the $S^6\times S^6$ cross pair. *That lemma outlives the estimate it was found for.*

**What is owed, and it is now three quantities rather than four.** Bounds at an arbitrary pure critical point in the band for $a$, $b$ and $k$, all three of which are row data of $M$ weighted by the top eigenvector: $q=\hat w^\top D\hat w$, $k^2=\hat w^\top D^2\hat w$, $b=\lVert D\rVert_\infty$. **In an orbit-free block the structure simplifies further**: $u=v$, the swap $j\leftrightarrow k$ fixes $M$, so $w_j=w_k=:w_0$ when $\lambda_1$ is simple, $D=2\operatorname{diag}(u)$, and the eigenvector equation gives $u\!\cdot\!\Pi w=(\lambda_1-M_{jk})w_0$ and $N\Pi w=\lambda_1\Pi w-2w_0u$. *Those two relations are exactly the couplings a bound on $q$ and $k$ needs, and they come from criticality and simplicity alone.*

### The ordering argument [post F47](findings/INDEX-traps.md) asked for, and the equality that blocked every estimate is what makes it work

*2026-09-02. Analysis only; the whole argument is four lines of trace arithmetic. **Gate 2 owed.**

**Claim.** *At every pure critical point with $\theta\ge\sqrt{3/2}$, and every pair $\{j,k\}$ with $o\ne0$ and $T=\theta+M_{jk}>0$, the pair clause holds: $\lambda_{\max}(\widetilde N)=T$.*

**Proof.** $\widetilde N\mathbf1=0$ and $\widetilde No=To$, and $\mathbf1\perp o$ since $\sum_io_i=\sum_i(M_{ki}-M_{ji})=(-M_{kj})-(-M_{jk})=0$ by the row sums. So when $o\ne0$, $0$ and $T$ are eigenvalues on independent eigenvectors, and for any third eigenvalue $\lambda$,
$$\lambda^2+T^2\;\le\;\lVert\widetilde N\rVert_F^2\;=\;2-\lVert o\rVert^2-2M_{jk}^2 .$$
Now substitute [Lemma L68](findings/diagonal-half.md), $\lVert o\rVert^2=s_j+s_k-2\theta M_{jk}$:
$$2T^2+\lVert o\rVert^2+2M_{jk}^2\;=\;2\theta^2+2\theta M_{jk}+4M_{jk}^2+s_j+s_k\;\ge\;\tfrac74\theta^2\;\ge\;\tfrac{21}8\;>\;2,$$
the middle step by minimising $2\theta^2+2\theta M_{jk}+4M_{jk}^2$ over $M_{jk}$ at $M_{jk}=-\theta/4$ and dropping $s_j+s_k\ge0$. Hence $\lambda^2\le2-\lVert o\rVert^2-2M_{jk}^2-T^2\le T^2$, so $\lvert\lambda\rvert\le T$ and $T$ is the top. $\square$

> **GATE 2: THE ARGUMENT IS A PROOF, AND IT GIVES MORE THAN IT CLAIMED.** *[r383](reviews/REVIEW_r383.md) and [r384](reviews/REVIEW_r384.md), each re-deriving every step cold and agreeing; neither found a counterexample and both state that none exists inside the hypotheses.*
>
> **(1) The conclusion strengthens to simplicity, which is what [I18](plan.md) actually needs.** Step 4 gives $2T^2>\lVert\widetilde N\rVert_F^2$ **strictly**, so $\lambda^2<T^2$ and $T$ is a **simple** eigenvalue, the last line above wrote $\le$ and threw that away. Since [Lemma L122](findings/second-order.md) makes the pair block $\tfrac12\widetilde N-\tfrac12M_{jk}\mathrm{Id}$, an $L_e$-eigenvalue $\tfrac12$ *is* an $\widetilde N$-eigenvalue $T$, and a repeated top would satisfy "$\lambda_{\max}=T$" while failing I18. **Restated with the strictness this is [Lemma L128](findings/second-order.md)(ii)'s pair half verbatim, at a critical point rather than a maximiser.**
>
> **(2) $T>0$ is free, not a hypothesis.** $\lVert M\rVert_F^2=2$ gives $\lvert M_{jk}\rvert\le1$, so $T\ge\sqrt{3/2}-1>0$; [r378](reviews/REVIEW_r378.md)'s sufficient condition is redundant.
>
> **(3) The band is not needed.** [r383](reviews/REVIEW_r383.md) improves the threshold to $\theta^2>12/11$ by keeping $s_j+s_k\ge2M_{jk}^2$ rather than dropping it (minimum $\tfrac{11}6\theta^2$ at $M_{jk}=-\theta/6$); [r384](reviews/REVIEW_r384.md) puts it at $\theta\ge1$. **Either way the theorem covers every catalogued pure critical point above $\mathbb{CP}^3$, far outside the band**, and the band is barely spent, the chain is slack by a factor $\approx1.58$ at both cross pairs screened.
>
> **(4) "It settles the generic case" is an OVERSTATEMENT, and it corrects [post F47](findings/INDEX-traps.md) too.** The $664/664$ census counted **cross pairs only**; over *all* pairs, orbit-free pairs run **$45\%$ to $78\%$** at every catalogued in-band point ([r384](reviews/REVIEW_r384.md)). *So the leftover is not a thin exceptional set, it is most of the pairs, and F47's "generically empty domain" is the same miscount read the other way.*
>
> **(5) The leftover's description is holed.** It is $M_{jk}\ge0$, not $>0$, with equality exactly when rows $j$ and $k$ both vanish, a **padded pair**, which criticality and the band permit and where the orbit-free budget degenerates to $\theta^2\ge2$ and fails. *The record's standing warning that padding passes coordinate tests applies here.* **And $\lVert M\rVert_F^2=2$ belongs in the hypothesis list**; the argument survives $\le2$.
>
> **(6) Scope.** The pair half is **one of [I18](plan.md)'s three clauses**; nothing here touches the four-set or $\mathcal D_n$ clauses.

**Why this is the right kind and the five estimates were not.** It never bounds $\lambda_{\max}$ from outside. **It uses the equality itself as the instrument**: because $o\ne0$ makes $T$ a *known* eigenvalue, the Frobenius budget must accommodate $T^2$ twice over before anything can exceed it, and $\theta\ge\sqrt{3/2}$ makes the budget too small. *The structure [post F47](findings/INDEX-traps.md) identified as the obstruction to every bound is exactly what supplies the ordering.*

> **(7) Two contributions worth keeping.** [r384](reviews/REVIEW_r384.md) proves $2T^2+\lVert o\rVert^2+2M_{jk}^2\ge2\theta^2$ **always**, keeping $s_j+s_k$, using criticality at $(j,k)$ for $u\!\cdot\!v=\theta M_{jk}-M_{jk}^2$ and $\lVert u\rVert^2+\lVert v\rVert^2\ge2\lvert u\!\cdot\!v\rvert$, which is the clean form of the threshold; and it derives the within-factor slack in closed form, $\theta\big(1+\tfrac q{p-1}\big)/(n-1)$, off the record. **And it names the evidence gap plainly: no non-sphere-product pure critical point is catalogued inside the band, so the in-band test set is exhausted by $S^6\times S^6$ and $S^5\times S^7$.**

**And it settles the case the estimates could not reach.** [Post F47](findings/INDEX-traps.md) records that orbit-free pairs are non-generic, $664$ of $664$ in-band cross pairs have $o\ne0$, so **the clause now holds on all of them**, and [I18](plan.md)'s pair half reduces to the orbit-free blocks alone, where $u=v$, $M_{jk}>0$, and the Frobenius budget is the failing $\theta^2+5M_{jk}^2+2\lVert u\rVert^2\ge2$. *The two halves have swapped difficulty: the case no estimate could touch is closed, and the case the estimates were designed for is what remains.*

**Hypotheses, stated.** $\theta\ge\sqrt{3/2}$ (the band, used only as $\tfrac74\theta^2>2$, so anything above $\theta^2>8/7$ suffices); $o\ne0$; $T>0$, for which [r378](reviews/REVIEW_r378.md)'s $M_{jk}^2-\theta M_{jk}+u\!\cdot\!v=0$ gives the sufficient condition $u\!\cdot\!v>-2\theta^2$; [Lemma L68](findings/diagonal-half.md) and the Frobenius identity, both already audited.

### The orbit-free case is a twin pair, and a twin pair carries an explicit eigenvector of $M$

*2026-09-02, while Gate 2 runs on the ordering theorem; this is a separate and smaller claim. Analysis only. **Screened**: [diagonal-half.md](findings/diagonal-half.md) already has the twin vocabulary and [Lemma L68](findings/diagonal-half.md)'s $2\theta M_{ab}\le s_a+s_b$ with **equality exactly at twin pairs**, which is $o=0$ in this section's notation; the eigenvector below is not there.*

**Orbit-free means twin.** $o=0$ is $M_{ij}=M_{ik}$ for every $i$, i.e. the transposition $\tau=(jk)$ is an automorphism of $M$, the record's *twin pair*. [Lemma L68](findings/diagonal-half.md) then gives $s_j=s_k=\theta M_{jk}$, and [r378](reviews/REVIEW_r378.md)'s identity gives $\lVert u\rVert^2=\theta M_{jk}-M_{jk}^2$, the two agreeing through $s_j=\lVert u\rVert^2+M_{jk}^2$.

**The eigenvector.** With $P_\tau M=MP_\tau$, the antisymmetric line $\mathbb R(e_j-e_k)$ is $M$-invariant, and
$$M(e_j-e_k)=-M_{jk}\,(e_j-e_k),$$
since the $i$-component is $u_i-v_i=0$ and the $j$-component is $-M_{jk}$. **Combined with the recorded gap $\operatorname{spec}(M)\cap(0,\theta)=\varnothing$ this re-proves $M_{jk}\ge0$ at every twin pair**, by a route independent of the quadratic $M_{jk}^2-\theta M_{jk}+\lVert u\rVert^2=0$, *the eigenvalue $-M_{jk}$ must be $\le0$, since $-M_{jk}\ge\theta>0$ would need $M_{jk}\le-\theta$ against $s_j=\theta M_{jk}\ge0$.*

**And the symmetric part has a block form the orbit-free case should be attacked in.** On $\operatorname{Sym}=\{x:x_j=x_k\}$, in the basis $(x_I,\;x_s=(x_j+x_k)/\sqrt2)$,
$$M\big|_{\operatorname{Sym}}=\begin{pmatrix}N&\sqrt2\,u\\ \sqrt2\,u^\top&M_{jk}\end{pmatrix},$$
so $N$ is a **codimension-one compression of $M|_{\operatorname{Sym}}$ with the bordering vector $\sqrt2u$ known exactly**, and $M|_{\operatorname{Sym}}$ inherits the whole spectral gap. *That is a genuine handle on $N$; what it still does not touch is the additive $2\operatorname{diag}(u)$ that turns $N$ into $\widetilde N$, which remains the orbit-free case's whole difficulty and is where the next attempt goes.*

*2026-09-02, synthesis after Gate 2 on the ordering theorem. Analysis only; no new derivation, a reading of what the record now holds.*

**The ordering theorem and the joint estimate fail and succeed on opposite sets, which neither attempt could see while it was the only one.**

| pair type | ordering theorem ($o\ne0$) | joint estimate $(\dagger)$ |
|---|---|---|
| cross / non-twin, $o\ne0$ | **proves it**, $T$ simple, needs only $\theta\ge1$ | fails at **every** such pair, $a>T$ in closed form ([r381](reviews/REVIEW_r381.md)) |
| orbit-free / twin, $o=0$ | silent, $T$ is not known to be an eigenvalue | **clears** at $S^6\times S^6$ by a factor of five, and at every screened in-band point except one family |

*So the estimate that [post F47](findings/INDEX-traps.md) fenced was fenced only on the blocks the ordering theorem now closes, and it survives on exactly the blocks that remain open.* **That is the useful shape, and it was invisible until both existed.**

**What the combination leaves.** [r382](reviews/REVIEW_r382.md)'s screen over all in-band $S^p\times S^q$ with $p,q\le40$ found **seven** within-factor failures of $(\dagger)$, all in the family $S^5\times S^q$ with $q\ge34$, extreme splits, where the small factor's row data is concentrated. Everything else screened is covered by one instrument or the other. **The residue of [I18](plan.md)'s pair half is therefore: twin pairs at extreme splits, plus the padded sub-case $M_{jk}=0$, plus whatever lies outside the screened family, and the last is most of the problem, since no non-sphere-product pure critical point is catalogued in the band at all.**

**And the residue has the right shape for the ordering method rather than for another estimate.** At a twin pair the transposition $(jk)$ is an automorphism of $M$, so $e_j-e_k$ is an eigenvector of $M$ at $-M_{jk}$ and $M|_{\operatorname{Sym}}$ is $N$ bordered by $\sqrt2u$ with corner $M_{jk}$. **What is missing is a second known eigenvector of $\widetilde N$**, the ordering argument needs two, and a twin pair supplies only $\mathbf1$. *Finding one, or proving the budget without one, is the single next question, and it is a question about eigenvectors rather than about bounds, which is what [post F47](findings/INDEX-traps.md) said the successor must be.*

### The twin case: the trace bound on $\mathbf1^\perp$ clears where $(\dagger)$ failed, and is asymptotically borderline

*2026-09-02. Analysis only; all arithmetic by hand from closed forms in $m$ and $q$.*

**First, what a twin pair does and does not give.** The general identity specialises: with $u=v$, $Bu=2M_{jk}u-u\circ u$, so
$$\widetilde N\,u=(\theta-M_{jk})\,u+u\circ u ,$$
**$u$ is an eigenvector exactly when $u\circ u\parallel u$**, i.e. when $u$ is constant on its support, false at $S^m\times S^m$, where $u$ takes $\alpha$ on $F_1\setminus\{j,k\}$ and $\gamma$ on $F_2$. *So a twin pair supplies no second eigenvector this way, and the ordering argument stays out of reach.*

**But the trace bound on $\mathbf1^\perp$ is a different instrument from $(\dagger)$, and a better one here.** Working in $\mathbf1^\perp$ (dimension $d-1$, $d=n-2$) with $\operatorname{tr}\widetilde N=-2M_{jk}$ and $f=\lVert\widetilde N\rVert_F^2=2-2M_{jk}^2$, Cauchy–Schwarz on the non-maximal eigenvalues gives
$$\lambda_{\max}(\widetilde N)\;\le\;\frac{-2M_{jk}+\sqrt{(d-2)\big[(d-1)f-4M_{jk}^2\big]}}{d-1}.$$

| point | bound | $T=\theta+M_{jk}$ | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| $S^6\times S^6$, within-factor | $1.28847$ | $1.37086$ | **clears** |
| $S^5\times S^{40}$, within-factor ($\theta=1.26346$, in band) | $1.32188$ | $1.55061$ | **clears** |

*The second is one of [r382](reviews/REVIEW_r382.md)'s seven $(\dagger)$ failures, $k^2=0.2735$ against $0.2465$ there, so **the residue named in the previous section is covered by this bound at the point that defined it**.*

**And here is the honest limit.** As $d\to\infty$ the finite-dimension factor $\tfrac{d-2}{d-1}$ tends to $1$ and the bound degenerates to $\sqrt f$, so the condition becomes $\theta^2+2\theta M_{jk}+3M_{jk}^2\ge2$, **the Frobenius condition that fails at $S^6\times S^6$**. At the balanced product both sides are $2-\tfrac1m+O(m^{-2})$: $\theta^2=2-\tfrac3m+O(m^{-2})$ and $2\theta\alpha\approx\tfrac2m$, against a bound whose square is $f\big(1-\tfrac1{d-1}\big)\approx2-\tfrac1m$. **So the comparison is decided at second order in $1/m$, with the trace term $-2M_{jk}/(d-1)$ contributing at exactly that order.** *That second-order computation is the next concrete step, and it is arithmetic in $m$ rather than a new idea, the first time this item's remaining question has been that small.*

### The second-order comparison, done exactly: the trace bound clears at every balanced product, with a closed-form margin

*2026-09-02. Analysis only; the computation below is exact in $m$, not an expansion and not a screen.*

**Set-up.** At $S^m\times S^m$, within-factor pair, write $D=d-1=2m-3$, $E=d-2=2m-4$, $f=2-2\alpha^2$. The trace bound $L=\big(-2\alpha+\sqrt{E\,[Df-4\alpha^2]}\big)/D$ satisfies $L\le T$ **iff**
$$E\,[Df-4\alpha^2]\;\le\;\big(DT+2\alpha\big)^2 \iff \frac{2E}D\;\le\;T^2+\frac{4T\alpha}D+\frac{4\alpha^2(E+1)+2ED\alpha^2}{D^2},$$
every term after $T^2$ being positive.

**The three exact values.** $\gamma^2=\tfrac{m-1}{m^2(2m-1)}$, $\alpha=\tfrac m{m-1}\lvert\gamma\rvert$, $\theta=(2m-1)\lvert\gamma\rvert$ give
$$\theta^2=2-\frac3m+\frac1{m^2},\qquad \theta\alpha=\frac1m\ \text{(exactly)},\qquad \alpha^2=\frac1{(m-1)(2m-1)},$$
so $T^2=\theta^2+2\theta\alpha+\alpha^2=2-\dfrac1m+\dfrac1{m^2}+\dfrac1{(m-1)(2m-1)}$.

**The comparison, and it is positive term by term.** Since $\dfrac{2E}D=\dfrac{4m-8}{2m-3}=2-\dfrac2{2m-3}$,
$$T^2-\frac{2E}D=\underbrace{\frac2{2m-3}-\frac1m}_{=\ 3/(m(2m-3))}+\frac1{m^2}+\frac1{(m-1)(2m-1)}\;=\;\frac3{m(2m-3)}+\frac1{m^2}+\frac1{(m-1)(2m-1)}\;>\;0 .$$
**Strictly positive at every $m\ge3$, and the remaining right-hand terms only help.** *So the trace bound clears at every balanced product, the degeneration feared in the previous section does not happen, because $\theta\alpha=1/m$ exactly and $2E/D$ falls short of $2$ by $2/(2m-3)$, and those two $1/m$ terms do not cancel.*

### The separation attack, opened: two exact constraints every $T$-eigenvector must satisfy

*2026-09-02, way (i) of [post F48](findings/INDEX-traps.md), prove $T\notin\operatorname{spec}(\widetilde N|_{\mathbf1^\perp})$ directly, abandoning the false $\lambda_{\max}\le T$. Analysis only. **Gate 2 owed.**

**At a twin pair the clause is unconditional separation.** With $o=0$ the phrase "off the orbit direction" is vacuous, so the whole clause is: **no $x\perp\mathbf1$ satisfies $\widetilde Nx=Tx$.** Suppose one does.

**Constraint 1, from the twin identity, and it costs nothing.** Pair $\widetilde Nu=(\theta-M_{jk})u+u\circ u$ against $x$ using self-adjointness:
$$(\theta-M_{jk})\langle u,x\rangle+\langle u\circ u,\ x\rangle=\langle u,\widetilde Nx\rangle=T\langle u,x\rangle=(\theta+M_{jk})\langle u,x\rangle,$$
$$\boxed{\ \langle u\circ u,\ x\rangle=2M_{jk}\,\langle u,x\rangle\ }$$
**Every $T$-eigenvector is orthogonal to $u\circ u-2M_{jk}u$.** *So the $T$-eigenspace lies in a codimension-two subspace, $\mathbf1^\perp$ and this, and if $u\circ u-2M_{jk}u$ happened to be a multiple of $\mathbf 1$ the constraint would be empty, which is exactly the constant-$u$ case where $u$ itself is an eigenvector.*

**Constraint 2, from the spectral gap, quadratically.** Extend $x$ by zeros at $j,k$; then $N x=Tx-2\,u\circ x$, and $\lVert MX\rVert^2\ge\theta\,X^\top MX$ (the gap, as $M^2-\theta M\succeq0$) becomes, with $\lVert x\rVert=1$, $S_1=\sum u_ix_i^2$, $S_2=\sum u_i^2x_i^2$, $c=\langle u,x\rangle$:
$$T\,M_{jk}\;-\;(2\theta+4M_{jk})\,S_1\;+\;4S_2\;+\;2c^2\;\ge\;0 .$$
*Both $S_1$ and $S_2$ are $x$-weighted moments of $u$, and Constraint 1 pins the combination $\langle u\circ u-2M_{jk}u,\ x\rangle$, a first-moment statement against a second-moment inequality.*

### The Dirichlet identity worked, and it gives a window rather than a contradiction

*2026-09-02, the one instrument [post F49](findings/INDEX-traps.md) leaves. Analysis only.*

**The equality case is settled and it is the useful half.** $R=\tfrac12\sum_{i,l\in I}M_{il}^2(x_i-x_l)^2$ vanishes exactly when $x$ is constant on each connected component of $\operatorname{supp}(N)$. **So if that support is connected, $x\propto\mathbf1$ on $I$, which contradicts $x\perp\mathbf1$ unless $x=0$**, the separation holds outright at every twin pair whose deleted support is connected, and the padded case is the disconnected extreme ([Lemma L129](findings/diagonal-half.md) closes it by another route). *Connectivity of $\operatorname{supp}(M)$ is on the record as $\circ$-indecomposability ([support-dichotomy.md](findings/support-dichotomy.md)); what is needed here is connectivity of the support with **two rows deleted**, which is strictly stronger and is not recorded.*

**An upper bound on $R$, free.** $(x_i-x_l)^2\le2(x_i^2+x_l^2)$ gives
$$R\;\le\;2\sum_i x_i^2\Big(\sum_{l\in I}M_{il}^2\Big)\;=\;2\big\langle x^{\circ2},\,s^I\big\rangle\;\le\;2\max_i\big(s_i-2u_i^2\big),$$
using $s^I_i=s_i-u_i^2-v_i^2=s_i-2u_i^2$ at a twin pair. **So the identity brackets the same quantity from both sides**, $0\le TM_{jk}-(2\theta+4M_{jk})S_1+2S_2+2c^2\le2\max_i(s_i-2u_i^2)$, and neither end is a contradiction: the lower end is what [post F49](findings/INDEX-traps.md) leaves and the upper end is a bound on the Dirichlet energy, not on the eigenvector's existence.

**Status of [I18](plan.md)'s twin half after six attempts.** Perturbation, variational ascent, trace–Frobenius, rank-one split, joint estimate, trace bound on $\mathbf1^\perp$, all fenced, the last three by [post F48](findings/INDEX-traps.md) (the target was false) and the eigen-equation route by [post F49](findings/INDEX-traps.md). **What is closed**: every non-twin pair ([Lemma L128](findings/second-order.md) route, Gate 2 passed); every padded pair ([Lemma L129](findings/diagonal-half.md)); every within-factor twin pair of every $S^p\times S^q$ ([r387](reviews/REVIEW_r387.md)); every twin pair with connected deleted support (above). **What is open**: twin pairs with $0<M_{jk}<\theta$ and disconnected deleted support, at a non-sphere-product pure critical point, **of which the record catalogues none inside the band.**

### I18's four-set clause, opened: it reduces to a mass bound, and concentration is what the band forbids

*2026-09-02, [I18](plan.md)'s second clause, untouched until now. Analysis only.*

**The clause.** By [Lemma L121](findings/second-order.md) the four-set block of $L_e$ has eigenvalues $\pm\sqrt\Sigma/(2\theta)$ with $\Sigma=A^2+B^2+C^2-AB-BC-CA$ in the opposite-pair sums, so **[Lemma L128](findings/second-order.md)(ii) asks $\Sigma\ne\theta^2$ at every four-subset**, the $\ne$ repair, not a bound.
